# Native on-foot VR (replacing Explorer Cam) — design, 2026-10-13

Credit: the initial investigation and research that made native on-foot VR possible is the work of [pixel-565](https://github.com/pixel-565). The maintainer approved naming them in the Thanks of the release that ships this arc (2026-10-25), tied to the arc's first commits c3a99013 and 1535fb59.

## Status

- **2026-10-27 RC2 report, look to aim in the disembark lifts (log `edvr_gfx_20261027_085355`):** in the station and ship lifts the game turns the aim by the mouse path while the processor's stored delta reads 0 (or about 0.01 deg), so F109 filed the look as blocked or foreign, cancelled nothing, and its probes and asks walked the view until the guard latched it off (three trips in about 8 s at each lift; the SRV exit too, log `edvr_gfx_20261027_105845`). Ruled out: the game's own look block; EDVR's own publication. Cause (static RE, CONFIRMED in flight `edvr_gfx_20261027_064839`: at a station with 16 humanoids the old rule would have misrouted 100% of the asks; F129 routed all of them, no trip): the processor runs once per humanoid, and EDVR gave its ask to the first call after the update, another humanoid's when one came first. F129 (`0d071613`, FLOWN OK): only the player's own component (`[comp+0x2E0] == [act+0x88]`) takes the ask. Flown OK since: F130 (the weapon UI's rows near the SRV), F131b/c (look to aim holds for panels, the Esc menu and the inventory), F133 + F134 (the ADS judder with the head aim off), F137 (mouse look aimed down moves the view as a neck). - **2026-10-26 Frontier flight `edvr_gfx_20261026_101921` (`22cabf3c`):** the preview hooks install, and the composition applies 2,532 times with zero refusals. The Location stage output moves onto the CustomisationVisual pose (11 cm, 4.0 deg). The drawn eyes stay on the HMD activity (38 µm) and the ship overview is still inside the Lynx Highliner. Ruled out: the displayed view consumes that stage output. Mission capture `102137780001` and ship capture `102221594003` each retain both authored meshes. The 77-vertex pair is the live curved panel and the exact pick mesh. The other pair is a flat 2.00 by 1.126 m quad at z=1.10 with UV 0..1, and it is not on screen. The scene eye is the kind-5 camera origin at `camera+0x50` (view-constant refresh `0x5924A2` into `gCameraPos`), built from a copy of the HMD primary, not from that Location output. The finalizer now writes the composed pose to the HMD primary as well, and the eye-producer hook replaces that stale copy before the per-eye multiply. The completed-mission panel is stock again: the mesh hook, the plate clear, and the tonemap clear are out. The ship-preview eye stays the preview pose without the local headset. A seat whose neck and camera are both 25 cm under the stored standing ones follows that neck, and a stored seat is kept while the neck stays there, which stopped the head floating and the view popping. The combat hunch, whose camera stays up, still holds the standing eye. The laser-rifle optic anchor accepts a one-frame gap between the joint snapshot and the root, after the 18:34 ADS flight refused every sample and the snap left the sight 2 deg left of the head. While aiming, the stance raise is published as zero so the sight lock owns the eye; holding the standing raise left the pistol low. Compose math is unchanged. Leash, ADS and bracers stay as previously confirmed. The `24a2b567` reachability failure is closed by this flight; its journal entry remains below.

- **F109 (FLOWN 2026-10-25, log `edvr_gfx_20261025_071049`, v0.21.1-236-g33e05706, Pimax Crystal Super; `snap turn (F109)` OK 12 of 12; the pilot: works well, but it did not engage at first and lost its function until toggled: F109b): look to aim on foot; the player's own turn in ADS; snap or smooth turning.** RE (`analysis\decomp\verify_20261025_onfoot_look_input.txt`, inbox item `20261025-053908-onfoot-look-input`): the right stick's look is its own actions (act+0x180 yaw, +0x188 pitch), the processor sums dt x rate x stick + g x mouse + dt x spring, the aim takes the delta whole in the call. (1) **The ADS stick bug** (a tester: the avatar turned, the view did not): F62b's split counted a stick's turn as the head aim's whenever it wrote (ours = d x in / (mouse + in)); now ours = g x in with g from clean calls only (`nofoot::f109::Split`), with look to aim on or off. (2) **Look to aim** (`fix.native_on_foot_look_to_aim`, off by default): the ADS head aim's map run all the time on foot, armed and unarmed, yaw and pitch, no cone: a follower on the game's applied turn (`nofoot::f109::Follower`), centred once at each engage from the reported head, smoothing (`_smoothing_ms`, 150) only with nothing drawn, 180 deg/s cap, the guard all the time (re-based every 10 s under 1 deg), the look-blocked hold, the ADS press inside it measures only and unwinds nothing; the player's look dropped in the update hook (pitch always; yaw by the turn style). (3) **Turn style** `fix.native_on_foot_turn_style` (snap | smooth) and `fix.native_on_foot_snap_turn_deg` (45, 15-90): snap from the stick (0.70 / 0.25) or a mouse flick (20 deg in 150 ms, 400 ms cooldown) with a 20-100-30 ms comfort fade; smooth passes the stick's and the mouse's yaw; in ADS too. (4) The runtime's reset returns the seated space to its origin itself (no translation left after a standing session). F22-F25's controller and `_look_to_aim_yaw_sign`, `_comp_delay`, `_comp_sign` are retired. Lines and rules `look to aim (F109)`, `snap turn (F109)`, `smooth turn (F109)`, `ADS player turn (F109)`. Journal: 2026-10-25, F109 (its flight card). **F109b (FLOWN 2026-10-25, log `edvr_gfx_20261025_085120`, v0.21.1-250-gaba55fce: guard trips 0, new bases 19, `snap turn` 19 exact; the pilot: "look to aim failed while trying to use the cutting tool and locked me in a weird position": F109c):** the key read off at launch and every engage came in the tick it turned on; the losses were two false guard trips, which F109 held until a toggle (17 s, then 5 min 18 s): a smooth turn of 191 deg read as -12.2 deg of pitch in the base's axes, and the game pitching the view 17.9 deg in a jump. The guard now takes a new base past 15 deg of the player's own turn, restarts a growth run after a 200 ms rows gap, and holds (a new base, counted) a residual its asks cannot explain (over 2.5 x the net ask + 4 deg); a trip stops look to aim for 2 s, the third in a minute until a toggle. The smooth check read the avatar's turn from comp+0x7B8, which stays 0 (53 false disagreements): now the summed processor delta over whole ticks. `ADS player turn` was absent: no ADS second had a turn of the player's own. Journal: 2026-10-25, F109b. **F109c (NOT FLOWN, branch `claude/onfoot-look-to-aim-3` from aba55fce, built green):** at the Arc Cutter's start (08:57:09) the split took gains of -405.4, 741.1 and 22.2 (0.85-1.00 in every other second) from calls whose delta held a term of the game's own; the asks went to the game divided by them, the aim reached +85 deg, the map's +-60 clamp dropped 60.18 deg of counted pitch that the follower kept, and for 20 s the follower asked down into the map's limit: the aim held at -35, 4-61 deg under the head, and the view 25 deg over it (the unwind at the toggle took the aim from -35 to +25). A gain is now taken only between the game's own ends (comp+0x808 / +0x80C, 5% either side, their sign); the pitch account is exact and only its publication is held to +-60; the 1 s line reads the aim's pitch (the FP root) against the account. Journal: 2026-10-25, F109c.

- **F119 (BUILT, NOT FLOWN, measure only; branch `claude/onfoot-head-containment` from c53b06df): head containment, Phase 0.** On foot the game's collision keeps the commander's head out of walls, and EDVR adds the physical head's translation to the game's camera, so a lean can push an eye through a wall (a PvP cheat). The approved design: a leash (fade toward black past a soft radius from the rest point; past a hard radius for about 0.3 s recentre the position, never the yaw) and a wall contact rule (world geometry filling much of an eye's view at near-zero depth: black at once, a recentre if it persists), no user key, native on foot only. This build measures what sets their numbers and changes nothing that is drawn: the head's offset from the rest point by stance, item and ADS (p50, p95, max, a histogram; EDVR's own eye offsets logged apart), every move of the rest point on foot, and an 8 x 8 grid over each eye's scene depth (cells within 5, 10 and 20 cm of the camera and 3 cm of the near plane; the player's weapon, arms and body told from the world by stencil bit 0x10; the coverage at a head offset under 3 cm as the baseline). The commander's collision radius is not an exe constant in 334925 (the hand-over waits in the analysis inbox). Line `native on foot head containment (F119) 1 s`, rule `head containment (F119)` (soft and hard radius from normal play's p99.5). No key. **Next flight:** the card in the journal, 2026-10-25, F119.

- **Now-head fix (F32).** The provider no longer refuses a whole frame over an optional head: an unusable one is dropped for that frame and logged, because a refusal steps the runtime's ladder down for the session. The provider logs the first version 2 accept and any version 2 size refusal; the runtime logs its first publish, each ladder step-down and the negotiated version; the d3d11 side reads the now head at every marker post (any mode) and logs its first read and the first valid head.
- **F33 (BUILT, NOT INSTALLED; `fix.native_on_foot_body_align` = off by default, live).** Body align: the seated origin moves so the game's first-person camera sits at the third-person body's pov, so the first-person arms meet the torso. No game writes.
  - **Runtime.** Frame output version 8 (`eyeAlign`, a seated-space translation, and `eyeAlignSerial`; version 6 and 7 callers read zero). The runtime folds it into the seated origin as a translation through the look compensation's route (`seated.replace`), with no origin generation bump and no currentOrigin write, and a rebase (a new seated origin) resets the applied value. The same seated space carries the render, "now" and layer poses.
  - **Controller (d3d11, `alignTick`).** The error is (cam - HMD) - pov3P in body axes (right, up, forward), minus the trims. cam is the job camera; pov3P is the head joint (neck census) plus Explorer Cam's rest offset, through the AMC matrix. HMD is the eye position of the game's list-B view (world axes). The integral takes 0.2 of the seated error per frame (5 cm at most), clamped to 0.6 m; a critically damped second-order filter (tau 250 ms) follows it; the published value moves at 5 cm per frame at most. The guard: when the error has not fallen to 90% 2 s after the offset started, the offset goes to zero for good until the key is toggled. Held while ADS, and while an input is missing or the AMC sample is over 100 ms old.
  - **Deviations from the spec, for the flight.** (a) HMD_body comes from the list-B eye position in world axes, not from the runtime's physicalHead mapped into body axes: the list-B view already gives world axes, so no seated-to-world transform is needed for it. (b) The body-to-seated rotation uses the list-B view C (world from view) and the render head R, as F31's H_M does; sign and order unverified. (c) fp_root is logged "unread": the mode-2 root cross-check is not wired. (d) The head joint is the neck census head (as the P1 probe reads it), not a skeleton slot read in the hook. (e) The rest pov offset comes from Explorer Cam's skeleton walk when that has derived one; otherwise the pov is the head joint itself plus the trims. The once-a-second line's `pov:` field says which ("derived" or "head joint + trims"). The walk does not run on foot, so the fallback is the usual case until it is wired there. (f) The runtime folds the applied offset into lookSeated; with look-to-aim on, the applied value is rotated with the look so the commanded seated offset is kept.
  - **Keys.** `native_on_foot_body_align` (off | on, live); `..._trim_right_cm`, `_trim_up_cm`, `_trim_forward_cm` (hidden, clamped to +-30). **Risks.** The shoulder gap when looking down; the lean decouples (the HMD's own lean is in the error, so most of it cancels, but the trims and the pov are fixed by the rest offset); the stance swing moves the eye about 20 cm; option A (the body's own placement) later.
- **Ruled out (F31):** the game renders the right eye first in native on foot (F27 to F29). The visor is correct with first = left (Sean, F30 swap test), and the layer swap was persistent under first = right (F30 07:38:51). **Next flight (F31, when Sean says):** no `eye rule cockpit (first = left)` change lines; no stand-down at a mode edge (or the `re-armed at native render-mode edge` line when one happens); the visor correct with `remlok_swap_eyes = 0`; the 5 s `H_M vs C: angle` line at rest near 0 degrees and rising in a turn; `t' (written)` and `forward under H_M` side by side for the marker stutter.

## Eye-dump crash: d3dcompiler_47.dll unloaded under a live blob (2026-10-23)

- **Crash.** Pressing eye dump in native on-foot VR killed the render thread with 0xC0000005 at `d3d11.dll+0x358A35`, inside `EyeDrawSnapshot::pointSampleUiTexture` (`src\d3d11\eye_draw_snapshot.h`), reached from `captureCandidateInputs` for a large single-mip RGBA8 weapon-UI candidate texture (Elite's minidump of 14:08:47). The crash sentinel read `fault-page state=free ... covered-by-unloaded=d3dcompiler_47.dll`.
- **Cause.** The sampler compiles its 384x384 point-sample kernel with `D3DCompile` from a `LoadLibraryW(d3dcompiler_47.dll)` handle and called `FreeLibrary` right after, while the `ID3DBlob` `code` (and `errors`) were still alive. Their vtables live in that DLL. `code->GetBufferSize()` then read an unmapped vtable, and so would the `ComPtr` destructors. It bites only when nothing else holds the DLL; `shader_swap.cpp` and `gpu_pass_profile.cpp` keep their handles forever, which hid it whenever one of those features had run.
- **Fix.** The handle is a function-static, loaded once under the sampler's mutex (a failed load retries) and never freed, as in `gpu_pass_profile.cpp`. The blobs are scoped to the kernel-build block, so they are released with the DLL mapped on both paths; a missing `D3DCompile` export or a failed compile returns false without touching a blob. No other `LoadLibrary(d3dcompiler...)` in `src\` is followed by a `FreeLibrary`: the two in `shader_swap.cpp` never free theirs.
- **Rig.** `tools\eye_draw_snapshot_unload_test\` (build.bat `:rig_eye_draw_snapshot_unload`): its own process, `d3d11.lib` only, no `D3DCompile` of its own. It asserts the DLL is absent after the WARP device exists, runs the sampler on a 1024x768 RGBA8 grid three times (first compile, kernel reuse, a second device that recompiles) and spot-checks seven output texels each time. `eye_draw_snapshot_test` could not catch this: it links `d3dcompiler.lib` and calls `D3DCompile`, which pins the DLL. Against the unfixed header the rig dies with 0xC0000005 reading an address no loaded module covers; with the fix it passes.
- **Ruled out:** the sampler's shader or the 1024x768 source as the fault (the same dispatch passes once the DLL stays loaded).

## F83 diagnostic tracing (local implementation, 2026-10-17)

The jump lattice samples every second source pixel for SkinE, motion vectors and EngineSlots across all 16 scheduled eye0 frames. It preserves the integer slot words, caps the run at 320 MiB, and joins only when scene frame, render frame, epoch and both eye capture sequences agree. Each row reports not reached, refused, or written; a late DO_NOT_WAIT refusal has no capture sequence or payload. Existing one-shot full-resolution SkinE captures remain available for edges and pixels.

The UI writer annotation uses the proven synchronous CPU submit path and exact active instance TLS at the existing 434D149 writer observer. It records the native render frame/QPC and joined getter identity beside the exact 336-byte record, before the generic record/byte caps; the 1024-slot and 336-KiB reserves have explicit overflow. The issue observer runs inside the existing draw bracket after marker/UI state changes and before restoration. It records effective target view, viewport/scissor, VS b0 identity/range and a deferred bounded copy; PS texture inputs retain source resource/view identities and explicit refusal metadata. The eye draw reader labels unavailable payloads instead of treating them as projection evidence. B10/DB89 and 025B/46F are candidate shader families only. `eye_run_ledger.py` checks full-record equality through the indexed t33 stream. A writer record matching multiple draw/eye uses is `exact_many_draws`; only distinct renderer/part/instance identities claiming a shared GPU tuple are `ambiguous`; zero matches are `unmatched`. A flight is still needed to verify capture coverage and compare both eye projections during head motion.

## F84 airborne and UI tracing (local implementation, 2026-10-17)

The manual eye-dump request still starts its 16-row capture immediately. When issued on foot while grounded, it also arms one 30-second companion request. A read-only native AMC root/velocity snapshot arms the companion on a fresh airborne classifier sample (`|filtered vy| > 0.8 m/s`), with a 100 ms freshness limit; feet lift alone is not a trigger. If the player is already airborne when the manual run starts, that run records the native trigger and no duplicate is queued. The companion waits through an active eye/final/lattice run, draw census, or object ledger; if the jump ends while busy, it waits for the next fresh airborne sample. Stale snapshots, busy deferrals, start refusal, timeout, on-foot exit and shutdown have explicit log states. The companion uses a unique stamp, links its parent stamp and trigger/root/velocity timing into the final JSON and lattice manifest, and starts a new census only after old census/object-ledger work is idle. Its normal 16-row pipeline writes through the same final-eye, optic and lattice completion path as a manual capture.

For the next flight, press the manual eye-dump key while grounded, wait about two seconds for that immediate run to finish, and jump within 30 seconds. A jump during an active capture is logged as deferred; a later jump is then needed if the first one lands before capture becomes free. Use the paired manual and `airborne_companion` stamps to compare pose, instance/palette, SkinE, motion-vector, engine-slot and final-eye rows around the jump. The state-machine and full-image sampling WARP tests live in `tools/eye_draw_snapshot_test`; the focused `eye_draw_snapshot` rig and Python schema/reader tests pass.

UI candidate storage now reserves 768 rows for all 16 frames, three eye buckets and 16 candidates per bucket, plus 384 non-UI rows. It preserves the exact issued target and shader identity; 025B's valid VS camera binding is b1[270..275], while its lack of b0 is recorded as unused. UI images prioritize B10 t0 and 025B t2. Small existing mips are retained whole; otherwise supported RGBA8 sources use deterministic full-source point sampling to 384x384, with source dimensions, format and coordinate/color semantics in the v15 file. Per-frame UI imagery has its own 6 MiB allowance; non-UI per-draw allowance remains 20 MiB. This remains capture-only evidence, not a UI behavior change. No flight has yet validated these F84 runtime captures.

## F77 changes (2026-10-17)

The elbow-out sign now comes from anatomical plan side (left -1, right +1), preserving the established model-X half-space while removing dependence on translated clavicle position. The regression translates each arm across model X zero and checks the same shoulder-relative solution and outward/below constraints. Existing pose-event rows retain their fields and add the sign plus actual/required outward distance. The event budget is eight per active item serial per minute and 32 globally; separate counters identify item/global suppression. These thresholds affect diagnostics only.

FinalCrisp scheduling records explicit native render identity beside its unchanged temporal scene, epoch and sequence. The callback uses that stored identity, including for delayed or missing callbacks; zero/unset render frames cannot pass matching. No fixed counter offset is assumed. The source samples and freshness failures remain available in the manifest.

The targeted candidate sidecar reserves independent capture capacity for the observed hand/held-item shader family and exact suspected rifle optic pair. Both are candidates until the geometry/contribution evidence identifies them. It retains bounded draw inputs and frames, with explicit refusals and missing data, so environment geometry cannot consume this budget. Limits: first three mapped render frames, 192 draws, 64 MiB pool data, 32 MiB vertex streams, 24 MiB material inputs and 8 MiB ROI. The first two optic draws receive alpha-first mip/material/sampler capture and centered 512-square before/after regions; at the measured 2016-square source size the dot falls inside that crop. Issued, skipped and unknown draws remain distinct; incomplete pairs cannot establish shader contribution. Pistol contact policy, rifle aim, body offset and floating UI remain unchanged.

Validation: `build/F77-full-build.log` ends with all gates passed; 413 native-frame checks, zero failures; 164 pooled jobs plus the serial checks and installer resource validation. The new nonempty C++ fixture round-trips shifted packed VB/IB windows, frame domains, material payload, sampler and ROI pairs through the Python reader. Full-pass input SHA-256 is `d21f6de1ba7faaa3aedacf8092279fe77b91fe7b1f4bfe34890e9e77dc074513`. ## What "finished" means

Explorer Cam goes. Pressing nothing, the commander leaves the ship in native
stereo, with a usable HUD, inventory, weapons and menus, and returns aboard
unchanged. Six workstreams, in dependency order:

| # | Work | Size | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Activation: hook the setter's vtable slot, swap 5→3 only when admitted | small (CodeHook pattern, ~300 lines + rig) | low; addresses verified |
| W2 | EDVR frame path: re-key on-foot gates from "journal on foot" to "eyes are stereo" | medium; ~6 gates | medium; regressions on the panel path |
| W3 | HUD: port the on-foot UI elements into projected 3D space (three stages, below) | **large**; the bulk of the arc | high; RE + several flights |
| W4 | Contexts: inventory cursor, radial menus, maps, contacts, SRV, elevators, Apex, loading, intro video, deaths | medium; mostly per-context admission | medium |
| W5 | Remove Explorer Cam (6 files, ~5.7k lines, 8 keys, F5 hotkey, F8 page) | small | none, once W1-W4 fly; keys quoted and asked first |
| W6 | Body and view: show a full body like Explorer Cam's, with a ~200 ms damper on the view (not body yaw) | medium | medium; the neck census decides the damper's shape |

### W1 — activation

Install pattern exactly as `skin_entity_hook.cpp:22-26` / `explorer_cam.cpp`:
PE timestamp + image size identity (`explorer_cam.cpp:410-423`), SEH-guarded
prologue compare (`sehCheckBytes`), refuse-and-log on mismatch. Hook the
vtable slot (`vtable_hook.h:115-146`) rather than the body: the entry is a
0x21-byte .pdata stub chained into two more ranges, so a 5-byte detour is
fine but the slot is simpler. The handoff's rules carry over: forward once,
same object, caller thread; never call the setter ourselves; never write
+0x20/+0x3694/+0x3698; unknown identity → passthrough.

Admission (the handoff's own warning: an incoming 5 alone is not an on-foot
detector). Swap only when the journal's `Disembark` arrived, or Status.json
says OnFoot, within the last N s; never for the intro video, galaxy map or
loading screens. W4 grows this list; F0 measures what the natural 5-requests
actually are.

Note from the disassembly: the setter dispatches by mode class (jump table
0x28724EC: 1 → 0x2872467, 2 → 0x287247E, 3..6 → 0x287248C), so 5→3 stays
inside the same backend class. That is consistent with the handoff seeing no
resource transition fault.

### W2 — EDVR's on-foot gates

From the code map, these key on "on foot" and assume a mono panel:
`vr_world_route.h:4-17` (route owns the frame on foot);
`native_temporal.cpp:384,453` (eye shift suppressed, screen draw taken);
`ui_layer.cpp:2366-2372` (journal on foot + screen-depth draws);
`temporal_pass.cpp:1545-1553` (footSplitNow); `native_frame.cpp:307-311`
(deferred pacing on foot); `vscreen.cpp:988-996,5819` (16:9 panel shape);
`transition_flash_eye_base.cpp:285-315`. Each needs a "native stereo on foot"
branch that behaves like the cockpit. The F2 skin join is NOT coupled to
Explorer Cam (`engine_velocity.cpp:2496-2502`); it stays.

RemLok, F9 (2026-10-14): in native stereo the RemLok lines are ALWAYS drawn, even in a

### W3 — the HUD: port the on-foot UI into projected 3D space

Goal (Sean, 2026-10-13): the on-foot UI elements (radar, left panel,
inventory, radial menus, reticle, weapon label, prompts) placed in the
headset as projected 3D surfaces, not one flat HUD quad. Three stages:

1. **Does the game already place on-foot UI in 3D behind a gate?** The
   handoff restored the reticle and weapon label in both eyes in a later
   experiment, and the game re-requests cinema every frame in native mode (H4).
   F1's caller RVA locates the requester. Question: is there a 3D placement
   path, behind a gate, that the requester can reach?
2. **Element inventory from a `dump_draws` pair (cinema against native).** Per
   element: its draws, its source target and its screen rect, and whether the
   elements separate cleanly. Done offline from the dumps.
3. **Per-element placement and interaction.** Each element is body-locked,
   world-locked or head-lazy, at its own depth, composited by EDVR. Interaction
   maps a cursor or pointer onto the placed surfaces for inventory and radial
   menus. Placement choices are Sean's call after stage 2.

The machinery to composite a 2D layer into the eyes already exists (the UI
layer path, `ui_layer_math.h:8-13`, `kScreen` family at :583-587). The
handoff's runtime comparison saw the HUD resources still produced in mode 3,
with their usual PS-SRV composite consumers absent.

Fallback if stage 1 finds that the game skips the HUD render entirely in mode
3: find what skips it, starting at 0x28540B0 (mode 3..6 AND settings+0x2AE0==1
predicate, no direct callers).

### W6 — body and view

Sean: show a full body like Explorer Cam's, and damp the view. F1's census
shows the third-person body exists in native mode with zero view masks (the
F0 flight, 10:50:56: the local AMC with 15 of 54 parts instanced, including
EVASuit_Torso, EVASuit_Arms and EVASuit_Legs). The neck census (F1) says
whether the view rides the animated neck. The head joint and the camera are
not yet in one space, so the census logs both with their spaces named.
Plan: a ~200 ms damper on the view that follows the neck bob, not body yaw.
Read-only until W6 is designed.

## Proposed first flight F0 (one flight, several hypotheses)

Build on the branch, behind one temporary key `fix.native_on_foot`
(default off; listed above; removed when W1 ships as behaviour):

- the setter hook, logging every call (`native on foot: incoming=5
  effective=3 source_after=3 onfoot=… disembark_age_ms=…`) and refusing
  loudly on identity mismatch, so "never ran" is distinguishable from
  "ran and passed through";
- a once-a-second line from the runtime: submit shape per eye
  (stereo vs panel), so H3 is measured, not guessed;
- a counter per W2 gate showing which engaged while eyes were stereo.

Flight: VR in the ship, key on, disembark at a station, walk, draw a weapon,
open inventory, a radial menu and the map, board again. Then key off,
disembark again (cinema) and take `dump_draws` on foot in both modes for the
W3 census.

Decides: H3 (gate counters); W4's admission list (every natural incoming
mode and its context); W3 step 1-2 (dump comparison, offline).

## Ruled out

- ruled out: wrong motion vectors on a terminal's screen as its doubled text (F105), because in dump 221109514003 the content's shift between raw frames matches -MV plus the jitter step to 0.23 px at most (median under 0.1) over 15 frame pairs, on the text and on the terminal's body alike.
- ruled out: the UI resolve's clamp alone as the cure for a terminal's text (F105), because replayed on dump 221109514003 it changes 1 to 2% of the tooltip's pixels and leaves the striping; the resolve's rebuild from the raw frame is what reads solid.
- ruled out: the interface texture's resolution as the cause of a terminal's soft text at a distance (F108), because in dump 045208629001 DLSS reconstructs "PHAEACIA / MILITARY" legibly from the same frames (its output before the resolve) where the eye got the broken strokes of the rebuild; the texture carries the detail, the hold threw it away.
- ruled out: back-face culling hides the native torso, because CULL_FRONT on the matched 37080 torso draw changed nothing (F18).
- ruled out: the F52 audit's world rows are the main scene's camera, because they came from the first-person body pass (VS 7B0DC42D383F694C / PS 0DF03E64DF9DBEF1), whose camera is head-locked (F52 flight, log 163043); F53 takes them from main-scene passes only.
- ruled out: the povCamera joint as the body anchor, because it is a root child that follows neither the stance nor the upper-body twist: the 3P neck sat 21 cm right of the eye (F52 flight); F53 anchors the neck with the rest geometry.

## Journal

- **2026-10-13, F0 flight 3 (Epic, Pimax OpenXR, build v0.19.1-25-g15eb62b5,
  10:36).** The 6 reached admission and was refused: `reason=selector_invalid`
  on both disembark requests. Cause: our check. It read owner+0x60 and
  compared it with the selector. But the selector is embedded in its owner at
  +0x60, and owner+0x60 holds the selector's vtable (the constructor 0x27FBFC0
  writes it there). The check now reads the selector's vtable, requires it to
  be the setter's (image base + 0x52E9608), and compares owner+0x60 with the
  selector by address only (d4875a12). Every setter line now shows `sel`, `vt`,
  `owner` and `owner_back`, so a refusal shows which part failed.

  - `HumanoidModelManager::SetMode` is at EliteDangerous64.exe+0x1A112B0, vtable slot 0x30 of the manager whose vtable is +0x5200F90. Its first
    22 bytes `40 53 48 83 EC 20 48 8B D9 39 91 30 02 00 00 75 05 45 84 C0 74 1F` (push rbx; sub rsp,0x20; mov rbx,rcx; cmp [rcx+0x230],edx; ...).
    Args: rcx = manager, edx = mode (0 first-person models, 1 third-person), r8b = force. The mode is stored at [manager+0x230].
  - The per-frame hook is the povCamera joint handler at EliteDangerous64.exe+0x19B1240, entered for every humanoid. Its first 32 bytes
    `40 53 48 83 EC 20 48 85 D2 48 89 74 24 30 48 8D B2 B0 01 00 00 B8 A0 02 00 00 48 0F 44 F0 48 8D` match the brief. The manager is
    `[rdx+0x1B0]` (rdx = the receiver). Local player only: `[manager+0x238] != 0` and `[manager] == base+0x5200F90`.
  - Conflict check: Explorer Cam's FindJoint sites are return addresses +0x19B12D5 and +0x19B1359, both past the 6 bytes this hook steals
    (+0x19B1240..+0x19B1245, `push rbx; sub rsp,0x20`). No other hook in the tree touches either entry.
  Mechanism: the SetMode detour (a callback relay, ecm::buildCallbackRelay) records the game's requests for the captured local manager and,
  while the body is wanted as third person, forwards a request for 0 as 1 (as 0 while aiming down sights; ADS is Status.json Flags2 bit 5,
  `journalAds()` beside the F16 breathable flag). A request for 1 is never changed. The povCamera hook runs the original first, then holds
  the local manager at the desired mode through the SetMode trampoline, so EDVR's own calls never reach the detour. When the hold ends
  (key to game, native ended, session ended, shutdown) the game's own mode is restored once. The game's mode is the last game request,
  or the value read before the first hold when no request was seen. A captured manager not seen for 60 frames is dropped without a restore.
  The two hooks install when the key first reads third, after the identity check, the vtable slot check and both prologue checks; the
  relays are placed within two gigabytes; nothing is patched if any check fails. Flat profile: refused.
  Logs (the hook threads never log; they queue, and the frame boundary writes):
  - install: `native on foot body mode: installed -- SetMode at EliteDangerous64.exe+0x1A112B0 ..., stolen=N bytes, prologue 22 bytes verified, relay at 0x.. (thread T)` and the povCamera line with 32 bytes.
  - `native on foot body mode: game asked M (thread T) -> forwarded M'` (on a change only)
  - `native on foot body mode: set M (ADS a, frame thread T2)` (each EDVR call)
  - `native on foot body mode: restored to M (reason, frame thread T2)`
  Read it this way: a `game asked 0 -> forwarded 1` with `set 1` and no `restored` is the hold working; an install line with no `set` line
  means the local manager was never captured (the `local third-person humanoid seen` line says it was).
  Note: the first run of this build will not show the body's model change in the logs, only the calls; the visible result is the flight's.

Ry(psi) . err_body, with D = diag(-1,-1,+1). err_body is the target minus the camera (the trims are in the target); the sign follows the measured plant (cam_body moves by D . applied at psi 0), so the loop closes on the rig's plant. The head's motion in body axes is Ry(psi)^-1 . diag(1,1,-1) . tS. psi = seated head yaw (render row 2) less the headset's yaw in the body (C row 2 less the AMC basis row 2). The psi sign and the z column are not measured: the calibrate flight decides them. The `view map:` line prints psi every 5 s.
- **Calibrate (`fix.native_on_foot_body_align = calibrate`, one flight).** Six 1 s steps: +5 cm seated X, rest, +5 cm Y, rest, +5 cm Z, rest, repeating. No loop, no guard: the offsets are scheduled. At the start of each step the step that just ended is measured: the camera's body position and tS, the mean over its last 0.5 s less the mean over the 0.5 s before it began (`calibrate step ...`). The body<-seated 3x3 comes from the three active steps.
- **Live now pose (`fix.now_pose = next | render`, live).** The d3d11 key goes to the runtime through the native frame output, version 9 (version 8 plus one word, `nowPoseRender`). The client asks 9 first and steps down to 8 for an older d3d11.dll. The runtime's `g_nowPoseRender` (head_pose_time.h) picks the answer: next (default) locates Elite's "now" request one display period past the latest frame's display time, as today; render locates it at that display time itself (the WaitGetPoses latch's instant). With render, the pose cache's display answers are not used (its slots are one period ahead), so every display call takes the owner path. Each change is logged on both sides (`now pose: ...`), and the runtime logs its default at start (`native_now_pose_config`).
- **pose_cache and frame_end_overlap** stay per-launch keys in edvr_openxr.ini (already read at startup, already logged at start). They are not made live; a relaunch flips them.
- **Marker angles.** Every 5 s in the marker path: M (read at entry, F37) against this call's list-B view, and against the runtime's now answer (`M against C ... M against the now answer ...`). That shows which pose M was built from.
- **Overseer note.** The `next` answer may not be what fixed terrain black squares (the TERRAIN CULL COVER may have). now_pose is an open choice; Sean watches for black terrain squares with render.
- **Deviations.** The `neck-to-camera` offset is logged, not applied (F39's interpretation stands). The view map's psi sign and the z column are unverified until the calibrate flight.

### 2026-10-15: F42 (frame-locked head pose, now_pose = render_locked)

- **Why.** Flight evidence: now_pose render plus forward is the most stable marker; pose_cache off is much worse. The design pass found at least four head samples per frame: the latched render pose, the game's pose one period on, every "now" query re-located at display time (under render those bypass the cache's display slots), and the cache slots.
- **The third state.** `fix.now_pose = next | render | render_locked` (live). The frame output's version 9 word carries 0, 1 or 2; the runtime's `g_nowPoseMode` (head_pose_time.h) holds it. render_locked answers every display "now" call with the latched render pose of the frame.
- **The latch.** The render pose is kept in PoseFrame at the publish point of waitPoses. The pose cache's record gets a `frame` slot (target = the display time). publishPoseCache runs for render_locked even with pose_cache off, takes no locate for its now and next slots, and reuses the record's keys and invalidation, so a withdrawn publication is never served.
- **The answer.** locateHeadFor tries the frame slot first (display call, seated origin); a miss falls through to the cache and the hop and is counted as a fallback.
- **The game pose.** Under render_locked waitPoses sets `game = render` (time included), so the game array and GetLastPoses(ForTrackedDeviceIndex) read the same sample. The separate locate of the game's pose is skipped.
- **Proof line.** `head pose samples per frame: mean ..., max ... distinct; now answers: latched ..., other ...; fallbacks from the latched path ...; angle_delta p95 ... deg` once a second (to the trace, not the gap sink). The samples: the render latch, the game array and each display "now" answer, hashed per frame (the bytes of the pose). Expect 1 distinct, 0 fallbacks, 0.000 degrees at p95 under render_locked. GetLast* read the same snapshot as the render and game samples, so they are not hashed separately.
- **Deviations.** The proof line is on its own line at the gap's cadence (not appended to the gap line), so the rig's gap-line count is unchanged. The rig does not exercise render_locked (the default is next); the flight is the test.
- **Risk.** The terrain cull (display-time answers caused black squares on fast turns before the cull cover). Sean will fly a fast planet-surface turn with render_locked and watch for black squares.

### 2026-10-15: F44 (draw-time marker instrument, measure only)

- **Key.** `fix.native_on_foot_marker_probe` (off, hidden, live, TEMPORARY; VR only). Nothing drawn changes; no constant buffer, pool or binding is written. The machinery is `src\d3d11\draw_record_tag.h`, meant for the weapon ammo readout next.
- **Tag.** reticleWorldPost writes each world marker's t' (not key 10) with a 24-bit sentinel in the lowest 8 mantissa bits of x, y and z: the key (8 bits) and the render frame (16 bits), salted. Under 2^-15 relative per component; a zero, denormal or non-finite component is left untagged (counted). The tag, t' as written and P = node+0x50 go to the render thread through per-key sequence-counted atomic cells.
- **Find.** A t33 pool is watched once an on-foot HUD draw (VS 95D01BA609BF7500 or 46546443FD3C3F88) binds it; it must be a structured buffer of stride 336. At each Unmap of a DISCARD or NO_OVERWRITE map, +16 of each record is checked for the sentinels of the last 8 frames: the last-found index per key first, then the whole mapped range with 16-byte streaming loads (at most 4 scans a frame; over 2 ms backs off 30 frames). Each find keeps (pool, record index, X0).
- **Match.** Each HUD draw whose pool has a find (this frame or the last) copies its b0 rows 9-11, b1 row 275 and instance stream entries (the single stride-8 buffer at StartInstanceLocation; v0.x) into a staging slot; the first pool-family draw of each eye a frame (eye by the depth probe) copies the world b0 rows 9-11 and b1 row 275. Read back 2 or more frames later without a wait. When FirstElement + v0.x is a find: v0 = V_hud (X0 - o_hud), v_target = V_w (P - o_w).
- **Log, once a second.** `marker record found at index N` (key, tag age, map type, finds at the last index, index same or changed, X0 == t' bit-exact or not, scan times), or `sentinel NOT found`; per eye the angle v0 vs v_target (mean, max), the V_hud vs V_w rotation, head speed from the ring (mean, max), and the frame check |P - o_w| beside |t'| and |X0 - o_hud|; a draws line with each refusal counted (stride, stream, constants, no find, no world view, rows not a rotation, and so on). Each refusal reason is also named once.
- **Deviations.** V_hud and V_w are GPU copies of what each draw binds (ranged binds included), not a binding shadow plus mapped contents: the copy is what the draw reads, and no CPU copy of every b0 write is made. A HUD draw with no scene depth bound takes the eye whose world rows are nearest (counted as "eye by nearest world rows").
- **Not done.** No correction. The flight is the test: whether the sentinel survives into the pool at all, the record index's stability, and the angle at rest and while turning.

Output span: [job+0x28] when [X+0x210] is 0, else [[X+0x1F0]+0xA0] when count-1 < [[X+0x1F0]+0xE0]; 0x43FB740 is never called; count = the u16 at P, cap 0xC0. On the worker: no allocation, logging or locks (a try-flag skips a second local call), every read and write under SEH; statistics go through a sequence counter to the frame thread.
- **Key.** `fix.native_on_foot_pose_freeze` = off | probe (default) | on; hidden, live, TEMPORARY. probe writes no game memory. on writes M'_j = local_j x M'_parent(j) for F in parent-first order, anchored at M_anim(a), the local blended from the animated toward the rest record (quaternion nlerp, position lerp) by a weight that moves over 0.3 s; the weight rises only while not ADS (journalAds) and the animated head (joint 44, read in the hook before any write) has held its height within 2 cm for 1 s. A faulted write stands the writes down for the session. Pure math in `native_on_foot_core.h` (`pfzFrozenSet`, `pfzRestModel`, `pfzBlendRecord`, `PfzBlend`, `PfzHeadRest`), checked in native_frame_test.
- **What it logs.** Once per X: `pose freeze: plan for X=...` (P against GetPoseData, the joint count, the foot's index, a, the torso child, F's member count and list, whether 35, 36, 34 and 44 are in F); the rest chain against the game's own 0xFDE0D0 for 34 and 44 (a leaf that reads P and writes 64 bytes; called only when its entry bytes match). Every 5 s on foot: Animate calls, local calls, the thread id and thread changes, [X+0x210], [X+0x12C], [X+0x128], [X+0x212], calls per output buffer, the count, joints 34 and 44 animated minus the rest chain anchored at a (mean, min, max and mean vector, mm), the weight and frames written. Every 5 s from the census: GetModelMatrix(34) against the hook's newest span matrix of 34 (and the written one when on), with the age. Each hook refusal is named once.
- **Risks.** A weapon attached to a 3P hand would float away from a frozen hand. The skin is uploaded from the t2 rows (APPLY_BIND_POSE) and the function that packs those rows was not found, so the skin may read another buffer: then on changes the animated matrices and nothing visible changes (not confirmed either way; the span cross-check says only whether GetModelMatrix sees the write). The write lands after [X+0x12C] = 1, so a reader that rotates the ring in the meantime may miss it. The bind pose of the arms may be a T or A pose.
- **Not done.** Not flown, not installed. The frame thread drains the statistics every 5 s, not at 1 Hz. Only the 3P skeleton's X is used (the local AMC's own interface is not read separately).

### 2026-10-15: F50 (the marker lag delta against a per-eye baseline; the body's vertical lock)

- **Why (F47 flight, log edvr_gfx_20261015_141552).** Both eyes matched (eye 0 to record 8, eye 1 to record 9), but the fix was gated off every frame: F47 projected the world point P through the marker's b0, which lives in the tracking (seat) frame, about 54 degrees from the world's. ruled out: P through the marker's b0 as the delta, because b0 is in the seat frame, not the world's.
- **What changed (marker, `fix.native_on_foot_marker_fix`).** `drawtag::ndcLagDelta`: ndc_marker = the record's X0 through the draw's own b0 rows 4, 5, 7 at o_hud; ndc_P = P through the eye's world b1 rows 270..273 at o_w; m = ndc_marker - ndc_P; (dx, dy) = -(m - c), which moves the marker to ndc_P + c. c is a per-eye baseline (`drawtag::LagBaseline`): seeded from the first 30 frames with the head under 3 deg/s, then an EMA (alpha 0.05) of m on frames with the head under 3 deg/s and |m - c| < 0.01 NDC. No patch, and no hold, until it is seeded with a standard deviation under 0.5 px. Reset on a change of b0 row 5 or row 7 scale, the marker target's size, or the eye's matched draw place; 90 slow-head frames in a row over 0.01 NDC start the seed again. Gate |dx|, |dy| < 0.05 NDC. The one-frame hold, the both-eyes rule, the ordinal guard and the one patched B10B draw per eye are unchanged.
- **Rationale.** The flight measured c at about (0.0000, +0.03609) NDC in both eyes, constant across distance and position: a frustum-centre difference between the HUD's and the world's projections, a static calibration. What is left after it is the lag.
- **What changed (body, `fix.native_on_foot_body_align_vertical` = off | on, default off, hidden, live, TEMPORARY).** Body vertical locked to the ground (feet clipped under terrain with pov at F48). With vertical off, body mode drops the body-up component (AMC row 1) of the body run's position and velocity after the filter, so d moves the body only along its right and forward axes; the up trim is left out of the target; F48's standing height is logged, not applied. With vertical on, F48's behaviour.
- **What it logs.** Per eye each second (`marker fix (F50, ...)`): c in NDC and px, its standard deviation and state (seeding, seeded, ready), resets and the last reason; |m - c| in px by head speed (< 3, 3..20, 20..60, >= 60 deg/s); patched draws, held, refused as not ready, gated; the residual after the patch, X0 through the patched rows read back minus (P + c), by head speed (about 0 at every speed if the patch took). The honesty check: m on slow-head frames binned by head pitch (< -15, -15..15, > 15 deg) and roll (|roll| < 10, >= 10 deg) since the last reset; a spread over 2 px between two bins of 30 or more frames logs `the baseline is not constant: masking`, and the fix is not to be claimed. Body: the vertical-off note on each entry to body; once a second the up component d would have had (the target's up in body axes, mean and range) and the per-frame step dropped, beside the standing height.
- **Rig.** native_frame_test: the lag delta lands the marker on ndc_P + c and its gate refuses; the baseline seeds over 30 slow frames, refuses a fast head and a far m, restarts after 90 far frames; the vertical drop.
- **Not done.** Not flown, not installed. The honesty check logs only; it does not stop the patch. The would-be vertical is the target's up (what d converges to with vertical on), not a shadow filter's output. The eye-assignment reset keys on the eye's matched draw place, not on the record index.

### 2026-10-15: F54 (the held weapon: MGMC records measured; shifted with the FP raise)

- **Why.** F51/F53 raise the FP arms (the FP AMC's records) but the held weapon stays put, so it floats off the hands while the raise is on. The static RE (build 332841) names the likely renderer: MotionGraphModelComponent (MGMC). Its submit job 0x43ED820 (thunk 0x43B796A; rcx = the MGMC) skips an object whose mask [obj+0x380] is zero, else writes one 0x150-byte record at obj+0x230 (position obj+0x240..0x248, copy obj+0x354..0x35C) from the instance matrix every run, and hands its pointer to 0x4C837B0 (deferred). The viewmodel byte is obj+0x1C8. Not proven: what the weapon entity is made of is data, not code.
- **What changed.** Two hooks through the F9 relay plumbing (`installF9ProbeInto`), installed in every VR session behind the identity check. The MGMC post-hook (35 prologue bytes verified, 8 stolen: mov rax,rsp; mov [rax+0x20],rsi; push rdi, run by the trampoline after the relay enters the wrapper; the return value forwarded unchanged). The 0x4C837B0 pre-hook (24 bytes verified, 7 stolen; twelve arguments forwarded; the caller from `_ReturnAddress`, since the relay jumps). Both prologues match the offline exe. SHIFT: only while `g_f51FpOn` (raise_fp on, body mode, native stereo on foot, the same gate as the FP AMC shift), an MGMC with mask != 0, byte +0x1C8 != 0, and its record within 0.3 m of FP handAttach 51 or 52 (world, unshifted, published by the frame thread each frame) before the shift moves both position copies by the published FP raise (constant raise_cm, 10 cm, along the up row) after the job returns. Not cumulative: the job rewrites the record each run. Never with mask 0. The hooks do no allocation, logging or locks; reads and writes under SEH; the counters and tables are drained once a second on the frame thread. No new key.
- **What it logs (once a second, native stereo on foot).** `weapon (F54): MGMC submits`: calls, mask 0, unreadable, tabled, the local FP weapon's matched and shifted counts, the raise d, and the four handAttach joints (FP R51 L52, 3P R66 L67, world). Up to 8 `MGMC <ptr>` lines nearest the hands: the byte, the mask, the record position, the distance to each of the four joints, calls and shifts, marked when within 0.3 m with the byte set; a count of the rest. `0x4C837B0 calls` (the AMC's excluded) and one line per caller RVA (known sites named: MGMC, GUI mesh, the five unidentified roots), with calls, records and the record nearest an FP hand (index, pointer, position, distance; up to 256 records scanned a call). Install or refusal lines for each hook. The F51 line's weapon text now points at the F54 lines.
- **Risks.** The muzzle flash and the lights do not follow: they are driven by their own joints or records, not this record. The ammo readout (the AR display, HumanoidARRenderComponent 0x1A14320) is built from the game camera matrix and submitted through the GUI path, camera-space, so it does not follow either. A wrong match (another viewmodel MGMC within 0.3 m) would rise too; the lines show what matched. The joints lag the job by up to a frame (about 3 cm at a walk), inside the 0.3 m match.
- **Rig.** native_frame_test: the 0.3 m match (0.2 and 0.29 m match; 0.35 m and NaN do not), the mask, byte and unknown-joint gates, and the shift moving both record copies by the same d.
- **Not done.** Not flown, not installed. Whether the weapon is an MGMC at all is the flight's question (the per-MGMC lines answer it). Only the 8 MGMCs nearest the hands are listed per second, not every one. The 0x4C837B0 tally records only while native stereo is on foot.

The bent spine list is written with the square-up's write (an arm the IK does not write rides it). The bend rides the arm IK's hook path: `pfz::g_ikWanted` is now also set by the bend key in full 3P, and an FP-snapshot or G refusal skips only the arms and the square-up. No allocation, logging or locks in the hook; reads and writes under SEH (the existing guarded write; a fault stands the IK and the bend down).

The key's change line.

### 2026-10-16: F59b (the full-3P head follow through ADS, its fallback, the eye - neck residual)

- **Cause of the ADS dropout (F58 log edvr_gfx_20261016_021950, scratchpad f58.txt; code).** The body frame was there: 40 of the 49 `head follow ... from none` seconds were ADS with a fresh AMC sample and the pov joint (the F58 state `ramping out: ADS` is reached only past the `no fresh AMC sample` and `no pov joint` tests). `alignTick`'s wait chain ends `else if (ads) wait = "held: aiming down sights"`, so in ADS the body-target block never ran (`g_f58FollowSrc` stayed -1, printed `none (no body frame ...)`) and `bodyFilter` got err = 0: d did not hold, it decayed to 0 at tau 0.1 s (5 cm a frame), so the 3P body went back to its own place for the whole aim. The other 9 seconds were a stale AMC sample (over 100 ms; `held: no fresh AMC sample`).
- **What changed.** Full 3P only (body mode, `hide_fp_body` and `body_unclip` on; `f58Full3P` is now computed before the waits): (1) ADS no longer waits; the target runs through it as outside it (the F48 standing window gets `ads`, so ADS is still never a rest). (2) The body frame (`nofoot::followPick`): live (a fresh sample with the head census and the pov; it becomes the last good frame); else the AMC matrix (a fresh sample without the census: its matrix, job camera and root, the last good frame's 3P joints carried into it through their body coordinates, `nofoot::carryBody`); else the last good frame itself; never one older than 0.5 s (`kFollowHoldMs`); past it, none (the old waits). (3) A change between two sources ramps the target from the last output over 0.25 s (`nofoot::FollowBlend`; the change frame outputs the last output exactly); to or from none is immediate, as every wait was. The bend still gets the sample as read. No hook changed; no game memory is read by the new code. Outside full 3P nothing changes.
- **What it logs (once a second, full 3P, on the F58 line's tick).** `head follow (F59b): head follow source: job camera | amc matrix | last good frame (N ms) | none`, the frames per source this second, the oldest frame used, the ramp, ADS. `eye - neck residual after the shift, the bend and the square-up` (body axes right, up, forward; eye = the job camera): from the hook's published post-bend neck 34 (its (T - N1) means; T = (eye - d) + rest, so eye - (N1 + d) = (T - N1) - rest; the square-up turns about 34's vertical and leaves 34 where the bend put it), cm per axis and the norm of the means, bend calls and written; and the same less the rest offset (0, 15.5, 16.1). When no bend call measured it: `the hook's post-correction neck is not available this second ... not inferred`. A second line: eye - (census neck + d), per-frame mean and norm mean; whether the census's GetModelMatrix reads the hook's bent pose is not verified (equal to the hook's figure means it does).
- **Rig.** native_frame_test (201 checks): the pick (live wins; matrix or last up to 500 ms, 501 is none; no last frame is none), the ramp (no jump on the change frame, half at 0.125 s, there at 0.25 s; to and from none immediate), the body-axes residual on a 90 deg yaw, `carryBody`, and (T - N1) - rest = eye - (N1 + d).
- **Not done.** Not flown, not installed. The hook's residual exists only while the bend runs (the key on, full 3P, a plan); with the bend off only the census figure is logged. The residual is per-second means of the hook's (T - N1), not a per-frame norm. ADS in full 3P now moves the body with the head where F58 held it at 0: whether that suits aiming is the flight's question. No key added.

Since G subtracts d, d_w does not depend on the d it was measured at (open loop). The frame thread (`f60FitStep`): a weapon is held when the publication is under 100 ms old and both distance gates are open; the ramp (0.3 s in and out) rises in full-3P body mode with `arm_ik = on`, its base weight above 0 and the slider above 0, and is zeroed at once outside that; fit = slider x ramp. The hook allocates, logs and locks nothing; it reads only its own copies.

### 2026-10-16: F61 (rotation calibration: does a seated yaw or pitch reach the game camera's orientation?)

- **What changed.** New temporary key `fix.native_on_foot_rot_calibrate` = off | on (default off, hidden, live). On, while native stereo is on foot, the d3d11 frame thread (`rotCalTick`) publishes a scheduled seated rotation: yaw +5 deg about the head for 1 s, rest 1 s, pitch +5 deg about the head's right axis for 1 s, rest 1 s, repeating (`nofoot::rotCalStep`, F40's calibrate shape; no loop, no guard). It rides version 9 frame output in the retired slots `reservedOffset[0..1]` (radians; `reservedOffsetEnabled` stays 0, so no version bump and no older runtime reads it). Off publishes zero, and the runtime turns the origin back.
- **Runtime (`rotPoll`, after `eyePoll` in `seatPoll`, no frame open).** The yaw turns `lookSeated` about the vertical through the head, as `lookPoll` does, with the same `eyeApplied` fold. **The pitch path was not wired** (a `SeatPose` carries yaw only), so it was added: an overlay that turns the seated space about the head's right axis through the head (`seatPosePitched`, composed at every `seated.replace` by `seatedPoseFor`; zero pitch is exactly `xrFromSeatPose`, so the default is unchanged). The pivot and axis are the head's when the rotation leaves zero and are kept until it returns, so the return is exact. `lookRebase` zeroes the applied rotation. Each apply is traced: `rot_calibrate_runtime` with the applied yaw and pitch and the head's seated yaw and pitch before and after.
- **What it logs (d3d11, per 1 s step).** `rot calibrate (F61): step ...`: the commanded rotation before and after; the change in orientation (dyaw, dpitch, in each source's own axes: yaw + = turned left, pitch + = up), the mean over the step's last 0.5 s against the 0.5 s before it began, from (1) the list-B camera C (`g_worldC`, rows 0..2 read as right, up, forward), (2) the scene rows cb1 270..273 (the engine-motion source camera, `engineVelocityLastSourceCameraRows`: forward is the clip w column, right and up the clip x and y columns) and (3) the runtime's render head; the head's own motion (render + the command's change: a seated rotation of +a turns the reported head by -a); per-step frame and missing-input counts. After each yaw and pitch step: `rotation reaches the game camera: yes|no; gain X; sign Y`, the camera from cb1 when measured, else C; residual = camera change - head's own motion; no under 1 deg; gain = |residual / command|; sign - means the camera turned with the reported head.
- **Verdict.** Not yet measured.
- **Rigs.** native_frame_test (209 checks): the schedule, the three sources' deltas (left turn yaw +10, rise pitch +10), the head subtraction and the verdict rule (0.9 deg no, 1 deg yes, gain and sign). openxr_native_test (`rot_calibrate_cases.h`): the pitch overlay leaves the head in place and turns its seated pitch by -5 deg with its yaw unchanged; zero is the pose; +5 then -5 is the pose again.
- **Not done.** Not flown, not installed. The C axes' labels (row 0 right, row 1 up) are assumed; cb1 is the definitive one. The engine-motion source camera may be either eye; the step lines carry its sample count. The pitch is not folded into `eyeApplied`: fly with body align off. Temporary keys added: `fix.native_on_foot_rot_calibrate`.

(6) ADS: `_arm_ads_shoulder_forward_cm` defaults to 0 (was 5; code and edvr.ini); `fitShoulderTarget` drops the forward push and takes k_reach = `fitReachK(adsW)` (0.82 to 1.0); d_w's lateral is blended over 0.3 s at each change of the ADS flag (`FitAdsLat`). The 5 cm cap, the filters and the 0.3 s ramp are unchanged; the hook allocates, logs and locks nothing.
- **What it logs (once a second, with the F60 line).** `weapon fit (F62a): weights`: forward and lateral weight means, the sliders, ramp and raised factor now, the raised factor and grip gate means, frames applied, the disengage factor, d_w - d_head and the pull (right, forward, cm), the pull's max and clamped frames, the shoulder-mid residual Sd - Umid (right, forward), the ADS lateral blend's frames. `weapon fit (F62a): bend`: the bend's calls and bent counts, calls at the fit's limits and their hits (8, 8, 6), all hits, suspended calls and the before-residual max; per arm in ADS (weight over 0.5) the reach after the assist (mean, max) and the elbow's interior angle (mean, min); k_reach. The F58 line adds the fit-limited and suspended counts; the F60 line prints the raised factor and the k_reach in use.

Lines `eye capture (F62a): marker dump series armed` (the folder and file names) and `... series <stamp> (<why>)` (frames, sequences and whether consecutive, final and pre crops of 32, the files); with fewer than 32 final crops a self-check line gives the count per reason (not reached, not tried, no fresh projection, staging, write) and the first six missing crops with their ages.

The F60 Sd case now passes k_reach; the F59b residual case uses the full-3P offset.

The F60 flight's before-residual was 55..58 cm with the fit engaged and about 32 cm without; if the fit's new gates do not bring it under 35 cm the bend stays suspended (watch the suspended count). Whether the fit engages with a weapon raised depends on the grip gate holding above 0.5 (the F60 lines' last gate was 0.0..0.2 in most seconds, 0.90 once); that is the flight's question. The crop centre is still the drawn marker when its read-back is fresh, else P. Temporary keys added: `fix.native_on_foot_body_fit_lateral`.

### 2026-10-16: F62b (the ADS head-aim: the headset steers the aim while aiming down sights, the view cancels the game's turn)

- **What changed.** New key `fix.native_on_foot_ads_head_aim` = on (default) | off, hidden, live, TEMPORARY, with two hidden live sign keys `_ads_head_aim_yaw_sign` and `_ads_head_aim_pitch_sign` (1 default, -1, 0 = that axis off). It applies only in native on foot with the full-3P body (body align = body, hide_fp_body and body_unclip on), the look hooks armed, look to aim not engaged and the F61 calibration off, while ADS (`journalAds`), with the weight wA (0.15 s in, 0.3 s out). Each frame (`adsAimTick`, before `lookPublishTick` and `alignTick`): (1) the headset's heading and elevation step since the last frame (the head in natural LOCAL) times wA is queued as look input through the F22 update hook (rotate-abs and pitch-abs = old + ours for one call, restored after), divided by the measured gain (the processor's delta over the whole input; fallback 1.0); (2) the processor hook splits its deltas (comp+0x5F4 yaw, +0x5F8 pitch) into ours and the player's (linear, as F22), and ours goes into the seated rotation: the yaw through the look total (`lookPoll`, about the head), the pitch through a new overlay about the seat's right axis through the head (`adsPoll`), clamped to +-60 deg; (3) the position lock wA (h - h_entry) (LOCAL) rides the eye alignment; (4) the body: F60's fit weights go to 1 and the head's target is ignored by wA (`adsFitDetach`, past F62a's disengage and 12 cm clamp), only with a fresh weapon-fit measurement. Release: the yaw is kept (a rebase); the pitch unwinds over 0.3 s by injecting the opposite while the cancel follows what the game applies, any remainder is chased 0.2 s and then dropped (logged); the lock and the body go with wA. A trip, or the feature no longer applying (the key off, on foot ended, not full 3P, look to aim engaged, the calibration on), returns the seated rotation to zero through the reset serial, the kept yaw included. The hook paths allocate, log and lock nothing (atomics; guarded reads and writes).
- **New interface: frame version 10, input version 3.** The d3d11 half needs the headset's own motion, which the seated render head cannot give while the seated space turns under it (rebuilding it from the reported head plus the published cancel is a loop with a frame of latency each way, marginally stable). Version 10 is a ladder step like 7: input version 3 adds `localHead[12]`, `localValid` and a reserved word after the version 2 words (`EDVR_NATIVE_FRAME_INPUT_SIZE_2`); the answer's retired `reservedYaw` carries the ADS pitch. The runtime asks 10 first and steps down to 9 (input version 2) for an older d3d11.dll; an older runtime's version 2 input is still read; a mismatched pair is refused. The runtime locates the head in LOCAL at the display time only for a version 10 ask.
- **Runtime beside it.** `seatedPoseFor` composes the ADS overlay (axis `seatRightAxis` of the seat's yaw, so a pitch after any yaw stays a pitch) under F61's; zero is the old pose. `lookPoll` now pivots about the head less the applied eye offset: about the head itself, `eyePoll`'s re-applied LOCAL offset moved the reported head by (I - R^-1) e. With no eye offset (every case before F62b's lock) the pivot is unchanged; look to aim with view-mode body align gets the same correction (never flown together).
- **Conventions, as the rig verifies them.** The seat convention: yaw + = left, pitch + = up. F61: a seated +a moves the camera by -a (gain 1, sign -), so a seated +a cancels an aim turn of +a. The game: yaw delta + = right, pitch delta + = up for signs 1 (both ASSUMED). A head yaw of +10 deg asks the game for -10 deg; the applied -10 deg is a seated yaw of +10 deg; the camera's net turn = aim + head - seated = +10 deg, the head's. The lock's offset is dH (LOCAL) = D (-e_body) in F40's map, so the camera's body motion diag(1, 1, -1) dH + D s is zero.
- **What it logs.** Per second while engaged or releasing, `ADS head aim (F62b): <state>, weight`: the head's yaw and pitch (LOCAL head, input version, steps, skips), injected (seat convention, the queued input, the gain measured or fallback), applied (ours) and the player's own, cancelled, the seated yaw carried and pitch (in flight, clamp hits); a second line: the camera - head residual (the camera's turn since the base, cb1 270..273 when fresh else C, less the head's turn and the player's own aim turn; ratio per axis: about 0 the view follows the head, -2 that axis's sign is inverted, -1 the camera does not take the aim there), the lock (cm, LOCAL) and the head's distance from entry, the guard's figures, the hook's writes, processor calls and refusals, the signs. Transitions: engaged, release, release complete (pitch unwound or dropped), stops (why), RUNAWAY GUARD TRIPPED (why), guard cleared; every 5 s in full-3P ADS when not engaged, why. Runtime trace: `ads_head_aim_runtime` (the first LOCAL head; every 5 s while the pitch is not zero). d3d11 log: `local head (F62b): frame input version 3 accepted`.
- **Guards.** More than 270 deg of seated yaw in 3 s; |camera - head| at least 8 deg and half the head's turn since the base, grown 4 deg over 0.5 s without falling 1 deg below its peak; a refused look-value restore. Each trips the feature off (the seated rotation to zero) until the key toggles, a sign key changes or on foot re-enters. The seated pitch is clamped to +-60 deg and the injected pitch is held inside it; the queued input is capped at 20 deg of turn.
- **Rig.** native_frame_test (230 checks): the sign and gain chain above (a measured gain of 0.5 doubles the input from the second frame; an inverted sign reads a residual of -2 x the head), the gain fallback, the LOCAL head's steps (left +, up +, the 180 deg seam, jumps refused), the 270 deg guard in 3 s (not over 4 s), the residual guard, the 60 deg clamp, the ramp (0.15 s in, 0.3 s out), the release unwind (20 deg to 0 over 0.3 s, the view still), the lock through F40's map, the body detach; version 10 with input 3 answered with the pitch and the LOCAL head, 9 with input 2 without, mismatched pairs refused. openxr_native_test: the ladder (a version 9 provider steps 10 down and a pitch it scribbles is not believed) and the overlay (after a 90 deg seat yaw a +8 deg pitch about the seat's right axis is -8 deg of reported pitch, no roll, the head in place).
- **Honest status.** Built, not installed, not flown. Nothing in the chain is measured: the injected look input reaching the aim in ADS (the pitch-abs write and the +0x5F8 delta are F22's static reads, never flown; the yaw path spun in F22-F24), the game's two signs (ASSUMED; the sign keys and the residual ratio are there to find them in one flight), the gain and the linear split, whether the game camera takes the aim's pitch in ADS (if not, the pitch ratio reads -1 and the guard trips: pitch sign 0 is the yaw-only fallback). The seated cancel's gain 1 and sign - are F61's result as the arc's analysis reports it; the F61 entry's verdict line above was not updated here.
- **Not done.** The cancel lands a frame or two after the game's turn (the runtime applies at the next WaitGetPoses), so a fast turn shows a residual of rate x latency; nothing compensates it. While aiming and moving the runtime replaces the seated space up to three times a frame (yaw, lock, pitch). Any stop returns the kept yaw to zero (the key off, a trip, leaving on foot), which turns the view by it. Temporary keys added: `fix.native_on_foot_ads_head_aim`, `fix.native_on_foot_ads_head_aim_yaw_sign`, `fix.native_on_foot_ads_head_aim_pitch_sign`.

### 2026-10-16: F62c (the marker patch without the trust gate; the waypoint series about this frame's P)

- **Evidence (log edvr_gfx_20261016_034818, the F59 16-frame image dump `eye_035139_mk_*`, marker fix off).** The drawn marker lags the displayed world by about 1.75 frames: 60 to 130 px at 4032 while the head turned at 115 to 185 deg/s, about 0.8 px per deg/s at 4032. P through the scene rows (cb1 270..273) follows the displayed world's motion within 5 to 10% on the pre-UI crops. So ndc(P through the scene rows) + e is the patch's target. F53's trust gate refused about 45% of frames, because the scene rows and the temporal pass's rows are not meant to agree (ruled out above).
- **What changed (the marker patch, `fix.native_on_foot_marker_fix`, off by default).** `drawtag::patchDecide`: a draw whose key is matched in this eye and in the other is patched on every frame where the eye's scene rows are this frame's, P has a find, both w > 0 and |dx|, |dy| < 0.1 NDC (was 0.05). Otherwise the last good delta is held for the one frame after it; otherwise the draw is refused. The trust gate is gone; its comparison stays in the F52 line as a measure. The patch measures against the scene rows (`g_cpuWorld`) whatever `fix.native_on_foot_marker_ref` says, so that key now steers only the F52 measure lines. e (36.3 px) and the one-frame hold are kept; the learned baseline c stays logged only.
- **What changed (the waypoint series, read only).** Crops are 1024x1024 (`drawtag::kMarkerDumpCrop`), centred on THIS frame's P through the eye's scene rows. P now carries its probe frame, and the capture's frame must equal it (age 0; a frame's draws and submits come before its Present). An eye-frame with P off the eye (w <= 0, or NDC outside -1..1) or with no P this frame is skipped. The CSV adds per frame and eye: the head's speed in deg/s; ndc_P with its w, key and age in frames; ndc_marker (the game's rows, read back) with its age in ms and in frames; the fix's state; whether the fix patched the eye this frame (fresh or held), with its key, draw count and dx, dy in NDC and px. The eye run's crop clamp is now `drawtag::cropOrigin` (same rule).
- **What it logs.** With the fix key on, once a second per eye, `marker fix (F62c)`: the patch-applied fraction (draws bound at the issue over decisions), the fresh decisions, the refusals (scene rows stale, record not matched per eye-frame, both-eyes rule not met, w not positive, |d| over 0.1 NDC, no P, other: ranged b0, no CPU b0 rows, no CPU o_hud), the one-frame hold's uses and the bind refusals. The series' end line counts the skipped eye-frames (off-screen, no P this frame, no P yet) and the patched ones; the self-check names the skipped crops.
- **Rig.** native_frame_test: a frame with the scene and temporal rows 5.0 px apart at P fails F53's rule and is patched onto P (scene rows) + e; the 0.1 NDC limit (0.0999 patches; 0.1 and 0.1001 are refused with nothing to hold); the one-frame hold (once after a good frame, not twice; unmatched and both-eyes refusals never hold); the 1024 crop about P at age 0 (centre (2520, 1814.4), box (2008, 1302) in a 4032 eye; a one-frame-old P, w <= 0, an NDC outside the eye or NaN skip; the edge clamp, flipV, a right-eye region).
- **Not done.** Not flown, not installed. With the fix key off nothing drawn changes: the decision runs only with the key on. The series holds 64 staging crops of 1024x1024 (256 MB at 4 bytes a texel) while it runs, and its write at the end stalls the render thread longer than the 512 series did. If a frame's submits ever came after its Present, every crop would read "no P this frame" (the CSV's P_age_frames shows it). The dump's P is the newest find of any key, as in F53 and F59; the patch columns name their own key. `fix.native_on_foot_marker_ref` no longer steers the patch; it is a removal candidate when the arc closes (not removed).

### 2026-10-16: F63 (the held match, the CPU identification, the icon offset's bias; the ADS sight lock and why-lines)

- **Why (F62 flight, log edvr_gfx_20261016_054928, on disk in the Epic edvr_logs).** The patch was accurate when applied (4 to 12 px from P up to 100 deg/s, against 60 to 130 px unpatched) but applied in only 30 to 60% of frames in motion: the read-back match went stale (8 frames) whenever the marker composite's stream was not copied. The cost lines show no slot, buffer-full or lost refusals; every uncopied draw was in a frame without a find in the pool this frame or the last (tags in flight at 25..58 of 90 Unmaps a second in motion, 90 of 90 still). Settings: body_align was OFF in that flight, so F62a and F62b never engaged; a settings issue, not a code bug.
- **Ruled out:** the stream-copy ring or the per-frame staging cap as the cause of the uncopied draws, because the F62 cost lines count 0 no slot, 0 buffer full and 0 lost read-backs in every second.
- **What changed (marker, `fix.native_on_foot_marker_fix` on only).** (1) The match is `drawtag::HeldMatch` (place in the eye, record) held 90 frames from its newest confirmation; every B10B draw at the held place is patched with no read-back that frame; a contradicting read-back or CPU identification (the held place read another record while the key was tagged elsewhere, or another record than the held one) drops it; the both-eyes rule accepts a held match for the other eye. Without a find this frame the patch takes the key's newest P (within 90 frames) and the held record as this frame's pool Unmap wrote it. (2) Staging 8 slots of 2 MB (were 6 of 1 MB; headroom, not the cure). The untagged near-camera composites (five of six B10B draws per eye in F62, at places that move with the marker's, so not identifiable by place) are not copied when the CPU identification names a record that is neither a find nor a held record. (3) **CPU identification, primary:** the marker composite draws' instance stream (one stride-8 vertex buffer) is shadowed at its Unmap, before the real one (per eye 8192 entries about the eye's newest marker composite entry, streaming loads under SEH); at a draw its entry (offset / 8 + StartInstanceLocation) names the record, and a find of that record at the pool's newest Unmap names the key in the same frame. The read-back stays as verification. It depends on the stream being CPU-mapped (WRITE_DISCARD or NO_OVERWRITE); the settlement arc saw a 1,540,096-byte DYNAMIC stream mapped that way, but this flow is not measured: an UpdateSubresource write is counted, not shadowed, and the hold stays the fallback. (4) The patch aims at e less a bias b, the EMA (alpha 0.02, clamp 0.02 NDC) of the read-back residual of fresh patched frames against the target they used (`drawtag::BiasEma`).
- **What changed (ADS, no key; full-3P body mode with the F62b head-aim only).** (5) The ADS head-aim's "aiming down sights but not engaged" line prints whenever the key is on and ADS is true (no longer full 3P only), and names the body key that is off (`full3PWhy`); the weapon fit and the spine bend print the same line in ADS when not engaged. (6) The sight lock: FP joint 14 (FP def_c_povCamera_joint, index 14 per log 054928) joins the FP Animate snapshot (before any drop write); P14w = P14_model x F_root (the whole F_root, no minus d); E_R = cam + halfIpd R^ (R^ the FP root's row 0 made perpendicular to the FP forward and signed to the body's right; halfIpd the right eye's x offset from native_temporal, s->eyes[1][3], else 0.0315 m); e = P14w - E_R less its part along the FP forward, body axes through the AMC rows, seatedFromBody(e, 0); `g_adsSight` through alignFilter (0.02 a frame, 5 cm a frame, 12 cm clamp) while the head-aim weight is above 0 with a fresh snapshot, decaying (about 0.3 s) otherwise; added to the eye alignment. Guard: |e perpendicular| growing 1 cm over 0.5 s (AdsResidualGrowth's pattern, in metres) holds it off until the next ADS engage.
- **What it logs.** Per eye a second (fix on), `marker fix (F63)`: matches by the CPU identification and by a held match, the hold's P/X0 fallback, contradictions at the draw and at read-back, confirmations, the residual of fresh patched frames against P + e (mean, max px) and the bias. `marker fix (F63): CPU identification`: the stream, Unmap copies and their time, faults, other map types, UpdateSubresource writes, draws named (a find, the held record, untagged; copies skipped), no shadow this frame, outside the windows, and the read-back's entry 0 agreeing or not. The per-frame burst names each draw's CPU record. The waypoint CSV adds resid_x_px, resid_y_px (against P + e) and e_used_x_px, e_used_y_px per frame (nan until the read-back lands). `ADS sight lock (F63)` once a second: P14w - cam (body axes), half IPD and its source, e perpendicular after (mean, max) and before (estimate), the applied lock, the weight, the refusals; GUARD TRIPPED and guard cleared lines.
- **Rig.** native_frame_test (242 checks): the hold (90 frames patched with no read-back, held at 90 and not 91, a contradicting read-back drops it, older evidence and another place say nothing, a move); the bias EMA (alpha 0.02, unpatched frames ignored, the closed loop settles on ndc_P + e, the clamp); the stream window; the sight-lock e (level and pitched 30 deg: right, up and seated; the forward part removed), the right axis's sign, the half IPD; the 12 cm clamp; the guard.
- **Not done.** Not flown, not installed. The CPU identification's premise (the stream mapped by the CPU each frame) and the read-back's agreement with it are the flight's first question. The read-back residual compares the patched rows with the rows the decision used, which F50 measured at 0.00 px; if the 0.6 px a frame drift lives in the reference itself, the bias stays near 0 and the CSV will show it. The sight lock needs the FP snapshot (taken while the arm IK is not off, or the bend is on in full 3P); R^ ignores head roll (about 5 mm at 10 deg); the before-lock figure is an estimate. No key added.
