The marker rows take the record's HUD frame (camera axes, origin o_hud; the record's translation is a few metres, e.g. (0.359, -0.528, 2.460)), while P (node+0x50) is a world point: F47's "P through the world rows minus P through the marker rows" has read about 50 deg off in every flight (14:00:22 eye 0: +355 -755 px). At 14:00:22 key 1's "anchor" sat +489.6 -830.8 px from the scene's P against the game's own layout of +127.0 -86.5 (its head-still baseline), so |d| was about (+0.47, -0.91) NDC against the 0.4 gate. The rig passed because its scene and marker rows shared one frame and one origin. **The anchor.** A label's record is laid out in the HUD frame from its anchor v by the designed offset, X0 = v + scale (-off.x, off.y, 0), the scale being the record's own (the indicator lines: 0.940 at z 2.460, 0.933 at 2.440, 0.799 at 2.091: 0.382 z). One projection reproduces the flight's two labels' head-still baselines: key 1 (offset -0.4791 -0.3320) +127.0 -86.5 px and key 3 (-0.2773 +0.1094) +73.5 +28.5 px against the logged +73.52 +28.49 (fitted on key 1, checked on key 3). **Change: the dot's path.** The label's decision runs on v exactly as a plain dot's runs on its record (the waypoint and dot fix, F62c/F64/F66f): the lag and its head-still baseline, the 0.4 gate, the target P through this frame's scene rows (unjittered), the same affine row patch; the only differences are e = 0 (the anchor is a point, not an icon) and v taken from the record. The row patch keeps the record's UI offset from v, so the label's layout rides on its anchor; the read-back measures the record against the record's target. A label without a record scale is left as placed and counted. F94b's own-anchor formula and F93c's measured rule are gone from the hook. No key. **Log:** `marker design offset (F95b)` per eye a second: label draws, moved, refused by condition (no record scale, rows stale, no P, behind, gate with the largest and last |d| in NDC, other: both-eyes, ranged b0, no rows), the anchor at rest against P (a dot's lag at rest: under a pixel when v is right, the layout's error when not), the record scale over its depth (0.382 expected), and over the moved draws the label against its anchor a frame, the anchor's step in the world and the eyes' difference. `--health` rule `marker design offset (F95b)`: NEVER APPLIED when label draws are never moved (naming the commonest refusal and the gate's |d|) or when the game set a visible label for 10 eye-seconds with no draw reaching the decision; PARTIAL when most are refused or the anchor at rest is over 2 px off P. ### 2026-10-24: F95c (the commander's shadow has no head: the head kept in the shadow passes only)
The pilot, flying native on-foot VR (987f898a): "the shadow of the commander shows itself headless". The stock game's flat first person draws the shadow with a head (his screenshot: sun behind, a round head on the shoulders), so the game itself keeps the head out of the view and in the shadow. **How EDVR hides the head today.** `headHideStep` (`src\d3d11\explorer_cam.cpp`, the dither fade's post-call inside the submit job) zeroes the four view masks of the twelve head parts of the local third-person avatar (`sehZeroHeadMasks`). A mask is the set of views an instance is drawn into, so a zero takes the head out of every view, the shadow views included. Nothing in the pose changes and no draw is skipped on the D3D11 side.

**The game's rule (READ, capstone on the 334925 exe; note `analysis\decomp\verify_20261024_f95c_part_class.txt`, filed in the analysis repository as da436af).** The avatar visibility job (0x3DA58A0, the hook F18's P1 already sits on) zeroes every mask, then walks the job context's views (at +0x40, 0x6A0 bytes each, count at +0x1A940) and ORs a view's bit (+0x580) into the mask of each instance whose part admits it. The part's class (entry +0x670, AMC+0x1820 + idx*0x680, the census's `st`) decides: 1 every view, 2 the views whose flags (+0x688) have a bit of 0x7FF0 (the game's own test 0x2856680) and a bit of 0x1030, 3 the views with no bit of 0x7FF0, anything else none. The same switch runs on the avatar's filter (+0x2A8). The class is written only from the avatar's pending requests (0x3D9CA90, 0x3D9D560); the visibility job is its only reader found in the avatar code. In native mode the game already gives one part of this avatar class 2 (EVASuit_Gear_Back, `st=2` in the 13:55:10 census of `edvr_gfx_20261024_135403`); the head parts are class 1. Not traced: which field the stock first person sets (the switch at 0x2A99740 calls avatar slots +0xE0, +0xF0, +0x1C8 and +0x180, and HumanoidModelManager::SetMode reaches +0x1C8; the avatar's vtable was not located), so whether stock first person puts the whole third-person avatar or only its head at class 2 is open. It does not change F95c: both use the same rule.

**Change (no key: the stock game's behaviour).** The P1 hook (`eyeProbeHooked`) calls `explorerCamHeadShadowBegin` before the game's call and `explorerCamHeadShadowEnd` after it. For the local third-person AMC while the head hide writes (a placement, or native stereo's body in the game's first-person camera; F93d's third-person camera writes nothing as before), Begin reads the context's views and swaps each head part's class by compare-exchange (1 to 2, 3 to 0; 0 and 2 unchanged), so the game's own rule puts the head into the shadow views and no main view. End puts the game's class back (a class the game changed during the call stands), counts the head's (instance, view) pairs and leaves a ticket with that call's deny bits (every main and other view's bit). The fade hook then takes the ticket and keeps the head masks less the deny bits (`nofoot::f95c::guarded`; a bit a shadow view shares with an eye is removed) instead of zeroing them. A call the swap did not cover leaves no ticket (Begin also withdraws the avatar's previous one) and the fade hook zeroes as before, so a failure costs the shadow's head, never an eye. Three faults stand F95c down for the session (the head hide itself is unaffected). Pure parts: `src\d3d11\native_on_foot_f95c.h`. **Environment:** game-side, before any draw: every VR runtime, headset and upscaler; build 334925 only (P1's prologue pins); at most 64 views a context (more is not read and zeroes). **Cost:** per game frame, on the local avatar's call only: 12 class reads and at most 12 compare-exchanges each side, up to 64 view reads, 48 mask reads; no extra pass. The shadow passes draw the head's few instances, as the stock game does. The head now self-shadows the visible body and weapon with the sun overhead, as in stock first person.

**Lines.** `native on foot head shadow (F95c) 1 s`: the local avatar's visibility calls, how many ran the head as shadow-only (and parts), views unread, classes the game changed mid-call; the head's (instance, view) pairs after the call in the shadow views (the head drawn into a shadow pass) and in main or other views (removed by the fade hook, 0 expected); the fade hook's keeps (mask words left, words that lost a bit), zeroes and holds. `native on foot head shadow (F95c): the local avatar's visibility call sees N views: main, shadow (the head's), other ...; flags ...` whenever the views' flags change; a stand-down line. `--health` rule `head in the shadows (F95c)`: NEVER APPLIED when no call ran the head as shadow-only, the fade hook never kept one, or no shadow view took the head; PARTIAL for eye-view pairs, zeroes over 5% of the fade hook's writes, or a stand-down; IDLE for the third-person camera only. **Rig:** native_frame_test 839 -> 858 (`f95c_checks.h`, `run95c`: the class mapping and restore; admission over all 131,072 flag values: no class the swap writes reaches a main view, a visible head takes exactly the shadow views; a context shaped like F3's census (eyes bits 1 and 22, shadow views 31, 32, 40, an other view 41): before, every view, through the call, the shadow views, the guard idle; a shadow view carrying the eye's bit: the guard removes it; no shadow view: no view; the fade action). explorer_cam_test passed (the zeroing path unchanged without a ticket); hotkey_capture_test 657; reticle_depth_test 54; openxr_native_test 5281; `edvr_log --health` self-test 154 -> 162. **Build:** full `build.bat --wait-lock`, green, receipt `0c748a305766...`, 414.0 s (test rigs 297.7 s). Not installed, not flown.

**Next flight decides:** first `--health`. Working: the 1 s lines read head as shadow-only equal to the visibility calls, shadow-view pairs above 0 in sunlight, main or other pairs 0, fade hook kept about once a frame and zeroed 0; the views line names the shadow views' flags; the shadow on the ground has a head and helmet, and no head, helmet edge or near-clip sliver shows in either eye on fast head turns. If it never ran: no F95c line at all (a stale DLL or the P1 hook not installed), or 1 s lines with head as shadow-only 0 (views unread or the local avatar never matched) and the fade hook zeroed: the shadow stays headless and `--health` reads NEVER APPLIED. Shadow-only every call with shadow pairs 0 means the sun's views lack 0x1030: the views line's flags then say which bits they carry.

### 2026-10-24: F97b (the label sized like a panel at its anchor facing the eye)
F95 flight (log `edvr_gfx_20261024_152150`, 479d268d, Epic, 1536x1632 marker target): F95b worked ("label draws 4214: moved 4206"); the pilot: "The labels are better, but still change apparent size when yawing my head". **The cause, from the log.** The game scales a label's record by its depth along the game camera's forward axis, not by its distance: in the indicator lines the record scale over its HUD z reads 0.3820-0.3835 from 8.9 to 77.4 deg off the axis (15:26:42 key 3 at 8.9 deg: 0.930 at z 2.433; 15:26:52 at 41.3 deg: 0.691 at z 1.807; 15:27:07 at 77.4 deg: 0.209 at z 0.545), while over its distance it falls from 0.378 to 0.084. Drawn in the camera's plane, that is one NDC size wherever the label sits: key 3's layout offset read +74.7 +24.4 px at 15:26:42 (8.9 deg), +73.1 +27.6 at 15:26:47 (23.7 deg) and +73.2 +31.4 at 15:26:52 (41.3 deg). The flat game's design (a fixed size on the screen); in the headset the projection's NDC per radian grows as sec^2 of the angle along it and sec across it, so the label keeps cos^2 of its width and cos of its height as a head turn carries it off the eye's axis: 0.75 and 0.87 at 30 deg, 0.57 and 0.75 at 41 deg. A panel fixed in the world keeps its angle through a head turn, so (d), nothing wrong, is out. (b) the game's lagging camera: the scale's depth changes by the lag's cosine, under 0.1% a frame; (c) the eyes: F95b's eyes' difference 0.29 px mean. **The plain markers.** Their fix (F62c/F64/F66f) changes no size beyond the marker projection's constant scale sigma, so the dots and waypoints keep the game's fixed NDC size too and shrink the same way off the axis; they are small icons and nothing was changed for them. **Change.** A label is drawn as a panel at its anchor facing the eye, of the angular size the game designs at the centre of its view (its scale over its game depth: 0.382 rad a unit of layout). Its record goes where that panel puts it: from the anchor's direction, the game's designed angles D / z_game (D the layout offset in the HUD frame) along the panel's right and up axes (the eye's x and y made perpendicular to the line of sight). Its layout is mapped about the record by G = Je Jm^-1 / z_game: Jm the marker rows' Jacobian along the HUD's x and y at the record (per metre), Je the scene rows' Jacobian per radian along the panel's axes at the record's direction (`native_on_foot_f97b.h`; `affineRowsG`, the row patch with a 2x2 map). At the view's centre with the eye at the game's camera G is 1/sigma (the game's own unpatched size); at 30 deg about 1.38 across and 1.18 up. The anchor's patch decision (the lag, the 0.4 gate, the target P through the scene rows) is F95b's and gates the move. G is refused (the label drawn as F95b draws it, counted) without a projection, past 2.5x either way or with the record 0.4 NDC or more from the game's layout. No key. **Log:** `label size (F97b)` per eye a second: labels moved, sized, refused (no projection, out of range); by the angle off the eye's axis (0-10, 10-20, 20-30, 30+ deg) the draws, the game's size against the panel's (width, height), as drawn (1 when sized: measured through the patched rows), the record's depth over its distance; the widest angle. `--health` rule `label size (F97b)`: NEVER APPLIED when labels moved and none was sized; PARTIAL for a bin of 20 draws or more 5% off the panel's or most labels unsized; IDLE with no label moved; OK notes when no label was seen 20 deg or more off the axis. If the code never ran: no such line (a stale DLL), or labels moved with sized 0. **Next flight:** `--health`; turn the head with a label in view, 30 deg and more: the game's widths about 0.75 and under at 20-30+, as drawn 1.00; the label keeping its size and its place beside its dot through the turn; F95b's lines as before. **Rig:** native_frame_test 883, 0 failures (877 + 6: the game's label at 0, 15, 30 and 45 deg has cos^2 and cos of the panel's size, its offset alike; drawn through the patched rows, the panel's size within 0.2% and the record's angle from the anchor within 2%; the eye 15 cm over and 9 cm behind the game's camera, the marker rows 1 deg late, sigma 1.0094 and a jitter; G 1/sigma at the centre; the guards and the bins; a record carried too far refused); hotkey_capture_test 657; `edvr_log --health` self-test 181. **Build:** full `build.bat --wait-lock`, green on the first pass, receipt `1e71942941b1...`, 404.2 s. Not installed, not flown.

### F98, 2026-10-24: Explorer Cam torn down
W5 of "What finished means": Explorer Cam, the free-camera on-foot view behind F5, is gone, and native on foot is the on-foot VR mode. Sean approved the inventory and the key list before anything was removed. Main (20db2703, HUD Anti-Aliasing) was merged in first; its one conflict, the menu page list in `tools\gen_settings_schema.py`, kept both sides.

**What native on foot used, and where it went.** `explorer_cam.cpp` held three hooks native on foot depends on: the camera controller's update (+0x2DF3EA0; F93d's camera signal is the mode byte read after the update), the avatar dither fade (+0x3DD8C60; the head hide, F95c's shadow-only ticket, F15's first-person body, F19's clip modifiers, F21's hybrid, the neck census, the pose freeze's, shoulder drop's, arm and leg plans, and F3's avatar census all run in its post-call) and FindJoint (+0xFDEBB0; the local skeleton pair). It also held the fade-global claim for the body, the part-name check and the census lines. They are now `src\d3d11\native_on_foot_hooks.cpp` and `.h`. The pure halves are `avatar_hooks_core.h` (the build identity, the three prologues, the controller's mode byte, the fade guard, the part table, the local-AMC and capture tests, the census text, the callback relay) and `avatar_skeleton_core.h` (the skeleton interface's vtables and slots, the pose walk, the joint names); their namespace is `avh`. The store, pad and skin hooks and their rigs read the identity and the relay from there.

**Deleted.** The free camera, collision, box push, camera UI and zoom/DOF hooks; F5 and its sequencer, the hotkey keeper and the clash check; the head-joint follow and its trims; the isolation of the camera suite; the comfort fade's timeline (`explorer_cam_fade_core.h`) and the settings cache (`explorer_cam_settings_core.h`); the witness line; the menu's Explorer Cam page and the Hotkeys row's session lock; `engineMotionReady` and its motion state in `engine_velocity.cpp` (only the entry fade read it); the `kExplorerCam` view source in `view_source` and the station's centre rule; `tools\explorer_cam_fade_test` and its mutants; `docs\explorer-cam.md`. The comfort fade's channel (`comfort_fade.h`, `fadeAlpha` in the frame output, the runtime's blend) stays: nothing publishes a level now, so it reads 0, and F89's left-eye darkening shares its packing. The seat context keeps its `cameraOpen` bit and writes 0.

**What changes for native on foot.** (1) The hooks' boundary runs first inside native on foot's own tick in `device_hook.cpp`, where Explorer Cam's tick ran: it acts on the want and the body native on foot published the frame before, the same one-frame order as before. (2) The FindJoint and fade gates are open from launch while `fix.native_on_foot` is on. Before, they were open while Explorer Cam was armed, which the shipped F5 made true from launch, and otherwise only while native stereo was on foot; the flown configuration's behaviour is kept. (3) The skeleton reads' build addresses are armed when the hooks are first wanted (`skeleton reads armed (build 334925)`). Before, only Explorer Cam's arming set them, so with `hotkey.explorer_cam` empty the neck census could never verify a skeleton. (4) F33's pov is the head joint itself, always: the rest offset to the povCamera joint was derived only by Explorer Cam's placement (accepted). (5) The controller gate opens only on foot, as it did without Explorer Cam. (6) The hooks' own lines are prefixed `avatar hooks:` and `avatar head hide:` (were `explorer cam:` and `explorer cam head hide:`); no `--health` rule reads them. Every `native on foot` format string is byte-identical: a diff of the string literals of the native on-foot sources and of the moved file, before and after, removes only Explorer Cam's own text, include names and the two prefixes. At an unload the gate byte goes back first, then the fade global, as before; `gate_test` now pins that order and the tick's.

**Keys retired (F98).** `hotkey.explorer_cam` (F5; the key is no longer watched), `fix.explorer_cam_eye_up` (1.68), `_eye_forward` (0.10), `_eye_right` (0.0), `_eye_trim_up` (0.15), `_eye_trim_forward` (-0.08), `_eye_trim_right` (0.0) and `fix.explorer_cam_follow_smoothing_ms` (0): hidden retired lines at those values in `edvr.ini` (the [fix] seven after the F96 block, the hotkey in [hotkey]), and one `native on foot: ... is retired (F98)` note each in `retiredKeysNote` for a value that differs. `config_test` holds them (`kRetiredNotedKeys`) to that block and that function: no other line of the shipped file and no other source spells them.

A yaw or a pitch without roll leaves those axes where they were (the eye's right stays level and its up stays in the vertical plane through the line of sight), so the axes alone are not the cause under yaw and pitch. Two things move the label with the head anyway: (1) head roll turns the eye's axes about the line of sight, so the label orbits its dot and tilts with the head; (2) the eyes are not where the head turns about: they swing on the neck, about 10 cm over and 9 cm ahead of its pivot, and a placement taken from the eye moves with them. ### 2026-10-24: F98a (the twisted left elbow with the rifle: the stable pole transported from its seed; the F94a and F95a rules against F97a's design)
From the F97 flight (`edvr_gfx_20261024_162758`, Epic, build 877a5af8; F97a's armed body INSIDE 0 in every stance): the pilot, "my left elbow being twisted awkwardly with the rifle out if I look up while point my head down"; his idea, keep the spine and pose from changing when looking up. The dumps 163223146001 and 163240792002 show it: the left forearm comes up across the view from below, the elbow raised in front.

**At the dumps.** The game's aim pitch -23.9 deg (the rifle aimed down at the hip, held from 16:32:02 to 16:32:40), the head's LOCAL pitch +7.5 to +12.7 deg (looking up), the view about -15 deg. The left arm (`arm IK (F66d)`): the elbow's plane 90-97 deg from the stance's own (the twist about the upper arm the shortest-arc swing would have missed), flexion 52 deg animated against 103 solved, the hand's twist |raw| 97-102 deg with the forearm helpers at their +-90 limit in every call.

**The causes enumerated, with what told them apart.** (a) The chest following the game's aim pitch, the arm wrapping round it: the spine bend's pitch applied was 0.0 deg in every second, and the aim held at -23.9 while the elbow went back and forth between 1-23 deg (16:32:10-12, 16:32:28) and 89-97 deg off the plane: ruled out as the trigger (above). (b) The elbow's pole: the swivel sat 89-97 deg off the plane for 5-30 s at a time with the pose still, and came back only when F84's body-down pole took the swivel (the F82 laser-rifle protection with yaw 0: the plane's median 10.2 deg over 121 s; with F82's yaw over 1 deg or F82 off, 63.7 and 31.7 deg). The stable pole (F76) committed each frame's transported reference as the next frame's seed (and re-projected it onto the arm as written), so its reference turned by the solid angle of every loop the shoulder-to-hand axis went round: the aim's pitch, the pin moving the body with the head's pitch (the rest offset turns with it, 4 cm forward looking 15 deg up), F82's torso yaw (up to 16 deg). A static pose after such loops keeps an elbow at an arbitrary swivel. (c) F69a's upright target or F97a's raise against the game's aim pose: F93 raised the rifle by the same rule and was never over 45 deg (0 of 112 rifle seconds, aim near level); ruled out alone. (d) The left hand's target: 3.93 cm hand-to-grip in both states; ruled out. The cause is (b), brought out by (a)'s geometry: with the aim 24 deg down the arm's axis is far from where the pole was seeded and a loop turns the reference a long way.

**The fix.** The stable pole keeps its seed: the axis and reference of the frame it was seeded on (the item's first armed solve, as before) stay in the committed pole, the reference is transported from the seed to the arm's axis now in one rotation (ikStableSwivel's own transport), and only the previous radial (its fallback) follows the arm as written. The swivel then depends on where the arm is, not on how it got there. The pistol's body-down pole and F84's rifle support, which already take the body's down each frame, are unchanged; so is everything else in the solve (the constraints, the hinge swings, F82). No key, no threshold.

**Lines.** `native on foot left elbow (F98a) 1 s` with a weapon drawn, for the held item: the game's aim pitch (mean, min, max), the chest's lean (chest 24 to neck 34, forward) as written and as animated, F82's torso yaw, the elbow's swivel from the stance's plane (mean, max, calls over 45 deg), its step a frame (the angle between consecutive solved radials about the arm's axis: rms, max, steps over 10 deg), where the swivel came from (the seed's pole with the arm's angle from the seed's axis, a body-down pole, the legacy swivel), and the hand twist at the forearm's limit. `--health` rule `left elbow (F98a)`: PARTIAL when the elbow is over 45 deg off the plane in most of a second or a step is over 10 deg. Two rules read F97a's design: `neck height (F94a)` now judges the body's height and legs on unarmed seconds only (armed, F97a raises or lowers the body by design and `armed body (F97a)` judges it; the F97 flight read PARTIAL on the rifle's and pistol's raise), and `view motion (F95a)` reads the HUD against the eye on the median second as it does the view (the F97 flight's pooled 0.73 mm standing came from a few seconds, the largest 10.1 mm rms, beside a median of 0.19 mm, with no bob reported; the hold's own millimetre steps move the eye against the HUD by at most 0.44 mm a frame).

**Rig.** native_frame_test 894 -> 897 (`f98_checks.h`, `run98`): the arm's axis round a 40 deg cone and back, the pole from its seed returns to its reference exactly and moves under 6 deg a step, the frame-to-frame carry (F76-F97, the control) comes back turned about 84 deg (the cone's solid angle). `edvr_log --health` self-test 188 -> 193 (the F98a rule's three cases, an armed raise under F94a's rule, the HUD's one bad second). hotkey_capture_test 657, reticle_depth_test 54, openxr_native_test 5281.

### 2026-10-24: F98c revised (armed, the eye where it stands unarmed in the same stance; the marker fix on by default)

The eye height over the armed stance's neck is not that: the weapon stances lean the neck 12-25 cm under the upright one, so it would have brought the armed view down 12-18 cm (ruled out above).

**Measured (the F97 flight, standing, the head level, the model's heights):** the upright unarmed neck 1.543 m; the game's camera fists 1.625 m, rifle 1.559 m, pistol 1.573 m. **The rule.** Unarmed (no weapon or tool, F88's weight 0) each settled stance (F95a's window) stores its animated neck and the game's camera by class, standing or crouched (the pin's crouch weight against its standing calibration, else against the stored standing camera). Moving, the raise holds the last settled stance's, as unarmed. Crouched with no unarmed crouch stored, the standing unarmed raise over the crouched camera; with nothing stored (on foot with an item from the start), a starting raise that puts the upright neck 8 cm under the camera. F97a's upright raise, its guard that keeps the eye out of the torso, no target in the sights and the retired up key stay as in b1658763. ### 2026-10-24: F99a (a drawn item's hands from the game's own selection, not from Status.json)
The pilot, after the F98 flight (`edvr_gfx_20261024_192353`, ae6539ae, Epic): "when drawing a tool while moving, the tool would appear and then the hand would attach to it noticeably afterwards, can we tighten this?"

**The hands' authority.** The arm solve's weight is the armed flag's 0.3 s ramp (F66a, `ikArmedSolveWeight`). The flag came from Status.json's SelectedWeapon, or for a primary from F83's native selection. A tool or the pistol is not a primary (`F83 primary draw: ... primary=0 eligible=0`), so its hands waited for Status.json.

**The log.** The game's own selection (the F83 line, read in the look update each frame) against Status.json (the `armed (F66a)` line), draws from the fists: companalyser 19:27:01.132 / 01.818 (686 ms, running), repair tool 19:27:09.377 / 09.809 (432 ms, running), recharge tool 19:27:35.705 / 36.057 (352 ms, standing and walking), recharge tool 19:29:35.314 / 35.602 (288 ms, running). Swaps lag longer (0.52-1.39 s) but the hands are already armed through them. The FP hand began the draw about 50 ms after the game's selection (F68d's onset window for the companalyser: the attach 21 -> 69 cm from rest at -0.64..-0.57 s against Status.json, 79 cm, the tool at its place, by -0.18 s). The hand followed Status.json: `grip onset (F74)` "right hand, anatomical palm target written 0 ms after Status item change; armed weight 0.04", then "reached full armed envelope 1.00 at 297 ms". So the hand reached the tool 0.58-0.98 s after the game selected it. The rifle's hand was on the rifle before Status.json named it (19:26:18.679 written, Status.json 19:26:19.601). Moving made it show: standing, the game's own 3P draw kept the hands near the FP hands while they waited (the distance gate held 74 of 77 unarmed frames in the second of the 19:27:35 draw); running, the locomotion kept them away (13 of about 62, 34 of 57, 30 of 45). The other candidates are ruled out above.

**The fix.** `nofoot::f99::Bridge` (native_on_foot_f99.h), on the frame thread: a new selection of an item that is not a primary (`held`: not the holster, not 0xFFFFFFFF; F83's state publishes it), made by the game while Status.json names none, arms the hands at once. The bridge holds until Status.json names an item (the flag is then Status.json's, as before), the game puts the item away, or 2 s pass (released through the same 0.3 s ramp). The first selection read after the scope opens is not a draw, nor is a swap or the same selection read again. The draw's identity starts with the game's selection: the held item serial moves at the bridge's start and not again when Status.json names the item (only the item's profile changes then), so the off hand's acquisition and the elbow's stable pole are not reset under a hand already on the tool. A primary keeps F83's path. No key: it always helps.

**The instrument.** One line per draw, `native on foot draw onset (F99a)`: the game's selection's id, the body moving or still, and from the selection when Status.json named the item, where the hands' authority came from and when, and when the armed ramp was full, with the bridge's counts. It reads the selection itself, apart from the bridge, so a build whose bridge never armed the hands reads "the hands' authority from Status.json" at the game's lead. `--health` rule `draw onset (F99a)`: NEVER APPLIED when every draw the game selected 100 ms or more ahead of Status.json waited for Status.json, PARTIAL when some did.

**Rig.** native_frame_test 904 -> 911 (run99): the first selection not a draw; a draw armed at once and held until Status.json names it; released unnamed after 2 s and at once when put away; no bridge on a swap, a repeated read or a reopened scope; the flight's four leads at full weight 0.30 s after the selection against lead plus 0.30 s without; the record from the selection, and its control reading Status.json's authority. `edvr_log --health` self-test +3 cases.

**Build.** Full `build.bat --wait-lock` green on the first pass, receipt `4a7fe53fb4c0...`, 345.1 s. Not installed, not flown. **For the flight:** each tool and the pistol drawn from the fists running and standing: `draw onset (F99a)` with the hands from the game's selection at +0 ms and the ramp full near +300 ms; the repair tool's left hand staying on when Status.json names it; swaps and the rifle as before.

Y ms a frame`; it reads `tee clock: none` when no call was clocked. `--health` rule `marker tee (F100)`. ### 2026-10-24: F101 (three review findings: the version 1 input size, reticle follow game in the render path, render_locked after VR to flat)
An outside review of the branch at 50656377 found three bugs; each was confirmed against the code before the fix.

**1. The version 1 frame input size (since F31, 90b397bf).** `EDVR_NATIVE_FRAME_INPUT_SIZE_1` was `offsetof(EdvrNativeFrameInput, nowHead)`, 84 on x64. The version 1 struct ends at `valid` after uint64_t members, so its sizeof is 88, and the released provider (v0.21.1, main) requires exactly that. This branch's runtime sent 84 below version 7 (a released d3d11.dll refused every step) and its provider took 84, the version 2 size or the full struct (a released openvr_api.dll's 88 was refused). Fix: `EDVR_NATIVE_FRAME_INPUT_PADDED(words)` rounds a version's words up to the struct's alignment, as sizeof does; SIZE_1 is 88, SIZE_2 664 (ringCount already ends on an 8-byte boundary, unchanged). The provider also takes `EDVR_NATIVE_FRAME_INPUT_WORDS_1` (84), what this branch's runtimes sent from F31 to F100, and reads no version 1 input past `valid`. The runtime's ladder shapes moved into `native_frame.h` (`nativeFrameAsk`, `nativeFrameInputShape`) so the provider's rig drives the client's own. Audit of the other size macros: output versions 1 to 6 are four-byte members only, so every prefix is its version's sizeof, and 1 to 5 equal v0.21.1's (128, 140, 144, 148, 152); the request, table and decision structs are unchanged since v0.21.1. Branch-only history, not changed: an F31-F36 runtime's version 2 input (144 bytes, before F37's ring) and an F33-F39 runtime's version 8 output (180 bytes, before nowPoseRender) are refused and step down cleanly.

**2. Reticle follow game in the render path.** `game` promised that EDVR writes nothing to key 10 (F21), and the instance hook honoured it, but `fixDecide` still put key 10's P at F85c's hit depth and corrected the draw. Now a key 10 draw with the mode at game leaves `fixDecide` once its key is matched (`nofoot::f85::renderTakesKey`), before any decision is counted; the key's hold is kept, so a live switch back to aim or head finds it matched. No F86 dispatch is made for key 10 then; the other consumers dispatch their own after three frames, as when no reticle is drawn. The F85c line reads `reticle depth (F85c): the reticle is the game's (...): key 10 draws N left as the game placed them` each second key 10 was drawn (every 5 s on foot otherwise), and `--health` reads it as IDLE ("the reticle is the game's"), a weapon drawn or not.

**3. render_locked after a live VR to flat switch.** `publishFlatHead` reused `publishPoseCache`, which under render_locked skipped the `now` locate and published the latch: with the last VR frame's latch known a flat call was answered with that frozen pose, without it the publication was withdrawn and every flat call hopped behind the headset frames. Now a flat frame clears the latch and always locates `now` and `next` (`publishPoseCache(true)`); the latch answer in `locateHeadFor` is VR only; and `poseTargetFor`'s now-pose rule (render and render_locked) is VR only too, so the flat hop locates at the empty frame's display time, where the `now` slot is. The two other render_locked sites are in `waitPoses` (the game pose at line 1540, the publication at 1709): VR frames only, no flat leak.

**Rigs.** native_frame_test 911 -> 918 (`f101_checks.h`, run101, and a provider block): the v0.21.1 input and output structs frozen with static_asserts on their sizes and every shared offset; this runtime's ladder against the released provider's shape checks settles at 5 with 88-byte input, and with F31-F100's 84 every step is refused (the control); the released asks equal this build's for 1 to 5; through the real provider, a released runtime's 88-byte input with each of its asks 5 to 1 is answered in its own shape and nothing past it, 84 is taken, 80 and 96 are refused, and this runtime's steps 10 to 1 are each answered as asked; reticle follow game takes no key 10 draw and every other key. openxr_native_test 5281 -> 5288 (`flat_head_cache_cases.h`): in VR the latch answers (control); after the switch with render_locked set the flat call is answered from the `now` slot, not the latch, also with no latch known, and the stale hop locates at the empty frame's display time. `edvr_log --health` self-test +3 cases.

**Build.** Full `build.bat --wait-lock` green on the first pass, receipt `fea016dc72bd...`, 423.4 s. Not installed, not flown. **For a flight:** nothing new to look for on foot unless reticle follow is set to game (the F85c line then says so); a mixed pair (this openvr_api.dll with a v0.21.1 d3d11.dll, or the reverse) negotiates version 5.

### 2026-10-24: F103 (a hunched unarmed stance is not the standing reference)
The pilot, after the d60c26f0 flight (`edvr_gfx_20261024_220128`, Epic): "When I got into combat, my commander pose changed and suddenly my weapons/tools were above my head (or rather my head had been forced down)." Eye dumps 221302590005 and 221311389006 (22:13:02 and 22:13:11, the rifle drawn, the room in red alarm light) show the eye low among the shoulders with the rifle high on the right.

**The log.** Until 22:12:32 the fists stood upright: the animated neck 1.542 m, the head joint 1.665-1.688 m, the game's camera 2.8 cm over the neck (`neck height (F94a)` 22:12:31: "animated neck 1.542 m ... the game's camera over it +2.8 cm"). At 22:12:33 the fists' stance changed: the neck fell to 1.304-1.310 m and the head joint to 1.37-1.44 m, while the game's camera stayed (22:12:34: "animated neck 1.306 m (min 1.304 max 1.308) ... the game's camera over it +27.0 cm"). Settled and not crouched by the camera, F98c stored it as the standing unarmed neck (`eye level (F98c)` 22:12:34: "ueye 1.455 m ... the unarmed neck stored: standing 1.307 m", against 1.542 m a second before). From then the unarmed view stood 23.5 cm low (1.455 m against 1.692) and, with the rifle drawn at 22:13:00, the armed view too ("aeye 1.458 m ... standing 1.308 m"). The game places the weapons from its own camera, so they stood over the eye. The flight's `--health`: "the unarmed eye 1.688 m; the armed eye 1.602 m; the unarmed standing neck stored 1.310 m". The fists' "INSIDE 7" (22:12:41, moving) and the lowering in the holster seconds follow from the low eye. The game's state is not in the log (the session wrote no journal events; Status.json has no combat flag); the red alarm light in the dumps suggests the settlement's alert. The other candidates are ruled out above.

**The fix.** A standing stance is upright when its head joint is at a standing commander's height: the pin's own standing gate (F68e's calibration band, 1.50-1.90 m; `pinHeadUpright`). An unarmed standing stance whose head joint is under it is hunched: it stores nothing and its target is the stored upright eye, as an armed stance's is (`nofoot::f94::EyeLevel`, source `kEyeHunched`; with nothing stored, the starting raise). A crouch is stored as before, whatever its head's height. A head joint not read counts as upright. No key.

**The instrument.** `eye level (F98c)` counts the hunched stances ("unarmed N (the stance not known N, hunched N)"). The rule reads PARTIAL when the stored standing neck moves 10 cm or more from one second to the next: this flight's log reads "the stored standing neck jumped (1.543 -> 1.307 m): a hunched stance stored as the upright one". A fixed build shows "hunched" counted through the combat stance and the stored neck kept.

**Rig.** native_frame_test 928 -> 931: the flight's combat stance and the rifle after it, with F103 the view at the upright eye through both and the upright neck kept; the control (the d60c26f0 build) 23.6 cm down unarmed and armed; a hunched stance with nothing stored takes the starting raise and stores nothing, a crouch is stored whatever the head's height. `edvr_log --health` self-test +2 cases. Full `build.bat --wait-lock` green (the second pass; the first failed a rig tolerance on the stored neck, which is the settle window's mean), receipt `1c74527f8177...`, 237.5 s. Not installed, not flown. **For the flight:** into combat with the fists, then each weapon and tool: `eye level (F98c)` with hunched counted, the eye near 1.69 m unarmed and armed, no jump of the stored neck. Open: the 3P body still takes the game's combat pose under the upright eye (F97a's raise is for an item drawn only).

Its per-draw record is start instance 1504 (eye 0) and 4836 (eye 1), next to the panel's 1505 and 4837 in the same t1 and t6 buffers. A pointer controller's update (0x454F520) stores the mouse position in NDC at +0x84/+0x88 and turns it into a direction (0x456EEE0): it copies the game camera's state, replaces the pose with a canonical one at the origin (translation 0), unprojects (x, -y) through the camera's own projection and stores the normalised direction at +0xB0. Placing the pointer on a panel (0x4559C50) takes one of two modes, chosen by a mode object at +0x188: a ray from the origin along +0xB0 hit against the panel's triangles (panel vtable +0x178, then the ray-plane test 0x5E8820, which rejects t < 0 and t past FLT_MAX), or a 2D mode, the NDC mapped to 0..1 and through the panel's cursor window (FUN_144541A20, panel vtable +0x198) to a uv and then to a 3D point (+0x188). The panel comes into the camera's frame from its world transform (+0x740 to +0x77F) minus the camera position, through the camera's rows. The hit triangles come from the mesh owner's transform (vtable +0x10), which was not followed.

### 2026-10-24: F105 (a terminal's interface ghosting while its menus change)
**The report.** Flight `edvr_gfx_20261024_220128` (Epic, d60c26f0, Virtual Desktop OpenXR on a Quest 3, 90 Hz, 1536x1632 render, 3072x3264 output, DLSS preset K): "On a terminal, the UI is ghosting while cycling through the menus, took an eye dump." Of the six dumps only 221109514003 (22:11:09) is the terminal (the settlement's Facilities screen, the "BUILDINGS EXTERIOR" tooltip up); 220853512001 is the inventory transfer panel, the other four corridors.

**How a terminal is drawn.** Not a composite into the eye and not the canvas route of the flat maps (b17cb2dd is flat only): the game draws the screen in its G-buffer pass as a lit surface whose EMISSIVE term is the interface, VS 889A5279E68F0672 / PS EBA95E15B0A66102 (four colour targets; the interface sampled from a texture array at t2, the slice from the instance record; disassembled from the shader dump, 3616 bytes). So it is in DLSS's input. The UI layer cannot take a surface; ui depth classified it as a composite and had no stand-in (22:04:38 `ui depth: a new interface family -- vs 889A5279E68F0672 ps EBA95E15B0A66102 draws into 1536x1632 DXGI format 23: samples a learned surface but has no depth shader of its own yet ... left alone -- this composite still swims`); the layer's census named it every window (22:11:28: `vs 889A5279E68F0672 ps EBA95E15B0A66102 (no family) 4.00 a frame`). F100's marker tee and the marker fix handle the marker composite (VS B10B032BDFD46700), not this pair; the dump's marker counts are null.

**The causes and their signatures, checked on the dump.**
1. The interface in DLSS's input with nothing holding it to the current frame. Signature: the coverage mask empty over the screen and the resolve idle. CONFIRMED: `UI.bin` 0 of 2,506,752 pixels, `UiPrevious.bin` all zero, decision flag 64 clear on every screen pixel; the raw input (C00..C15) shows the tooltip crisp in all 16 frames while DLSS's output (T, P and the final crops) shows it dim, striped and doubled; 0.4 to 0.94% of the screen's output pixels lie outside the raw 2x2 range by more than 8/255 (frame 0 highest), against 0.04% on the terminal's body beside it. The UI resolve (ui_resolve.h) is EDVR's answer to interface text in DLSS's input under the transformer presets, which ignore the bias mask; it acts only where the coverage mask is marked.
2. Wrong motion on the screen. Signature: the content's shift between raw frames against -MV plus the jitter step. REFUTED: over 15 frame pairs the residual is 0.23 px at most (median under 0.1), on the menu text and on the terminal's body alike; the screen takes the engine-record path (11) like its surroundings.
3. The game's own menu transition. Signature: two menus blended in the raw frames. Not seen: the content does not change in the 16 frames. It cannot explain the doubling in a still frame, which is DLSS's alone (the raw frame is crisp).
4. Virtual Desktop's frame synthesis (the game at 61 to 77 fps under 90 Hz). Signature: EDVR's submitted frames clean. Not the cause of the dumped artifact: the final crops, which are what EDVR submits, already carry it.

Replayed offline on the dump: the resolve's clamp alone changes 1 to 2% of the tooltip's pixels and leaves the striping; its rebuild (Catmull-Rom of the raw frame at the unjittered position, bounded by the raw 2x2) gives solid single text in every frame.

**The fix (`src\d3d11\world_screen_coverage.h`, ui_depth.cpp, vscreen.cpp).** Right after the game's draw of the pair, with a learned surface bound, in the scene's depth and with an external upscaler running, the draw is issued once more through a stand-in pixel shader (`kWorldScreenCoverageHlsl`, the game shader's input signature element for element) into the eye's coverage mask (2: an attached stroke, so the engine-record motion stays the pixel's) and its edit mask (1), against the game's own depth with GREATER_EQUAL and no writes. The eye comes from the scene depth bound, as the planets' does (the G-buffer's colour target must not join the eye-target table). No game target is written; the game's depth is only read; every binding is put back. The UI resolve then holds the screen to the current frame and rebuilds it from the current frame wherever DLSS departs from it by more than its tolerance (12/255). No key. Limits: the masks are marked in the G-buffer pass, so a hand or weapon later drawn over a screen is treated as the screen where it covers it; EDVR's own temporal AA is untouched; the layer's census still lists the pair as left in the scene (it is, by design), so `--ui-composites` reads it as before.

**Health.** `ui depth world screens (F105): N frames, seen S, marked M (eye 0 a, eye 1 b); refused: no eye, no mask, no shader, state` every ui depth window (1800 frames) while an external upscaler runs, zeros included, and a once-only note at the first mark. `--health` rule `world screens (F105)`: no line is the code never having run; seen 0 IDLE; seen and none marked NEVER APPLIED (the refusals named); under 90% marked or one eye only PARTIAL. Five self-test cases, rendered from the C formats.

**Rig.** ui_depth_test: the classifier, the line, the stand-in's input signature against PS EBA95E15B0A66102's, and on WARP the second issue marking exactly where the screen won the depth test (an occluder nearer excluded), no game target or depth written, every binding back, and a refusal with an unordered-access view bound or no depth target that changes nothing; 32545 checks.

**Build.** Full `build.bat --wait-lock` green, receipt `241eb6920476...`, 197.5 s (an earlier run stopped at the retired-key scan for a comment that spelled the rig's directory name). Not installed, not flown.

### 2026-10-25: F106 (ADS: the sight in both eyes)
**Why.** F89 closed the left eye while the sights were up, so that the right eye, the one the sight lock lines up (F70), saw the sights alone. Testers report eye strain from the closed eye. F106 replaces the close: while the sights are up the left eye shows the right eye's image, turned into the left eye's view, so both eyes see the scene from the aiming eye, the sight is centred in both, and nothing goes dark. Depth flattens while aiming (both eyes see one image), as it does through a real scope.

**The mapping (`src\openxr\eye_share.h`; the shader `kStereoShareHlsl` in `stereo_shader_source.h` computes the same in float).** For each left swapchain pixel centre: the direction (lerp(tan left, tan right, u), lerp(tan up, tan down, v), -1) in the left view, from `views[0].fov`; turned by inverse(q_right) * q_left (`views[i].pose.orientation`, both in the layer's space) into the right view; projected with `views[1].fov` to the right swapchain image's u, v; then through the eye-1 blit's own mapping (its viewport `viewports[1]` within that image, then the capture's bounds and clamp, `constants[1]`) to the texel of the right eye's capture. Rotation only: no position enters. These are the views the projection layer submits, so the mapping holds on canted displays (the Pimax Crystal Super cants each view about 10.75 deg, and the views carry it) and with asymmetric fovs (Quest 3).

**Coverage.** A left pixel keeps its own image where the right eye drew nothing for its direction: behind the right view, outside its fov, outside its placement (a trimmed viewport), or inside its hidden-area mesh. The share fades in over 3 deg from the edge of the right eye's drawn rectangle (by axis angle, starting 0.25 deg inside it). The hidden area is the runtime's visibility mask for the right view (the mesh the game's hidden-area mesh is made from), rasterised once a mesh into a 256 x 256 mask over the right fov: every texel a triangle touches is hidden, then a zero band of two mask texels and two right-eye pixels, then a 3 deg ramp, so a masked corner of the right image reaches the left eye neither through the mask's filtering nor through the image's. Under a fov trim the runtime withholds the mesh from the game, which then draws those corners; the share still keeps out of them.

**Where it is drawn (`src\openxr\d3d11_stereo.cpp`).** In the left eye's scene pass, right after the left eye's own blit: one triangle over the left eye's viewport, the blit's vertex shader with the share pixel shader, rgb blended by a = share x coverage (source a + destination (1 - a)), the left image's alpha kept; a pixel with a = 0 is discarded. The comfort fade and the plugins' overlay apply over it afterwards, as over any image. The source is `srvs[1]`, the right eye's capture. It is complete before `renderCaptured` is called (both eyes are captured, and a separate graphics device's transfer is completed at the top of `compose`) and nothing writes it during the call (the passes write only the swapchain images); it holds the scene, the HUD and EDVR's menu, which is drawn into the eye texture before the capture. On a replayed pair the share is this frame's level, mapped with the pair's own views. Share 0 draws nothing more: the image is bit for bit today's. Cost: one more full-viewport draw on the left eye while the share is above 0. F89's darken pass is removed.

**Layer.** Unchanged: each eye's own pose and fov. Moving the left view's position to the right eye's would let a compositor's positional reprojection undo the shared viewpoint. No depth layer is submitted (the runtime has no XR_KHR_composition_layer_depth path), so no left-eye depth disagrees with the shared image.

**The interface.** The share crosses as F89's darkening did, in the version 10 answer's word (`EdvrNativeFrameOutput::reservedProjectionChannel`, renamed `leftEyeShare`; offset, size and type unchanged; the signal header `left_eye_share.h`, renamed from `left_eye_darken.h`). An F89 to F105 d3d11.dll sends its darkening there with the same timing, and this runtime draws it as the share. This d3d11.dll with an F89 to F105 runtime gets the old close. The way back is new: once a press, when the share returns to 0, the runtime fills an `EdvrNativeEyeShareReport` and calls the d3d11.dll export `edvrNoteNativeEyeShare`, which writes the press line. A d3d11.dll without the export is not told; the runtime log's `eye_share_press` line has the same figures.

**Key.** `fix.native_on_foot_ads_sight_both_eyes` (on | off, default on, live), on the Native on foot page as "ADS: sight in both eyes", where "ADS: close left eye" was. The same conditions and timing as F89's close (`nofoot::f106::share`, `native_on_foot_f106.h`): the ADS lock's weight (0.15 s in, 0.3 s out) with the key on, in native on foot with a weapon or tool drawn (the full third-person body); the guard logs a weight above 0 off foot or unarmed. The close's key is retired as F100 retired the training connect probe: a hidden retired line in the shipped `edvr.ini` at its last value (on), a once-only note in `retiredKeysNote` for a value that differs, and config_test's retired-key scan.

**Lines.** At the first read and at each change: `native on foot ADS sight in both eyes (F106): fix.native_on_foot_ads_sight_both_eyes is on|off -- ...`. At each edge `ADS sight in both eyes (F106): shared|stereo (key, lock weight)`, once a second in ADS `ADS sight in both eyes (F106) 1 s: share ...`, and `... GUARD TRIPPED ...`. Once a press, from the runtime: `ADS sight in both eyes (F106) press: peak, frames (at full weight, refused, replayed) over s; the eyes' rotation (left view against the right) yaw pitch roll deg; tangents left L/R/U/D, right L/R/U/D; the left eye from the right at full weight N% (wholly M%); hidden area used|none (T triangles)`. The coverage is computed on the CPU from the same mapping, with the mask, on a 48 x 48 grid over the left eye's placement at the press's first frame. The runtime log: `left_eye_share,level,state=shared|stereo,path=left_scene_pass` (edges, and once a second while shared) and `eye_share_press,...` (the press line's figures and `told_graphics=yes|no_export|refused`).

**Health.** `--health` rule `ADS sight in both eyes (F106)`, in place of `ads close left eye (F89)` (`ads transition (F89)` stays): OK when a press reached full weight with 30 to 100% of the left eye taken; NEVER APPLIED when a share was asked for (the 1 s lines, key on) or an F89 trace press came with the key on and no press line came back (the share never ran; a runtime from before F106 darkens instead); IDLE with the key off or no ADS; PARTIAL for presses that never reached full weight, an implausible coverage, refused frames or a guard trip.

**Rigs.** openxr_stereo_test (`share_cases.h`; WARP, 128 px eyes, both submission paths, sRGB and UNORM swapchains): (a) parallel symmetric eyes: the left pixel looking straight ahead samples the right image's straight-ahead texel; (b) displays canted 10.75 deg each way with asymmetric fovs: every left pixel inside the coverage shows the texel the rig's own quaternion arithmetic gives for its direction, the world's straight ahead is the same texel in both eyes, and the renderer reports yaw +21.5, no pitch or roll; (c) the left pixels outside the right fov keep the left image bit for bit, and the band rises monotonically over about 3 deg; (d) share 0, -0, -1 and NaN are bit for bit the render without a share, with the same shader work, and a share above 0 adds one triangle; (e) share 1 inside the coverage is the right eye's own pixel, bit for bit; (f) with a hidden area over two corners whose texels are red in the right capture, no left pixel carries red or turns black, and the control with no mesh does show the red. Also: the right eye and the layer's views unchanged, a trimmed placement's border black, the CPU coverage within 0.03 of what the GPU drew, the pure mapping and mask on their own, and the shader's embedded bytes against a compile made at test time. temporal_shader_build: the fifth stereo shader and its bindings (192-byte constants at b0, the right eye at t0, the mask at t1, the sampler at s0). native_frame_test: the share's decision and timing, its signal and the report's validation. openxr_native_test: the word rides a version 10 answer only. edvr_log.py: the rule's OK, NEVER APPLIED (both ways), IDLE and PARTIAL cases.

**A flight must show.** In ADS with the rifle and the pistol: the sight centred in both eyes, no dark eye, no strain; at the far left of the view, which the left eye sees alone, its own image with no seam. `--health` first: `ADS sight in both eyes (F106)` OK; the press lines with yaw about +21.5 deg on the Pimax (about 0 on the Quest 3), tangents matching the runtime log's views, coverage between 30 and 100%, hidden area used. 1 s lines with a share and no press line mean the share never ran.

**Build.** Full `build.bat --wait-lock` green, receipt `ce4a59843f1b...`, 278.3 s; openxr_stereo_test 25721 checks, native_frame_test 932, openxr_native_test 5288, all passing. The first run's stereo rig caught the coverage figure kept from a trimmed placement within a press; it is now computed again whenever the rotation, a fov, a placement or the mask changes. Not installed, not flown.

### 2026-10-25: F108 (a terminal held only while its content changes)
**The report.** F105 flew in 1c26ea5f (log `edvr_gfx_20261025_044101`, Epic, Pimax Crystal Super over Pimax OpenXR, 90 Hz, 2016x2017 render, 4032x4034 output, DLSS preset K): `world screens (F105)` OK, 63345 of 63345 screen draws marked (eye 0 31480, eye 1 31865). The pilot: the ghosting is gone, but "The Terminal UI looks low res/no AA or upscaling from a distance? ... the UI itself also appears low res, but doesn't smear."

**The dumps.** 045208629001 (04:52:08) is the terminal, seen from a distance: its screen covers 355x204 render pixels (about 710x408 output), 68,621 pixels marked 2 in `UI.bin` and 255 in `UiEdits.bin`. 050027052003 is a close screen of another kind (`UI.bin` all zero: not this pair; DLSS shows it clean). 050016692002 is the carrier's menu.

**The causes, on 045208629001.**
1. The rebuild sets the resolution. CONFIRMED. Over the whole screen the resolve changes 1-2% of the output pixels (flat and dark, where DLSS already matches the raw frame), but on the interface's detail pixels (a raw 2x2 range over 16/255: 3,150-8,860 a frame) it replaced DLSS's output at 52% (frame 0) and 70-75% (frames 1-15); the result equals the Catmull-Rom of the raw frame at 60-74% of them, where DLSS's own output agreed with it at 2-12% (mean difference 15-24/255). The crop: DLSS before the resolve reads "PHAEACIA / MILITARY" cleanly; the raw frame and the final eye both show broken strokes and an unreadable "MILITARY". The clamp alone would change 5-13% of those pixels by about 1/255: the edit mark, every pixel every frame, is the loss.
2. Aliasing at a distance. CONFIRMED as the mechanism: the raw strokes drop out and change frame to frame (the texture is finer than the render samples it); the word's stroke light varies 7.9% rms frame to frame in the raw frame, 4.2% in DLSS's output and 9.6% in the final eye. DLSS integrated the aliasing over the jitter; the rebuild passed it through.
3. The texture sets the resolution. REFUTED at this distance: DLSS reconstructs the text legibly from the same frames. The texture's size, slices and mips were in neither the dump nor the log (F108's line now names them).
4. fix.ui_quality's panel sizing. Active (`ui_quality = 100` in the Epic ini; `ui quality: panels: the engine sizes panels x2.0000`), whether it sizes terminal screens not established; moot, the texture is not the limit.
5. Aside: at 04:59:55 a draw of the pair still logged `left alone` (on the carrier): it failed one of F105's tests, which one unlogged then; F108 counts and names them.

**The history restart, and preset K.** EDVR invalidates NVIDIA's history by writing the motion vector `size*2` (`backgroundHistoryHidden`, the engine-masked pixels; the shader's own comment: "modern presets honour only this"). The evidence that preset K honours it: `docs\terrain-history-shimmer-2026-09-17.md` (preset K, Pimax): `backgroundHistoryHidden` marked 1.81% of the eye, those pixels' DLSS output changed 1.98/255 a frame against 0.62 on the rest of the terrain (history restarted every frame), and removing the marks (the census then 0.000%) ended the shimmer, confirmed by Sean and by the dump's census. That is a measured effect of the value under K, not a measurement on a terminal; the next flight's dump after a menu change is that measurement.

**The change.** (1) UiContent takes a Texture2DArray view (`prepareArray`, `kUiContentArrayCs`; `kUiContentCs` and the 2D path unchanged): the view's slices from mip 0, a digest and two ages per 4x4 block per slice, its own entries under the shared 64 MiB. (2) The tracked stand-in (`kWorldScreenTrackedHlsl`) reads the game shader's own lookup from bindings still bound at the second issue: t1's record (stride 96) at the face-invariant's y, word 4 the slice and bit 31 a solid colour (no edit); the uv the texcoord times cb2[1].xy plus cb2[1].zw; the slice's ages at t14, the 2x2 blocks about the uv. It writes the edit (the age) only where those texels changed in the last 32 frames, and the coverage value 6 (bit 2 over the attached 2) on a change's first frame. (3) The motion pass: kind 2 with bit 2 writes the invalidate value and the reactive mask 1; a screen at rest (2) keeps its history. (4) An interface texture UiContent declines keeps F105's rule (the held stand-in, every pixel edited), counted by UiContent's reason. (5) Both stand-ins write the screen's state (1 rest, 2 edited, 3 first frame) to a per-eye R8 target the census counts at the frame boundary (`kWorldScreenCensusCs`, a ring of four staging buffers, read with no wait). (6) Each interface texture is described once: its size, slices, mips, format and binding, the view's mips and slices, UiContent's decision, and its first pass's footprint from an occlusion query, in render and output pixels (`temporalPassUpscale`). (7) A draw of the pair that fails F105's test is counted by the first test it failed and named once. No key.

**Cost.** The census: one 16x16-group pass over each eye's R8 state target (the render size) on frames with a screen; the state targets 2 x 4 MB at 2016x2017; UiContent 6 bytes per 4x4 block per slice of the interface texture, one pass a frame per texture. GPU time not measured (no timer on the census).

**Health.** `ui depth world screens (F108): N frames; draws tracked T, held without change tracking H (reasons); not taken at the classification: ...; census F frames with a screen (S skipped): frames with an edit E, a change began C; at rest R frames, edited x of y px; during a change D frames, edited x of y px; history restarts P px in C frames.` every ui depth window beside F105's line, zeros included. `--health` rule `terminal hold (F108)`: no line is the code never having run; nothing marked IDLE; held everywhere and none tracked, or every screen pixel edited at rest, NEVER APPLIED, OLD BEHAVIOUR; no census row, some screens held everywhere, or over 5% edited at rest PARTIAL. Nine self-test cases.

**Rig.** ui_depth_test: the classification's refusals in order; the census's rest and change classification and the window boundary; the F108 line; both stand-ins' signatures (the game shader's inputs; targets 0, 1, 2; the tracked one's t1, b2 and t14 array); the held pass as F105's plus its state; UiContent's array path (a seeded array no edit, a changed texel edited only in its block and slice, no edit 32 frames on, a sub-range view's slice index, a non-render-target array declined); the tracked stand-in on WARP with two instances (the interface's slice and a solid colour): 6 and the first-frame state exactly where an edit begins and only on its first frame, the edit only there, none on the solid colour, rest again after the expiry, t14 put back; the census pass (counts, the ring's fifth frame skipped); the motion pass on WARP (the invalidate value and MK 1 at the 1024 fresh pixels, everything else as with no mask). 42413 checks (F105's build: 32545); the existing check that an array view declines now reads that an array view from mip 0 is tracked and one from mip 1 declines. hologram_depth_test (which compiles ui_depth.cpp too) gains the `temporalPassUpscale` stub.

**Build.** Full `build.bat --wait-lock` green, receipt `8b6a351f64e3...`, 227.6 s (the first run stopped at the two rigs above). Not installed, not flown.

### 2026-10-25: F108b (a terminal's change held 7 frames, not 32)
**The flight.** F108 flew in 28e1e557 (v0.21.1-225, log `edvr_gfx_20261025_055612`, Pimax Crystal Super, DLSS K): `terminal hold (F108)` OK over 35 windows, draws tracked 23746, held everywhere 0, edited at rest 0% (6113 frames), during a change 27%, history restarts in 669 frames. The terminals' interface textures are 3760x2115 (others 1848x1833 and 1660x1833), one slice, one mip, DXGI 27, viewed as a Texture2D (format 28); the largest first footprint 1,248,173 render px. The pilot: "Terminal from a distance looks better, when changing a selection on the screen using the keyboard, it briefly goes low res and then comes back sharp after a second."

**Why the hold can be short.** The hold is not what keeps a change from trailing. F105's doubling (dump 221109514003: 0.4-0.9% of the screen's output outside the raw 2x2 range) was DLSS's history of the old content, with nothing marked. F108 restarts that history on a change's first frame: UiContent sees a change in the frame it happens, both eyes read the same ages, and the 2x2 blocks about the uv add a block of margin. So no old content survives to trail. What the hold covers is DLSS on a fresh history, whose first frames have one or a few jittered samples per render pixel. That is the soft look the pilot saw, for 32 frames (0.36 s at 90 Hz), longer where the interface animates (the flight's changes come in bursts: 669 change frames among 2863 frames during a change). No dump in the F108 flight caught a change, so the length below is derived, not measured.

**The length: 7 frames.** EDVR's jitter for DLSS is the Halton (2,3) sequence repeating every 8 frames (`kTemporalJitterCount`, `temporal_math.h`). Eight frames after the restart, DLSS's history holds every offset it gets at rest. So a block is held on the change's frame and the 6 after it, and DLSS is shown from the 8th. A narrower test gives the same count at the flights' 2x upscale: the frames until each of a render pixel's four output pixels has had an offset strictly inside it are 5, 4, 6, 8, 7, 6, 6, 6 from the 8 starting phases (an offset of exactly 0, the sequence's first x, counted for neither side; counted for the right, the worst is 6). A hold of 4 shows DLSS from the 5th frame, before an output pixel has a sample of its own from 6 of the 8 phases.

**The change.** `kWorldScreenHoldFrames` = 7 (`EDVR_WORLD_SCREEN_HOLD_FRAMES`, compiled into the tracked stand-in; no key): a block is held while its age is above 1 - 6.5/32, so k = 0..6 of UiContent's (255 - 8k)/255. UiContent's 32-frame expiry is unchanged, for every other family and for the screen's own ages. The census's rest boundary is now the hold, so a hold that outlived it shows as edits at rest. Found on the way: the flight's terminals are a Texture2D view, so their ages were 2D and were bound to the stand-in's Texture2DArray register; the log's restarts say the driver read them anyway, but the dimension did not match. A 2D interface's ages now reach the stand-in as a one-slice array view (`UiContent::arrayView`).

**Health.** The F108 line gains `a change held N frames` and `changes from rest C` (a burst of change frames counts once). `terminal hold (F108)` reports the hold (32 for an F108 line, which has none) and the mean held frames per change, frames with an edit over changes from rest. Four new self-test cases: a short hold, no change from rest, the F108 flight's own line, and two builds' holds in one log.

**Rig.** ui_depth_test: the census's rest boundary at the hold and its changes from rest; the line; the tracked stand-in on WARP for a Texture2DArray interface and a Texture2D one. A block is held exactly 7 frames counting the change's own (state 3 then 2, the edit at UiContent's age) and is at rest on the 7th frame after, while UiContent's age (199/255) still lasts, and to the end of its expiry. It is held again for 7 frames when it changes again, and for 7 frames from its last change when it changes within the hold. `arrayView`: a 2D entry's one-slice array view made once, an array entry's ages returned as they are, a foreign view refused. 42988 checks.
