### 2026-10-25: F109 (look to aim on foot; the ADS stick turn; snap or smooth turn)
The pilot: "Can you also dust off the look to aim functionality, we didn't get it working before, but it seems to work well in ADS?" Then three decisions: the head is the only look on foot (armed and unarmed, yaw and pitch, no cone); the mouse and a controller's right stick no longer look, but still turn the player for seated play, as a snap (default) or a smooth turn; and a tester's report fixed with it: "trying to rotate the view with the RS while ADS causes the avatar to rotate but not the player's view, leading to misalignment."

**Why F22-F25 spun.** The old controller was a closed loop on camera C's yaw (list-B eye 0, the left eye). Its view compensation was published as plus the game's delta (`comp_sign` 1, never flown at -1), while the ADS head aim's cancel, flown and working since F68a, publishes minus it (`adsSeatFromGameYaw`) through the same look total. With the yaw sign +1 (the direction F68a confirmed) every body turn moved the reported head further from the aim: F22's error ran to -170 deg, F23 tripped after 1.5 s, F24 with +1 "turned all the way back"; with -1 the loop converged but the body turned away (F24). Camera C being the left eye explains the F62b-F66 ratio of -1, not the spin. This is an inference from the code and the flown convention; the old controller is retired, not flown again.

**The RE** (build 334925, capstone, `analysis\decomp\verify_20261025_onfoot_look_input.txt`, inbox item `20261025-053908-onfoot-look-input`; 49 checks re-run by its script). The look update (0x1999190) reads four actions: the right stick's yaw and pitch (act+0x180, +0x188, value +0x18), curved and handed to the sink's +0x164 / +0x160, and the mouse's (act+0x190, +0x198), raw, to +0x174 / +0x170; its own look block (a mask query, 0x1999218) zeroes them in the same function. The processor (0x1A9EB50) sums yaw = dt x rateA x stick + g x mouse + dt x spring (comp+0x780), pitch likewise with -dt x comp+0x79C; g is one linear gain between a hip and an ADS end (comp+0x808 / +0x80C, blended by a 0..1 factor, probably the zoom); the springs are critically damped (comp+0x770 / +0x78C), a game-driven turn not traced further. The summed delta goes through one stage in degrees (comp+0x340 vtbl+0x38 / +0x48, class not resolved) and is stored at comp+0x624 / +0x628; the aim takes it whole in the same call (0x18FF1E0, [comp+0x7B8] += delta) and drags the body's yaw into a cone around it.

**The ADS stick bug.** F62b's processor hook split the game's delta by the mouse ratio, ours = d x in / (mouse + in). The stick's term is in d but not in the ratio, so whenever the head aim wrote (almost every call, head tremor) the stick's whole turn was counted as the head aim's and cancelled in the seated space: the avatar turned, the view did not. The guard could not see it (the player's own turn read 0 and the view followed the head). F109's split (`nofoot::f109::Split`): ours = g x in, g taken only from clean calls (no stick, no spring, a delta), a call whose ask the game dropped counted as blocked and never a gain, a snap's call takes no gain; the rest of the delta is the player's own, which the cancel leaves alone, so the stick and the mouse turn the view with the avatar in ADS while the head aims, with look to aim on or off.

**Look to aim** (`fix.native_on_foot_look_to_aim`, off by default; on: the head is the look on foot). The ADS head aim's map (F68a, with F92b's cancel published ahead) runs all the time on foot, armed and unarmed, in full-3P body mode. The ask is a follower's (`nofoot::f109::Follower`): the target is the LOCAL head's turn since the engage plus the centring, the ask alpha x (target - applied - in flight), so an ask the game drops is asked again once it leaves the in-flight account; held to 180 deg/s an axis. The centring, once at each engage, adds the reported head's offset from the aim (the render head in the seated space). Smoothing (`_smoothing_ms`, 150) only with nothing drawn: ramped out by F88's armed weight and by the ADS weight. The guard (the right eye's rows against the head, less the player's own turn) runs all the time, its base re-taken every 10 s while it reads under 1 deg; a trip stops look to aim until the key toggles or on foot re-enters. While the game blocks the look (3 dropped asks in a row) the follower holds and probes every 100 ms, then catches the head up (the view never moved). An ADS press inside it keeps its sight lock, eye and body detach, but neither clears the map nor unwinds it; F69i's centring only measures. Turned off on foot, the carried turn unwinds through the map's release (the view stays, the body turns back) and the mouse and stick look again; at the end of on foot the seated rotation returns to zero. F98c's settle window takes nothing while the aim is pitched 10 deg or more (the animated neck bends with the aim's pitch). F88's axes are the AMC's; the body's yaw from the aim is measured on the 1 s line, not acted on (no evidence yet that it swings).

**The drop and the turns.** In the update hook, while look to aim is engaged: the stick's and the mouse's pitch are zeroed for the call (the head alone pitches); with `fix.native_on_foot_turn_style` = snap the stick's and the mouse's yaw too, which only trigger snaps; with smooth they pass (the game's own turning). Each written value is restored after the call; the panel pointer reads its own mouse source (F104's RE). Snap: the stick past 0.70, re-armed under 0.25, one step a push; a mouse flick of 20 deg would-be turn (the mouse's input through the measured gain) within 150 ms, then a 400 ms cooldown and a re-arm under a third; the step `fix.native_on_foot_snap_turn_deg` (45, 15-90). The snap is the player's own turn (the split leaves it out of the cancel, so the view, the body and the HUD turn together in one call), injected once the comfort fade (comfort_fade.h) is black: 20 ms in, held until the game applied it (25 ms at least, 100 ms at most), 30 ms out. Turning works in ADS in both styles; whether ADS survived a snap is logged.

**The runtime.** A reset (the serial) now returns the seated space to its origin itself (`lookRestorePending`); turning it back by the total about the head where it is now left a translation whenever the head moved between the turns, which after a standing look to aim session would have moved the cockpit's seat. The eye alignment's folded offset is applied again by eyePoll in the same poll, as at a new origin. Not covered by a rig (the host needs a session).

**Retired.** F22-F25's controller (lookToAimTick, its guard and rate cap, the F24 passive sign check and its 5 s line, which had printed in every VR session since F92b), the reticle-follow-head condition, and the three test keys `fix.native_on_foot_look_to_aim_yaw_sign`, `_comp_delay`, `_comp_sign` (hidden retired rows, retiredKeysNote, config_test). `_ads_head_aim_yaw_sign` and `_pitch_sign` stay until after this flight.

**Proof.** Lines and `--health` rules: `look to aim (F109)` (the 1 s line: head, asked, applied, the player's own, the reported head's offset from the aim, the guard, the body's yaw from the aim, the drop counts, the split counts and gains, blocked, springs, F98c refused; NEVER APPLIED when never engaged or when the game took none of the head's turn; PARTIAL for a trip, the aim off the head with the head still, the player's pitch reaching the game, unsplit calls); `snap turn (F109)` (each snap's applied turn against its step; ADS held or ended); `smooth turn (F109)` and `ADS player turn (F109)` (per second: the avatar's turn, comp+0x7B8, less the head aim's asks against the view's turn beyond the head's; the tester's case reads NEVER APPLIED). Self-test 228 -> 239 checks. Rig: native_frame_test 937 -> 948 (run109: the split with a stick held while the head aim writes, the gain from clean calls only, the drop by style, the stick and flick detectors, the snap's run, the smoothing, the follower against the real map with a blocked stretch and a 30 deg centring, the per-second check); config_test (fourteen retired keys); hotkey_capture_test (the page has 40 rows).

**Flight card (Epic; `--health` first; look to aim off, then on).**
1. Look to aim off, the rifle, ADS, turn with the right stick and the mouse: the view turns with the avatar (`ADS player turn (F109)` OK, look to aim off).
2. Look to aim on (snap): unarmed, look 90 deg left and right and 45 deg up and down; the view only ever moves with the head, the body follows gently (`look to aim (F109)` OK, the reported head under 1 deg from the aim when still); walk while turning the head: you walk where you look.
3. The mouse and the stick: no pitch at all; a stick push and a mouse flick each snap 45 deg with a short blink (`snap turn (F109)` OK); at a locker the panel pointer still follows the mouse; the item wheel still selects.
4. Draw the rifle: the weapon points where you look at once; ADS and release several times, a snap in ADS (the press held or ended, logged).
5. Turn style smooth: the stick turns you continuously (`smooth turn (F109)` OK).
6. Board the ship: the cockpit faces the right way and the seat sits where it was.

### 2026-10-25: F110 (the ADS model eye on the right eye)
A tester (Quest 3 over VDXR, DLSS preset K, render 1365x1470, output 2100x2262, build ae6539ae, log `edvr_gfx_20261025_114257`): "ADS is right-eye-aligned every time I'm doing it while looking at my ship, but is nose-aligned if I'm looking away from it." His `--health`: `ADS eye chain (F93b)` NEVER APPLIED ("matched 0 of 2321 measured frames (F70's 0, model eye 2321, held 0)"), `ADS press fit (F91)` NEVER APPLIED, `ads transition (F89)` "r shown on 0".

**The log.** The sight lock's right eye is the eye solved from its scene rows when they are this frame's, else a model. The rows come only from world draws of three scene vertex shaders (`drawtag::kSceneVs`, F53). In all 36 of the tester's ADS seconds (11:45:05-45) the F66e line reads "both eyes 0, one eye 0, none/implausible 2248" and the lock took the model on every frame; the F53 census those seconds refused 1152-1296 world draws a second as "not a scene geometry VS" and accepted none. Outside ADS the rows came and went with the view (28 of 75 seconds, e.g. 11:44:43-46 and 11:45:00-02 with "not a scene geometry VS 0" and the marker fix applied on 71-72 of 72). So the right eye was solved when such a draw was in view (his ship, by his words) and modelled when not. The model was F63's: the job camera plus half the IPD along the FP right ("half IPD 0.0313 m (the right eye's offset)"). The job camera is the left eye: the pilot's flight over Virtual Desktop (`edvr_gfx_20261024_220128`) solved both eyes on every ADS frame (both 1241, solved 1241, model 0) with "eye minus job camera L 0.0 -0.0 0.0, R 6.2 0.1 0.1; IPD 6.18 cm". F63's model therefore stood 3.1 cm short of the right eye, between the eyes: the nose. F66e had found the job camera to be the left eye after F63 built its model, and on the pilot's rigs the right eye's rows were always there, so the model never showed. VDXR and a later fix are ruled out above.

**The fix.** The model right eye is the job camera (the left eye), or the solved left eye when only its rows are this frame's, plus the whole IPD along R^ (`nofoot::adsModelRightEye`). The IPD is the right eye's head-space x less the left's (`temporalPassEyeOffsetX(1)` and `(0)`, as a distance), twice the right's when only it is known, else 6.3 cm (twice F63's 3.15); outside 4-9 cm, the fallback (`nofoot::adsSightIpd`, `kAdsSightIpdFallbackM`, `kAdsSightIpdMinM`/`MaxM`; the half-IPD names are gone). The lock and every consumer of its error take it, F93b's eye chain among them. The terrain shader as a row source waits. No key.

**The instrument.** The F66e 1 s line now says which source the model took on the frames the lock used it (the job camera or the solved left eye), the IPD and where it came from, and, whenever the right eye is solved too, the job camera's model minus the solved right eye (body axes, mean, max, frames): about 0 cm, against F63's 3.1. The sight lock line reads "IPD" for "half IPD". `--health` rule `ADS model eye (F110)`: the share of ADS frames on the model; PARTIAL when the camera's model is more than 0.5 cm off the solved right eye; on a log before F110, PARTIAL whenever a frame took F63's model (the tester's log: "F63's model 2321 (100%)"; the pilot's: OK, 0 of 1241).

**Rig.** native_frame_test +4 (run110): from a left-eye job camera the model is the right eye (F63's half 3.13 cm short, the control); with only the left eye's rows, the solved left eye plus the IPD; the fallback (none, the right offset alone, out of range); mirrored offsets give the same IPD and the model goes along the FP right, also yawed. F63's check of the offsets reads the IPD. `edvr_log --health` self-test +4 cases. Full `build.bat --wait-lock` green on the first pass, receipt `7740e7e8b464...`, 336.9 s. Not installed, not flown. **For the flight:** ADS facing away from any ship or building: the sight on the right eye; `ADS model eye (F110)` OK, the camera's model within 0.5 cm of the solved right eye wherever both exist.

### 2026-10-25: F111 (the panel pointer instrument)
The F104 card's pass B flew (log `edvr_gfx_20261025_055612`, v0.21.1-225-g28e1e557, the right build, Epic, Pimax Crystal Super on Pimax OpenXR): the HUD keys at the game's own placement, distance 0.19 m (scale 0.990, 06:01:33.922), size 1.00 and room 1.00 (06:01:26). The pilot: "Changing those settings on the hud did not impact the mouse. Still couldn't click any UI buttons and control is still inverted in both directions i.e. moving the mouse up causes the cursor to move down."

ruled out: C2, EDVR's HUD rescale as the cursor's inversion, because pass B (the game's own HUD values) left it inverted on both axes and the click still failed (log edvr_gfx_20261025_055612)

**Both axes.** A point reflection: a direction negated in x and y, a 180 degree roll in some frame, or a projection whose x and y scale signs flip when it is unprojected. A view from behind the panel would flip one axis only.

**The pick's conventions** (build 334925; handed to the analysis inbox as `verify_20261025_onfoot_pointer_frame.txt`, beside `analysis\decomp\verify_20261024_onfoot_cursor_pick.txt`). The update (0x454F520, the controller's vtable slot at 0x55DC7F0) first resets the sprite (+0x100 = 0, rows +0x110/+0x120/+0x130 the identity, +0x140 = 0), reads the mouse point into +0x84/+0x88 (x right, y down) and keeps +0x80 = 1 once it changed (forced to 0 while byte +0x172 or +0x173 is set; then the other point at +0x8C is used). The conversion (0x456EEE0, its one caller) copies the camera state from (*[+0xA0])->vtable+0x58()->vtable+0x30(), sets its pose to the identity at the origin (axes built from (0,0,1) and (0,1,0): x right, y up, z forward), unprojects the clip point (x, -y, 1, 1) through the 4x4 the copy holds at +0x1F0, divides by w and stores the normalised direction at +0xB0. With no hit the sprite stays at that unit direction. The placement (0x4559C50, slot 0x55DC7F8) runs once per panel; in ray mode the ray from the origin along +0xB0 meets the panel's triangles (panel vtable +0x178 = 0x452B6A0; t < 0 and t > FLT_MAX rejected) and the nearest hit over all panels poses the sprite; in the 2D mode the NDC goes through the cursor window (+0x198 = 0x4541A20) to a uv.

**The candidates and their signatures** (each a sign of one stage's change against the mouse's, from one controller update to the next):
- K4, the mouse NDC inverted before the controller sees it: the OS cursor (GetCursorPos) against the NDC, r < 0 on an axis (n/a when the game recentres the OS cursor).
- K1, the direction against the NDC (the projection EDVR's GetProjectionRaw answer builds, or the game's S*E*S handedness, unprojected with x and y flipped): NDC to direction r < 0, the slope d(dir.x/dir.z) per NDC unit negative.
- K5, the direction behind the camera: a far point at z < 0, as an OpenVR-style projection (forward along -z) taken without the game's z flip gives: x and y follow the NDC, z < 0, no ray is accepted (t < 0), the sprite rests at the direction behind the camera, and the sprite as the camera sees it (x/z, y/z) moves against the mouse on both axes. That is the point reflection, the click that never lands and a cursor at its own depth, all at once.
- K2, the hit's frame or the sprite's: rays accepted, NDC to uv r < 0, or the direction to the sprite r < 0 (a 180 degree roll between the pick's camera and the panel).
- K3, the 2D mode's cursor window: window calls and no rays, NDC to uv r < 0.
- After the pick (the sprite's draw): every stage follows the mouse, rays accepted, yet the pilot sees it inverted: the verdict "none in the pick".

**The instrument.** Four hooks in the F9 probe pattern (`native_on_foot_f111.h` holds the addresses, the 21-, 22-, 16- and 23-byte prologue pins, 5 bytes stolen each, and the pure statistics): the update (the cycle before closes with the sprite as the placements left it, +0x100, +0x140 and the movie counter +0x1B4; after the game's update the new one opens with the source, the NDC, the direction, the OS cursor and the camera), the placement (scopes the next two to its controller on its thread), the ray hit (accepted or not, t and uv of the nearest) and the cursor window (its output). Each runs the original and only reads; the camera getters are followed only when their code is a plain accessor (mov or lea from rcx, then ret), else the line names the getter's bytes. The hooks are armed once in VR behind the identity check and each vtable slot, and open while native stereo is on foot. Lines: `panel pointer (F111): hooks armed N of 4`, up to five `panel pointer (F111) move:` lines a second (NDC, source, direction, placements, rays accepted, t, window calls, hit, sprite, uv and its source, movie notes, the OS cursor's step), `panel pointer (F111) 1 s: verdict: ...` (counts, behind the camera, the correlations NDC to direction, direction to sprite, NDC to the sprite as seen, NDC to uv, OS cursor to NDC, the slopes, the signs, the camera's position and rows) and every 10 s with the pointer `panel pointer (F111) so far: verdict: ...` (the flight's moves together). The verdict is the first of K4, K1, K5, K2, K3 that the signs show, else "none in the pick". What the log shows if the code never ran: no armed line (not VR), "hooks armed 0 of 4" with the reasons, or the armed line and no 1 s line (the hooks never saw the controller). The click path itself was not reached; the movie counter +0x1B4 and the accepted hits stand in for it. No key. `--health` rule `panel pointer (F111)`: the inverting stage; NEVER APPLIED with no hook armed or no controller seen; IDLE when the pointer never moved enough; PARTIAL with fewer than four hooks or no placement seen.

**Rig.** native_frame_test +10 (run111): a modelled pick through the pilot's path (up, right, back): sane, it reads "none in the pick" with the frustum's half-tangents as the slopes; with one stage turned at a time it names K1 (negative slopes), K5 (no hit, the sprite as seen reflected on both axes while the direction follows), K2, K3 and K4 (named before a later stage that also inverts); a still cursor reads too few moves; merged seconds keep their moves; the correlation needs three pairs; the getters' decoding. `edvr_log --health` self-test +6 cases. Full `build.bat --wait-lock` green on the first pass, receipt `469a277207ca...`, 289.5 s. Not installed, not flown.

**For the flight** (Epic; `--health` first): at a locker with the inventory open, the mouse up for a second, still, right for a second, still, a click on a row, then the head turned left and right with the mouse still; one eye dump. `panel pointer (F111)` names the stage; the move lines give the numbers for the fix.

### 2026-10-25: F109b (look to aim: the guard holds where it cannot judge; the smooth turn's check)
The F109 flight: log `edvr_gfx_20261025_071049`, v0.21.1-236-g33e05706 (the right build), Epic, Pimax Crystal Super on Pimax OpenXR. The pilot: "look to aim seems to not engage initially/loses functionality, but toggling it off and then back on seems to restore it - works well otherwise"; snap turns felt fine. `--health`: `look to aim (F109)` PARTIAL (344 s engaged, 3 engages, the head turned 2022.9 deg and the game applied 2029.0, 2 guard trips), `snap turn (F109)` OK (12 of 12 exact), `smooth turn (F109)` PARTIAL (agreed 1, disagreed 53), `ADS player turn (F109)` not present.

**Engagement.** One on-foot session, about 07:12:20 to 07:27:30. The key read off at launch (07:10:50, the live `edvr.ini`), and every engage came in the tick the key turned on: 07:14:16, 07:16:50, 07:19:42, 07:26:02. The lost function was the two trips. F109 held look to aim off after any trip until the key toggled, with a `not engaged: the guard tripped` line every 5 s: 17 s after the first (07:19:25 to the toggle at 07:19:42) and 5 min 18 s after the second (07:20:44 to 07:26:02).

ruled out: look to aim failing to engage at a session's start, because each of the four engages came in the tick the key turned on, and the key read off at launch

**The two trips were the guard's measurement, not a runaway.**
- 07:19:25: residual yaw +0.5, pitch -12.2 deg against the head's yaw +5.6, pitch -2.4. The base had stood since the engage at 07:16:50 (the 10 s re-base waits for a residual under 1 deg, and the turning kept it over), and since it the player had turned -191.1 deg with the smooth stick, from a view about 7.7 deg down (the seated pitch carried). The guard reads the view's turn since the base in the base's own axes, and a turn about the world's up seen from a base pitched p reads as a pitch of about asin(sin(2p)/2 (1 - cos turn)): -12 to -15 deg for a view 6 to 8 deg down. Subtracting the player's yaw cannot remove it, because it lands on pitch.
- 07:20:44: residual pitch -17.9 deg against the head's -0.1, 0.6 s after a 10 s re-base, the player's own yaw +0.8 since it. The commander was jumping: F87p's line at 07:20:43 reads the scene eye against the job camera at a pitch sd of 4.2 deg. The game pitched its camera itself. The head aim had asked for about the head's -0.1 deg of pitch, and no fault of its cancel moves the view by more than about twice what it asked.

ruled out: missing or stale right-eye rows as the trips' cause, because the guard steps only on this frame's rows and the smooth check's lines in the seconds before each trip read no rows 0 (07:19:19 and 07:19:20; 07:20:42 and 07:20:43)
ruled out: a runaway of the head aim's cancel (a sign inverted, or a camera that does not take the aim) at either trip, because both residuals were in pitch where the head had pitched -2.4 and -0.1 deg, and the first came after 191 deg of the player's own turn on one base

**The smooth turn's check measured the wrong thing.** The pilot was in smooth from 07:15:04. The per-second check took the avatar's turn from comp+0x7B8, which did not follow the aim: it read +0.00 deg in seconds where the game applied 5 to 35 deg, so the player's own turn read as the opposite of the asks. A rows gap also moved a turn into the next second (-146 against -79 for a 67 deg turn). Where a second was whole, the view matched the player's turn: 07:19:20, +46.18 against +51.41; 07:20:42, +37.90 against +40.66. The behaviour was right and the check was wrong.

ruled out: the smooth turn not reaching the view (the 53 disagreeing seconds), because comp+0x7B8 stays at 0 while the game applies the turn, and the whole seconds agree within 11%

**`ADS player turn (F109)` absent.** No ADS second had a turn of the player's own. There were three presses, all with look to aim on (07:14:49 for 2.2 s, 07:15:41 for 1.4 s, 07:15:49 for 1.2 s), and the player's own turn read 0.00 deg in every second, under the line's 3 deg. The card's step 1 (look to aim off, the rifle in ADS, the stick and the mouse) was not flown.

**The fix: the guard's validity gates** (`nofoot::AdsResidual`), which hold the guard where its measurement does not hold. They are not dead bands.
1. A player's own turn past 15 deg since the base takes a new base (`userRebases`), so the base's axes are near the view's whenever it judges. Under 15 deg the F68a rule is unchanged.
2. A gap over 200 ms without a fresh measurement restarts the growth run (`gapRestarts`): the run's 0.5 s must be seen.
3. Causal (set by the head aim's tick): the asks the head aim sent since the base are summed. A trip needs the residual on each axis within 2.5 x the net ask + 4 deg, because a sign inverted reads about twice the ask and a camera that does not take the aim about once. Past that, the game moved the view on its own: the guard takes a new base, counts it (`holds`) and writes a `the guard held` line (at most one a second).

The gates apply in an ADS press with look to aim off too, where a trip still holds the press off, as since F68a. Under look to aim, a trip stops it for 2 s, and then it engages again by itself with a fresh centring. The third trip within 60 s holds it off until the key toggles or native on foot re-enters.

**The smooth turn's check.** The avatar's turn is the processor's own delta (comp+0x624) summed on every call (`g_f109TotalYaw`). A tick counts only when this tick's rows and the last tick's are fresh, so a gap's turn is counted as neither the view's nor the avatar's. The line's format is F109's.

**Proof.** The look to aim 1 s line ends with the guard's gates: held, re-based (the player's own turn), growth restarted (a rows gap), trips and re-armed. `look to aim (F109)` reads them, the `the guard held` lines and the re-arms, and reports them without judging them. F109's line, which lacks them, still parses, and a trip is still PARTIAL. Rig: native_frame_test +5 (run109):
- a 191 deg turn of the player's own from a base 8 deg down reads about -16 deg of pitch in the base's axes, and the guard never trips (a new base every 15 deg, residual under 0.5 deg);
- the game pitching the view 18 deg in 0.3 s, with next to nothing asked, trips the guard without the causal gate and is held with it;
- with the causal gate on, a camera that does not take the aim and an inverted sign still trip within 2 s;
- a 300 ms rows gap inside a run restarts the run, and the trip comes 0.5 s after the gap, not at its end.

edvr_log self-test: +2.

**For the flight** (Epic; `--health` first):
- Look to aim on, smooth: turn 180 deg and more with the stick, and jump several times. Expect `look to aim (F109)` with no trip, re-based counted while turning, and any holds during the jumps; and `smooth turn (F109)` OK.
- Look to aim off: the rifle in ADS, the stick and the mouse. Expect `ADS player turn (F109)` OK.

### 2026-10-25: F113 (each eye's scene rows whenever the world is drawn)
The pilot, after the 33e05706 flight (`edvr_gfx_20261025_071049`, Pimax Crystal Super): "the weapon/tool ui has the same issue as the ADS right eye lock, looking away towards empty terrain causes the ui to go missing/be incorrectly placed". `--health`: `weapon UI pin (F85b)` refused 11022 draws, 10294 of them "no scene rows for the eye"; `ADS model eye (F110)` on the model in 56% of ADS frames. F109's look-to-aim guard reads the same rows and tripped twice.

**Where the rows came from.** An eye's scene rows (b1 rows 270..273 and the origin row 275) were taken only by `worldDraw`, which the draw tee reaches only for a vertex shader of the engine families, and only from a draw of the three scene mesh shaders (`drawtag::kSceneVs`) into the eye's scene depth. Facing bare ground or the sky none draws, so every consumer refused: the weapon UI pin, the marker patch, the labels, the ADS lock and F109's guard. F87f had named the depth prepass as a fallback, but its capture sat inside `worldDraw`, behind the same filter, so it never ran: "from F516BF02 0" and "both 0" in every second of the 04:41, 05:56 and 07:10 flights, against 1541, 0 and 2656-2727 marker frames with no scene rows.

**The census.** The F57 row census (the content of every b1 a frame, its first draw per eye, compared with the eye's main scene content) ran only before F100 put it behind the probe key, so its sessions are the F98 flight (`edvr_gfx_20261024_192353`, 570 lines) and a tester's (`edvr_gfx_20261025_114257`, 154 lines); the three flights the round named have none. Over the two sessions:
- the depth prepass (VS F516BF0201303B87, PS B40B0462256E31C2) was the main content in every compared frame (F98: 20,078 and 20,078 per eye; the tester: 313 and 658), never another, and drew in 3,025 and 3,173 of the tester's frames that had no scene mesh;
- the terrain patch (VS ACE405F428C17EF6, no PS) likewise in the tester's session (1,720 and 1,230 of 1,720 and 1,230 compared; 416 and 413 frames with no mesh), and drew in 20 frames of the F98 flight with no mesh to compare;
- VS 53211E8C072CD02E (PS 7EAC71963E66C5FE), the most frequent other first draw, carried another camera (up to 176 deg off): not a source.
The prepass is confirmed on both sessions, the terrain on one; F87's own analysis of the F86 flight (12,858 of 12,858) agrees on the prepass.

**The route: (a), with a check.** Route (b), rows built from the job camera and the eye offsets as F110's model eye, is ruled out for the pin above (F110 measured that model up to 2.2 cm off). The draw tee now sends a draw outside the engine families to `rowSourceDraw` when it is one of the two sources (`nofoot::f113::rowSourceOf`) and an eye still has no rows this frame. The eye is the scene depth view's (`eyeOfDraw`); the rows come from the CB shadow as before and are published exactly as a mesh's are (`worldPut`, `g_cpuWorld`, `eyeRowsPublish`, `g_worldOk`), with the eye's scene target size from the bound colour target when it is eye-sized. Once a second an eye whose rows came from a source, the tee's slow path stays open for that frame and the eye's next scene mesh draw compares its rows with the source's; a difference over 1e-5 (`f87::kFbTolerance`) latches the sources off for the session (logged, `f87::FbGuard`). F87f's capture, promote and compare are removed; its pure parts (`kFbVs`, `kFbPs`, `FbGuard`) serve F113. No key.

**The instrument.** The line `native on foot eye rows (F113) 1 s`, per eye: the frames on foot and how many had their rows from the scene meshes, the depth prepass or the terrain, and how many had none; the checks against a mesh and their largest difference; source draws refused (no scene depth eye, no b1 shadow, latched). It replaces the F87f line. `--health` rule `eye rows (F113)`: PARTIAL on a latch or an eye without rows in more than 2% of its frames, NEVER APPLIED when frames had no rows and no source ever gave any.

**Rig.** native_frame_test 962 -> 965 (run113): the sources and their partners (not the other camera, not a mesh); a second's accounting by source; the check's once-a-second schedule, its hold on the tee's fast path (`f100::TeeState::check`) and the latch. `edvr_log --health` self-test +3 cases. Full `build.bat --wait-lock` green on the first pass, receipt `456245659b54...`, 313.4 s. Not installed, not flown. The newest dump of the flight (072543386005) is a station interior with meshes in view and shows nothing of the failure. **For the flight:** a tool and a weapon out, looking at bare ground and the sky: `eye rows (F113)` OK with none near 0% and the prepass or the terrain giving the rows there; `weapon UI pin (F85b)` without "no scene rows"; `ADS model eye (F110)` solved on most ADS frames; F109's guard not tripping on missing rows.

### 2026-10-25: F116 (the HUD hidden while a terminal fills the view)
**The report.** Log `edvr_gfx_20261025_071049` (33e05706, Epic, Pimax Crystal Super, 2016x2017 render per eye, DLSS): "the hud clips through/is displayed while interacting with a terminal. Is it possible to hide the hud during these interactions?" In dumps 072154496003 and 060611711003 the radar, the compass bar, the objective and the suit block are drawn over a settlement terminal's screen. They are the HRC's HUD meshes, which EDVR has the game create (F10/F11) and places at 0.19 m (F12/F13): in front of a screen farther away, and depth-tested, so the screen cuts into them only where it comes nearer than 0.19 m. The pilot later: flat Elite does not hide its HUD at a terminal either, but its elements are smaller there.

**The signal.** No game state marks a terminal in use (Ruled out, F116, two lines). The F105 screens' footprint does: in every census window of the three terminal uses in the two sessions (055612 05:58:30-06:00:29 and 06:05:17-06:06:31, 071049 07:21:16-07:22:13) they covered 1.56-2.82 M render pixels a frame across both eyes (19-35% of each eye); walking past, 31-40 k (0.4%).

**The game's own hide (static, build 334925, capstone).** The HRC function (+0x1A16F10) submits the HUD's meshes only when its controller ([HRC+0x1D0], vtable +0x520D958) answers yes at slot +0x80 (+0x1A8F950): visible (slot +0x78) AND [controller+0x380] == 0 AND not an HMD (modes 3, 4). Slots +0x60 and +0x58 increment and decrement +0x380; +0x70 and +0x68 do the same to a sibling at +0x384, which slot +0x88 reads for another component (the function after the HRC's calls it on [obj+0x240]). EDVR's creation patch (+0x1A16F48, 0x80 -> 0x78) asks slot +0x78 alone, so the counter goes with the HMD test. Nothing shows whether the game raises it at a terminal, and the pilot reports flat keeps its HUD there; F116 therefore reads both counters and logs every rise, and does not act on them.

**The change.** (1) F108's census counts each eye into its own range (a 32-byte buffer, two views), and every frame takes a place in a frame order: a frame with a screen waits for its census row, one with none is 0 at once, one whose census was skipped is unknown and leaves the hide as it was. (2) The hysteresis on the render thread (`native_on_foot_f116.h`): the larger eye over 15% for 2 frames in a row hides the HUD; under 10% for 10 frames shows it. (3) P2 returns 0 without calling the game while the hide holds and was stepped within 250 ms (a stalled ui depth shows the HUD). That is the game's own path when its gate answers no: nothing before the gate has a side effect, and the placement (F12/F13) is skipped with the call. (4) The counters: the call site, the test, both pushes and pops and the six vtable slots are pinned and checked at install; per call the controller's vtable must be the verified one before the eight bytes at +0x380 are read. No key.

**Health.** `HUD hide (F116) 30 s: ...` every 30 s on foot, zeros included; `terminal episode N began` and `... ended after S s, F frames: footprint peak P; HRC calls C, skipped K`; `the game's counter rose` and `fell`, with both values and the footprint. Rule `HUD hide (F116)`: no HRC call is NEVER APPLIED (the hook never decided); a terminal over 15% for 2 s or more with the HUD submitted is PARTIAL; no census row is IDLE, naming whether an external upscaler ran; the hide held with nothing skipped is NEVER APPLIED; no hide is IDLE; otherwise OK. Nine self-test cases.

**Rig.** native_frame_test `run116`, 23 checks: the footprint (the larger eye's share), the hysteresis (on the 2nd frame over 15%, off on the 10th under 10%, the 10-15% band holding and restarting the count, single frames never hiding), the frame order (waiting, none, unknown, a row lost on read-back, a full queue), the hook's freshness, the counters' read order, the episodes, the submitted run and the lines. ui_depth_test: the census counts each eye apart (18 and 18; one eye alone 0 and 18).

**Build.** Validated in the arc's combined build (with F114b and F115); not built on its own branch.

### 2026-10-25: F114 (the pointer's verdict from the F111 flight; offline, not built)
The F111 flight (log `edvr_gfx_20261025_071049`, v0.21.1-236-g33e05706, the right build, Epic, Pimax Crystal Super on Pimax OpenXR; HUD distance 0.19, size 1.00, follow body). `--health` `panel pointer (F111)`: 826 s with the pointer, 65024 cycles, 2497 moves, ray 0, window 6265, nothing behind the camera; 1 s verdicts "too few moves" 732, "none in the pick" 93, K4 1 (07:24:44, as the panel opened). The pilot, before the flight: inverted on both axes, no click lands on a button.

**What the lines show.** Outside a panel the controller runs with no placement (13 placement calls a cycle, neither the ray nor the window; the sprite rests at the direction, as the update leaves it): gameplay, nothing drawn. With a panel open the game takes the 2D mode only: the cursor window (panel vtable +0x198) turns the NDC into a uv that follows the mouse (over the flight NDC to uv r +0.96 right, +1.00 down). The panel's uv-to-point (+0x188) then places the sprite on the panel's pick mesh, and that point moves against the uv on both axes. Over the 59 window hits (07:24:44-07:27:27), in the pick's camera frame (x right, y up, z forward): sprite = O + u U + v V, O = (0.83, -0.37, 0.60), U = (-1.63, -0.05, 0.10), V = (-0.07, +0.89, 0.00), residual 3-8 cm rms (the panel is curved). Its centre (uv 0.5, 0.5) lies at (-0.02, 0.05, 0.65): straight ahead (-1.9, +4.3 deg); its angular size (tan 2.5 wide, 1.4 high) is about the drawn panel's in the dump. An upright panel facing the camera has U along +x and V along -y; this one has U along -x and V along +y, the same plane and facing: the panel turned 180 degrees about the view axis. Example (07:24:53-54): the mouse right 0.067 NDC, u 0.502 -> 0.536, the sprite's x -0.032 -> -0.088.

F111's verdict read "none in the pick" because its sprite correlation counted ray hits only; in the 2D mode the uv was checked against the NDC and passed.

ruled out: K1, the unprojection, because the NDC to direction correlation is +0.84 right, +0.98 up over the flight (slope +1.064/+1.065 tan per NDC unit)
ruled out: K5, the direction behind the camera, because it was behind in 0 of 65024 cycles
ruled out: K3, the cursor window inverting, because the window's uv follows the mouse (r +0.96 right, +1.00 down)
ruled out: K4, the mouse NDC inverted before the controller, because the OS cursor followed the NDC (r +1.00 on both axes) over the first 100 s, before the game began recentring it; the one K4 second (07:24:44, the panel opening) read r -0.50 on x over 25 OS moves
ruled out: EDVR's HUD placement (F12/F13) as the 180 degree turn, because it only scales by positive factors and applies no head transform under follow body, and this flight ran it near neutral (distance 0.19 m, scale 0.990, size 1.00)

**Not proven, and why no fix was built.** (1) Who turns the pick mesh: its triangles are refreshed (0x45412E0) from the panel's mesh data through a transform its owner returns (vtable +0x10), not read yet; the game's own VR panel path (never used on foot in stock Elite) and the camera EDVR's native stereo hands the game are both open. (2) How the drawn cursor follows the sprite: in dump 072515662004 (07:25:15, the window's uv (0.658, 1.000) since 07:25:10, the sprite at (-0.184, +0.799, +0.622)) the cursor is drawn at (0.57, 0.58) of the drawn panel, which is neither the uv nor its turn (0.34, 0.00), nor where the sprite's pose would project from the pick's camera; so the cursor's draw has a transform of its own. (3) The click: the 2D branch's only movie call formats "%s %.5f %.5f" with the uv and is gated by the byte at exe+0x603CDB8; +0x1B4, which counts it, never moved, so the movie takes the pointer by another path. Turning the sprite back (the mesh read at 1 - u, 1 - v) would make the drawn cursor move with the mouse only if (2) has no turn of its own, and would land a click only if (3) reads the sprite; neither is known.

**The next instrument (one flight).** (a) The pick mesh's transform: the owner's vtable +0x10 output in 0x45412E0 (three rows, position, scale) per panel while placed, beside the HRC placement matrices (+0x430, +0x480) and the panel's world transform (+0x740 to +0x77F): which one carries the turn. (b) The drawn cursor: the draw census watch on VS 4EF6DDB075A927FA (b0 rows of the 128x128 cursor quad, both eyes) in an eye dump with a panel open, against the sprite's pose that frame: the cursor's draw transform. (c) The click: the controller's button path (the strings `UI_Mouse_Button%d` beside the format; the controller's other vtable slots) to the movie: what point a click uses. Flight: a panel open, the mouse moved in a slow circle, two clicks on a known row, one eye dump with the cursor over a row.

### 2026-10-25: F114b (the panel pointer's transforms, click path and mode, in VR and in flat)
The instrument F114 asked for, read only, with one addition: the hooks open in the flat profile on foot too, so a short flat session shows the stock path beside VR's. No behaviour change, no key.

**Read first** (build 334925, capstone; handed to the analysis inbox with this entry). The pick mesh's owner has its own vtable at 0x55DBA10 (+0x00 0x452D320 its mesh data, +0x10 0x4526E40 its transform; the scalar deleting destructor 0x44F36B0 sits in the slot before it). 0x4526E40 reads the camera through [owner+0x20] (the same getter chain as the pick's), then writes a flag byte at +0x00, the owner's world rows (+0x740, +0x750, +0x760) dotted with the camera's axes at +0x10/+0x20/+0x30, the owner's position (+0x770) less the camera's, in the camera's axes, at +0x40, and the scale 1.0 at +0x50: the layout 0x45412E0 reads back (rows at its +0x30.., position at +0x60, scale at +0x70). The controller's input set-up (0x4504BB0, its vtable +0x18) binds `UI_Mouse_ZAxis` at +0x78 and `UI_Mouse_Button0..2` at +0x60/+0x68/+0x70 and sets +0x170. Each update reads a button's state bytes (+0x24 now, +0x34 before): down when now is set and before is not, up the other way, written as 1 or 2 into the map at [+0x168]+0x18 (the wheel into [+0x168]+0x0C/+0x10), but only when byte +0x171 was set, and the update stores the input context's activity into +0x171 for the next frame. The 2D branch's "%s %.5f %.5f" call (the panel's name and the uv) is gated by the byte at exe+0x603CDB8 and counted at +0x1B4.

**The instrument.** A fifth hook on the owner's +0x10 (0x4526E40, its slot and 25 prologue bytes pinned). Within a placement it keeps the owner's world rows and the transform it returned; inside a ray hit it waits for the hit to be the nearest accepted one. At the cycle's close the camera's world rows and position follow from the two (C = (O^-1 Q)^T, c = o - C^T q; the orthogonality of C is logged), with no call into the game. The sprite is then followed three ways: in the pick's camera frame (`uv to sprite in the camera`), in the owner's own axes (`in the owner's axes`: the mesh's uv layout) and in the eye's view (the HRC submit's view rows and position, view 2 when there is one, the tangents over |z|: `as the eye sees it`). The camera's axes are compared with the eye's, the owner's with the HUD canvas's (HRC +0x430). The turn's verdict uses the eye as the reference, because the drawn panel is upright there:
- the sprite follows the uv for the eye but not in the pick's frame: **the pick camera**;
- it is turned for the eye but upright in the owner's own axes: **the owner's world transform**;
- it is turned in the owner's own axes: **the mesh data**;
- it follows everywhere: **none**.

In flat no eye's view is read; there the pick's camera is the screen.

The cursor draw: `mouse to the eye's view` says whether the sprite's own pose, as the eye sees it, follows the mouse. A cursor the pilot sees moving against the mouse while this follows it means the draw adds a turn of its own.

The clicks: per cycle the three buttons' edges (counted with the cycle's uv, the last press's uv kept), the buttons live (+0x171) per cycle, the sink (+0x168), the init byte (+0x170) and the note byte. The mode: cycles with the ray, the window or neither, and the mode object at +0x188 (its vtable, its +0x40 getter's RVA and bytes, decoded and its value read when it is a plain accessor). Each pick mesh owner function a placement names is logged once; one that is not 0x4526E40 says its transform was not read.

Lines: `panel pointer (F114b): owner transform hook armed`, `panel pointer (F114b) 1 s: profile vr|flat; turn: ...; cursor draw: ...; mode: ...; clicks: ...` (only in a second with a panel), `panel pointer (F114b) so far:` every 10 s with a panel. F111's hooks and lines are unchanged except that they open in flat on foot too. Rule `panel pointer (F114b)`, per profile: the turn, the cursor draw, the mode, the clicks; NEVER APPLIED when no panel was seen; PARTIAL when the owner transform was not read.

**Rig.** native_frame_test +9 (run114b). A modelled panel, eye, pick camera, owner and mesh, one turned at a time: the camera recovered from the owner's rows and transform (scaled owner, turned and yawed camera), then each verdict named from the readings alone:
- all upright: none, the 2D mode;
- the camera turned: the pick camera, its axes -1/-1/+1 against the eye;
- the owner turned: the owner's world transform, -1/-1 against the canvas, and the eye sees the sprite move against the mouse;
- the mesh turned: the mesh data;
- no eye: turned in the pick's frame;
- a still cursor, and no panel;
- a press counted with its uv, and the edges;
- the mode getter's plain forms (a getter that calls is refused).

`edvr_log --health` self-test +5 cases.

**Build.** Validated in the arc's combined build (with F115 and F116), not on this branch alone. Not installed, not flown.

**The flight card.**
- VR (Epic, native on foot): at a locker with the inventory open, the mouse in a slow circle for five seconds, then still; two clicks on one row; the mouse to the panel's four corners in turn; one eye dump with the cursor over a row; the head turned left and right with the mouse still.
- Flat (the flat profile, on foot, the same locker): the same circle, the two clicks on the same row (they should land), the four corners.

`--health` first, then both profiles' `panel pointer (F114b)` lines.

### 2026-10-25: F115 (boarding undoes every on-foot camera change)
The pilot (Pimax Crystal Super on Pimax OpenXR, Epic): "boarding the ship causes the headset to be placed at the former height when standing and then it moves to the neck, kind of. It ends up being too low and a reset HMD is required. Can you completely disable the native onfoot camera changes when a user boards their ship?" The maintainer's decision: from the moment the commander boards, every native on-foot change to the camera or head pose stops and is undone; the cockpit is the seat memory's origin and forward with nothing left over.

**The boarding** (log `edvr_gfx_20261025_071049`, v0.21.1-236-g33e05706, the right build; its runtime log `edvr_openxr_20261025_071051_484_31900` stamps UTC, 6 h ahead of the graphics log):
- 07:27:28.0: the game stops updating on foot (the look's input sample goes stale; no third-person submit from 07:27:29.1).
- 07:27:29.83: the cockpit is drawn (the cockpit holo panels' first draw at 29.832; the HMD camera's reset, transition flash frame 86241, holds frames 86242-86243 only).
- 07:27:30.13, the last on-foot second: the standing-height hold +16.9 cm (the head 16.9 cm under the seated origin, `seat_meter -15.8 cm`), the view 15.6 cm over the neck; the runtime's eye alignment y -0.346 m (13:27:29.291, serial 8576): a 34.6 cm raise. Look to aim carried yaw -5.84 deg, pitch +4.86 deg.
- 07:27:30.816: Status.json's on-foot bit falls and native stereo on foot ends; the runtime's seat memory hears "boarded" at 13:27:30.818 (origin_is_seat 1, apply_wanted 0, no seat change). Look to aim and the head aim stop, the yaw and pitch to zero at once (the runtime's resets 9 -> 10, compensation 0). The eye alignment ramps out over 0.5 s (the hold's `kHoldRampS` and the neck reference's `kRampS`; serial 8576 -> 8622 by 13:27:34.290, about 35 publications), the cockpit drawn throughout and nothing withheld or faded.
- 13:27:32.813 (2 s after): the seat meter reads the head 17.8 cm under the seated origin (head LOCAL 0.005/0.257/-0.627, origin 0.055/0.436/-0.555, yaw 27.5).
- 13:27:34.290 to the log's end: eye alignment 0 (serial 8622), look compensation 0.
- 07:27:37.578: the pilot recentres (`honour_press`, 16.1 cm) and the seat is stored.

**Three causes, in the order the pilot saw them.**
1. "Placed at the former height": native stereo on foot ends at Status.json's on-foot bit, 1.0 s after the cockpit is first drawn, and until then the raise and the look stay applied in the cockpit. The other 15 ends of native stereo on foot in the flights since 10-24 05:05 were not boardings: the journal has a Shutdown 6-9 s after each and no Embark (the pilot quit from on foot). Four boardings are in the logs, two VR (10-23 Frontier `edvr_gfx_20261023_095540`, this one) and two flat (Steam `edvr_gfx_20261024_041843` and `_155524`): the cockpit holo panels' first draw led Status.json's bit by 1.06, 0.98, 1.09 and 1.03 s, and the journal's Embark followed that draw by 13.7, 6.2, 4.5 and 4.3 s. In the four VR on-foot sessions of 10-24 and 10-25 (`_220128`, `_044101`, `_055612`, this one: 59 min on foot, the carrier's management screen and eight HMD camera resets at mid-foot transitions among them) no 30 s ui quality window counted a cockpit holo panel draw on foot, and in this log the family's first draw is the boarding's. Fixed here: the panels' first draw on foot is the edge, Status.json the backstop.
2. "Then it moves to the neck": the 0.5 s ramp of the 34.6 cm after the flag's fall. Fixed here.
3. "Too low and a reset HMD is required": the seated origin itself. The stored seat (0.055/0.436/-0.555/27.5, from an on-foot press at 12:06:54 UTC in the session before) was applied at the start (13:11:01, `intro_seat`); the pilot recentred in the menu at 13:11:07 (press seen, head y 0.256), which the seat memory passes through without storing (where unknown: `classifyReset` returns `PassThrough` before it looks at the press); the first on-foot entry (13:12:01, `transition_seat`) put the stored seat back. On foot the hold covered the 17 cm for 15 minutes; in the cockpit nothing does. Not an on-foot camera change. Fixed here by the pilot's decisions (2026-10-25): a recentre made in a menu or the cockpit is stored as the seat, a recentre on foot recentres on foot only, and boarding always puts the stored seat back.

ruled out: the journal's Embark as the early boarding edge, because it followed the cockpit holo panels' first draw by 4.3-13.7 s at all four boardings in the logs, later than Status.json's bit
ruled out: the HMD camera's reset (the transition flash event) or the avatar going quiet as the boarding edge, because both also happen at mid-foot transitions (10-25 04:55:25, 06:00:28 and 06:06:46 look like a boarding in the log)
ruled out: a late on-foot frame republishing after the edge, because the runtime's eye alignment stayed at serial 8622 and 0 m and its look compensation at 0 from 13:27:34.290 to the log's end (log edvr_gfx_20261025_071049)
ruled out: F109's runtime reset or the seat memory moving the cockpit origin at boarding, because the seat meter's origin read 0.055/0.436/-0.555/27.5 before (13:27:25.783) and after (13:27:32.813) the edge and no seat_reset ran until the pilot's press
ruled out: a flickering on-foot flag (which an instant zero would make visible), because 16 flights from 10-24 05:05 to 10-25 07:10 each show exactly one end of native stereo on foot

**The change.** One exit edge for the on-foot camera (`nofoot::f115::ExitEdge` over `nofoot::f115::CameraOnFoot`, native_on_foot_f115.h): the first frame the cockpit holo panels draw (vertex shader 1989E6D3B405FDE0, Elite's Disable GUI effects on, as the pilot flies; the HUD issuer probe in `beginPanelOverride` sees every VR-path draw) while native stereo is still on foot, or the flag's fall, whichever comes first. The panels' edge arms once the flag has been up 2 s with no panel drawn (a disembark's last cockpit frames end nothing), and panels that draw on foot and stop for 3 s with the flag still up are a false start (the camera changes resume, logged). The stock panel shader (GUI effects on) has no flight: it is counted on foot, not used, so those users end on the flag. No SRV boarding is in the logs: an SRV ends on the flag. `f115Tick` runs at the frame boundary before `adsAimTick` and `lookPublishTick` and sets `g_f115CameraOn`, which `adsAimTick`, `alignTick` and `rotCalTick` now take as "on foot"; at the edge `f115Exit` stops the head aim and look to aim (`adsStop`, so their lines keep the carried values), drops the map's seated yaw and pitch, always moves the reset serial, publishes the ADS pitch 0, the rotation calibration 0 and the left eye's share 0, zeroes the ADS position lock, restarts from zero the view run, the sight lock, the standing-height hold, the neck reference and the weapon eye's weight, and publishes a zero eye alignment under its own serial and a zero ADS shift. From that frame `alignTick` gates the eye alignment, the ADS shift and F74's world shift to exact zeros (`f115::gate`) until the camera is on foot again, so nothing ramps; the terms restart from zero at each entry too. No ramp is kept because nothing withholds or fades the view at that frame (the transition flash's two held frames are the HMD camera's reset, not the edge). The runtime (`lookPoll`): a reset serial now always puts the seated space back on its origin, not only while a compensation is left, so turns whose total came back to zero about a moving head leave nothing behind. No key.

**The seat (the pilot's decisions, 2026-10-25).** The seat comes only from a recentre in a menu or the cockpit, and boarding always returns to it. (1) `SeatMemory::classifyReset` (seat_memory.h) takes a press seen anywhere but on foot as `HonourPress` before its `PassThrough`: a recentre in a menu or a load is honoured and stored at once, as one aboard always was. (2) `kOnFootIsSeated = false`, the one-place switch the seat memory was built with for native on-foot VR: on foot a press, a game reset or an unobservable reset passes through (it recentres on foot only, nothing is stored), entering on foot applies nothing, and boarding is the transition that puts the stored seat back (`applyWanted` whenever the origin was moved on foot). The switch was chosen over a narrower change because each thing it does is one of the decisions; the one thing it would have dropped, a disembark taking back a player-looking recentre held for 5 s (the game's reset on the way out), is kept in `onContext`'s leave branch. A runtime recentre on foot (`seatProcessRuntimeRecentre`) recentres and is not stored either. The `seat_store` line names the press's place (`why=manual_reset_press_menu` or `_cockpit`). (3) One origin change at the edge: at the panels' edge the graphics half says "aboard" in the seat word from the next tick (`nativeOnFootBoardedEarly`, `seatContextPublish`), so the seat memory applies the seat at the edge, not with Status.json a second later; the runtime's look restore, eye alignment and pitches wait while a seat apply is due and until a frame answer newer than the apply arrives (`seatApplyAhead`), so the cockpit moves once, onto the seat, whatever order the seat word and the provider's zeros arrive in, and that move is the one `seat_reset` line.

**The instrument.** At the flag's fall, apart from the reset, `native on foot (F115): native stereo on foot ended at frame N`. The reset's line `boarding reset (F115): the on-foot camera ended at frame N (its source; the stock panel shader's draws on foot this stretch) ...` gives what was undone (the eye alignment with the hold's and the neck reference's raise, the look's carried yaw and the reset serial, the ADS pitch, the rotation, the ADS shift, the share), what was published at once, and how long before the avatar's last sample and the look's last input came. A second after the flag's fall `boarding reset (F115) 1 s: ...` names the edge's source and its lead over Status.json's bit, reads the values back from the provider (`nativeFrameOnFootWords`), says whether the runtime's pose carries the zero alignment (F89's serial), and gives the head's height against the stored seat (the seated origin once boarded) and its distance off it, and the seat: the player's last recentre in a menu or the cockpit this session and where (the graphics half's press count), or none, with the on-foot presses counted beside it. A false start has its own line. `--health` rule `boarding reset (F115)`: an exit with no reset line is NEVER APPLIED; anything not zero at the edge or a second later, a missing read-back, a pose that does not carry the zero alignment, a false start, or the head 10 cm or more from the stored seat is PARTIAL, the last named by where the seat came from (the player's recentre this session: the seat did not come back, or the player sits otherwise; none this session: the seat stored before it). Eight self-test cases.

**Rig.** native_frame_test (run115): the edges (one exit per fall, one entry per rise, a start on foot); the camera's state through `CameraOnFoot` (the boarding ends at the panels' first frame 0.98 s before the flag, the flag alone without panels, a disembark's last panel frames end nothing, a false start resumes 3 s after the last panel); the edge's shader against holo_material.h; the flight's 34.6 cm through the real hold and neck reference, an exact zero at the edge's frame, a quarter second and a second later and back in from zero on re-entry, against the 33e05706 build's ramp (over 15 cm a quarter second after); the read-back's zero test; the head against the seated origin (-17.8 cm a recentre's worth, 2 cm not); the provider's words read back. seat_memory_test (282 checks): the decision and press tables (on foot every reset passes through; a press in a menu is `HonourPress`); this flight's sequence (the old seat at the start, the menu press stored, a load's reset passing through, nothing applied on foot, a press there not stored, the boarding putting the menu seat back); boarding after an on-foot recentre returning to the stored seat; a disembark taking back a held aboard recentre; the transitions and the long story under the new rule. native_frame_test 973 checks. Both rigs compiled and run on their own on the branch, with the changed translation units compiled.

**Build.** Validated in the arc's combined build. **For the flight** (Epic; `--health` first): recentre once in the main menu, disembark, recentre once on foot, walk, board the ship last, sitting as in the cockpit. `boarding reset (F115)` OK: the edge from the cockpit's own panels about a second before Status.json's bit, the raise, the look and the pitch undone, all zero at the edge and a second later, the pose carries the zero alignment, the seat the player's menu recentre (on foot 1, not the seat), the head within 10 cm of the stored seat; the runtime log: `seat_store` with `why=manual_reset_press_menu`, the on-foot press `pass_through`, one `seat_reset` (`transition_seat`) at the boarding edge; the pilot: the cockpit appears at the seat with no slide and no recentre.

### 2026-10-25: F115b (an exit that is not a boarding)
**The flight.** F115 flew in aba55fce (v0.21.1-250, log `edvr_gfx_20261025_085120`, its runtime log `edvr_openxr_20261025_085122_102_18196`, Pimax Crystal Super on Pimax OpenXR, Epic). The pilot: "Did not board a ship this flight". `boarding reset (F115)` read PARTIAL: one boarding from Status.json, the eye alignment 11.1 cm undone (the neck reference 10.7, the hold 0.4), all zero a second later, the head +9.0 cm against the stored seat, "the runtime's pose did not carry the zero alignment".

**What the exit was.** A quit to the menu from the on-foot training. The session never had gameplay (`seat_context gameplay=0` throughout; the journal `Journal.2026-10-25T085129.01.log` holds only its Fileheader at 14:51:21Z, then Music and Shutdown at 15:01:54-56Z), native stereo on foot ran 08:54:09-09:01:25.894, and the game stopped submitting frames at 15:01:25.4Z, 0.5 s before the edge (the runtime's last head line 15:01:25.234, `flat_clear` from 15:01:26.465 until the shutdown at 15:01:47.930). No cockpit panel drew.

**Why the pose did not carry the zero.** No runtime frame came after the edge: the last frame input (runtime frame 48976, eye alignment serial 3831, -10.9 cm) was the one before it, so the zero (serial 3834) could not be carried. Not a gap in the publish path.

**The +9.0 cm.** That same last pose: its head is located in the seated space with the on-foot raise still folded into the origin, so it reads the raise over the head's real place (the seat meter 3 s before: -1.2 cm; -1.2 + 10.9 is about +9.7). The stored seat is this session's: the pilot's recentre in the menu at 14:53:46Z (`honour_press`, `seat_store why=manual_reset_press_menu`, F115's seat rule doing its job), and on foot the head stayed within 2-8 cm of it. Not a seat problem.

ruled out: a gap in the eye alignment's publish path as "the pose did not carry the zero alignment" in log edvr_gfx_20261025_085120, because the runtime handed no frame after the edge (its frames stopped at 15:01:25.4Z, the game quitting to the menu)

**The change.** The read-back now says what the exit was (`nofoot::f115::exitKind`): a boarding when the cockpit's own panels made the edge or drew after it, or Status.json says seated; otherwise "not a boarding (a quit, a load or a menu)". It records the runtime's frame sequence at the edge and says "no frame since the edge" when none came (`frameSinceEdge`), and then marks the head "not judged". `boarding reset (F115)` counts boardings and other exits apart: another exit's pose and seat are not judged, nor a boarding's with no frame since the edge; the zero read-back is still checked for every exit. F115's read-backs (no exit field) still parse, as boardings, so this flight's own log keeps its PARTIAL. No key.

**Rig.** native_frame_test (run115): the exit kinds (this flight's quit is neither, the panels at or after the edge and Status.json seated are boardings), no frame since the edge, the other exit's name. `edvr_log --health` self-test +3 cases (this flight's read-back as the new build would write it: OK with one other exit; a boarding with no frame since the edge; an F115 read-back without the field).

**Build.** Full `build.bat --wait-lock` green on the first pass, receipt `50ac4bcae35d...`, 245.2 s (native_frame_test 1015 checks). Not installed, not flown. **For the flight:** as F115's card; a quit from on foot now reads "1 other exit(s)", not PARTIAL.

### 2026-10-25: F118 (the reticle seen double; offline, not built)
The F113 flight (log `edvr_gfx_20261025_085120`, v0.21.1-250-gaba55fce, the right build, Epic, Pimax; look to aim followed the head in 193 of the 239 reticle seconds; no eye dump). The pilot: the reticle's depth was off, and sometimes it diverged (seen double). `reticle depth (F85c)` OK: 35627 of 35632 key 10 draws patched; 17807 readbacks (hit 15782, sky 1846, a surface under 0.5 m 1, off screen 178); refused 5 (no readback yet, at the start).

**What the lines show.** The reticle's depth is the left eye's depth at the one point under the aim line (the march), read back two frames later and smoothed in 1/D over 40 ms. The swing of a second is the disparity between its nearest and farthest target, 0.063 m x (1/D_min - 1/D_max). It passed 0.25 deg, beyond which the eyes must converge again or see the reticle double, in 32% of the seconds with look to aim following and 35% of the others. 18 seconds mixed hits with sky (the 50 m cap), all under look to aim, with a near object at the horizon: 08:54:31 from 3.39 m to 50 m, 26 of 89 readbacks sky; 08:54:37 from 2.97 m to 50 m. In those seconds the drawn D_f trailed the target by up to 38 m. 61 seconds jumped more than x2 between hits, crossing an edge. The flights before F113 show the same swing: 071049 in 18% of its look to aim seconds and 40% of the others (sky mixed in 58 s), 055612 in 16% (sky mixed in 9 s). What F113 changed for the reticle: on bare ground 071049 refused 2763 key 10 draws (no scene rows) and kept the game's fixed 5 m there, and now the reticle follows the ground.

ruled out: the eyes placing the reticle at different points, because the eyes' composite cameras (K) agree to 0.36 mm and 0.036 deg over the flight and both eyes draw one D_f a frame
ruled out: F113's rows reaching the reticle late or jittered, because the dispatch, K and the patch read the same rows of the same frame, those rows matched a scene mesh in all 823 checks (max diff 0), and the swing was as frequent before F113
ruled out: the player's own weapon, hand or body in the march, because a surface under 0.5 m came in 1 of 17807 readbacks and every hit under 1 m (8 s) is a walk up to a surface (08:58:06-16: 8 m to 0.81 m with the head under 30 deg/s, then the markers end)
ruled out: look to aim as the cause, because the swing is as frequent with it following (32% of the seconds) as without (35%); it puts the reticle where the pilot looks

**Not proven, and why no fix was built.** Two causes are left, and the 1 s line holds a second's minimum, maximum and counts, not the sequence, so it cannot tell them apart. (1) The edge: the point under the aim lies on a silhouette, and the reticle takes one side's depth (the near rock, or the sky) while the pilot looks at the other. The fix would take the depth from the reticle's footprint. (2) The change: the target flips between two depths, or the drawn depth trails a crossing by the two frames and the smoother, and each crossing asks for a vergence step that takes the eyes 150-200 ms. The fix would remove the latency (the depth placed on the GPU in the frame it is read) or the flips. A fix for one alone could leave the other.

**The next instrument (one flight; measure only).** A `reticle depth (F118) 1 s` line from f86Poll and the smoother: (1) the readback steps over 0.25 deg of disparity, split sky-hit and hit-hit, and the flips among them (a step undone within six readbacks); (2) the frames whose drawn D_f sits more than 0.25 deg from the newest target, and the longest such run in ms; (3) the reticle's footprint: four more lines of the same dispatch at +-0.6 deg about the aim line (the dispatch takes 32), and the readbacks whose five depths span more than 0.25 deg, with the centre on the far side. Flight (Epic, look to aim on, a weapon at the hip, 20 s a step): (i) the reticle held still on the edge of a rock against the sky 5-15 m away; (ii) swept slowly across that edge; (iii) held on flat ground 10-20 m away, then a slow nod; (iv) step (iii) with look to aim off. The pilot says which steps looked double. Double in (i), with edge readbacks and few steps: the footprint. Double in (ii) or (iii), with flips or trailing frames: the change.

### 2026-10-25: F118 instrument (built, measure only)
Built as described above, on `claude/onfoot-reticle-depth` (from aba55fce). Nothing that is drawn changes: the reticle's target, D_f and the patch are F85c's as before.

**The parts** (`nofoot::f118`, native_on_foot_f118.h). Disparities are stated at a nominal 63 mm IPD (0.063 m x |1/D_a - 1/D_b| in degrees), and a step is a change over 0.25 deg. `Steps` takes each hit or sky readback's target in order; a surface under 0.5 m or a line off the screen leaves F85c's target alone and is not fed. A step is sky-hit when one side is the sky (the 50 m cap) and hit-hit otherwise. A flip is a step whose target comes back within 0.1 deg of the depth before it within six readbacks. `Trail` takes each frame's D_f against the newest target: the frames over 0.25 deg, and the longest run in ms (a run carries over the second's end). The footprint: in f85cReticle's eye 0 draw, `ringDirs` turns the aim line u by 0.6 deg toward K's right and up (its x and y columns, made orthonormal across u), and toward left and down. f86Dispatch adds the four as lines after every consumer's, from line 0's origin over line 0's range, all four or none, so they never displace a weapon part's or the floor probe's line. f86Poll decodes them with line 0 (`footprint`): when all five give a depth, the span between the nearest and the farthest, and whether the centre is on the far side (a ring line found a surface more than 0.25 deg nearer).

**The line.** After F85c's 1 s line: `reticle depth (F118) 1 s: readbacks N (hit or sky); steps over 0.25 deg N (sky-hit N, hit-hit N), flips N, largest step D deg; drawn more than 0.25 deg from the target in N of N frames, longest run N ms, worst D deg; footprint (+-0.6 deg) read N, over a depth edge N (the centre on the far side N), largest span D deg, incomplete N, not dispatched N; at an IPD of 63 mm`. The `--health` rule `reticle depth (F118)` counts edge seconds (at least 4 footprints read, a quarter or more over an edge, at most 2 steps) and speed seconds (a flip, or a trailing run of 50 ms or more). The leading cause is the kind with more seconds (or both, or neither), and the rule gives the first time of each. Readbacks with no footprint read is PARTIAL. Five self-test cases.

**Rig.** native_frame_test (run118) checks:
- the disparity: 10 m against 50 m is 0.289 deg, 3 m against it 1.131 deg;
- 14 readbacks giving 4 steps (sky-hit 2, hit-hit 2) and one flip; a step back after the window is no flip; a flip-flop gives 4 steps and 3 flips; a drift inside the limit gives none;
- 4 of 5 frames trailing, with a 34 ms run carried over the second's end;
- the ring lines are unit and 0.6 deg off u from scaled and skewed axes, and an axis along u is refused;
- the footprint decoded from lines marched by the CPU procedure the shader runs, over a depth image with a 3 m surface's edge one pixel left of the aim (the centre on the sky, the left ring line at 3 m: 1.13 deg, the centre on the far side), over a wall at 10 m (under 0.01 deg), and with a line off the screen (incomplete).

**For the flight** (Epic; `--health` first; look to aim on, a weapon at the hip, 20 s a step, the clock time of each step noted):
1. Hold the reticle still on the edge of a rock against the sky, 5-15 m away.
2. Sweep it slowly across that edge.
3. Hold it on flat ground 10-20 m away, then nod slowly.
4. Step 3 again with look to aim off.

The pilot says which steps looked double. Expect `reticle depth (F118)` OK with its leading cause. In the 1 s lines, step 1 should show footprints over an edge with few steps, step 2 sky-hit steps, and step 3 few of either. Double in step 1 with that pattern is the edge, and the fix takes the depth from the footprint. Double in step 2 or 3 with flips or trailing runs is the speed, and the fix removes the latency or the flips.

### 2026-10-25: F109c (look to aim at the Arc Cutter: the gain from the game's own ends; one pitch account)
The F109b flight: log `edvr_gfx_20261025_085120`, v0.21.1-250-gaba55fce (the right build), Epic, Pimax Crystal Super, look to aim on. The pilot: "look to aim failed while trying to use the cutting tool and locked me in a weird position". `--health`: `look to aim (F109)` OK (203 s engaged, the head 2288.6 deg, applied 2135.3, guard trips 0, new bases 19), `snap turn (F109)` OK (19 flicks exact).

**The cutter.** The held items: the Energylink (`$humanoid_rechargetool_name;`) 08:54:25-08:56:49, the Arc Cutter (`$humanoid_repairtool_name;`) 08:56:49-08:57:45 and again 08:59:07-08:59:26 (look to aim off by then). With the cutter drawn, look to aim followed normally for 20 s (08:56:49-08:57:08: the head's turn applied, the reported head within 1.2 deg of the aim, the gain 1.00000). Then:
- 08:57:09.435-.769: the game blocked the look three times (blocked calls 21 to 28).
- The gain on the 1 s lines: yaw -405.42361 and pitch 741.12622 at 08:57:09, 0.97040 and 22.21323 at 08:57:10. In the flight's other 201 seconds it read 1.00000 at the hip, 0.85335 to 0.94379 in ADS, and 0 once before any was measured. There was no stick and no spring (spring calls 0), so the delta held a term of the game's own, and F109's window (1e-3 to 1e3) took that ratio as the gain.
- 08:57:10-11: the asked pitch was -18.52 and then -109.95, the applied +2.53 and then +39.69. The aim's pitch (the FP root, F98a's line) went from -20.6 to +85.0 and back to -13.6.
- 08:57:11: the counted pitch summed +39.69 while the map's carried pitch went from -18.06 to -38.55. The +-60 clamp had dropped 60.18 deg: 25 deg of turn the aim took (to +85), and 35 counted past it (a count of +120 deg is past any pitch).
- 08:57:12: applied -21.45, the aim -13.6 to -35.0 (the same 21.4), the carried pitch at -60.
- 08:57:13-32: the aim's pitch was -35.0 at its min and its max for 20 s, a value it reached nowhere else in the flight. The carried pitch was -60 and the asked pitch 0.00 in 18 of the 20 s while the head pitched 202.2 deg. The reported head stood 4-61 deg above the aim, and the chest leant 25-38 deg.
- 08:57:33: the pilot turned the key off. The unwind injected +60 over 1 s, and the aim went from -35.0 to +25.0 (+4.7 at two thirds) while "the view did not move".

**The answers.**
- What the game does with the look while cutting: it blocked the look briefly (three episodes, 11 blocked calls in that second), and for about a second it added a term of its own to the delta (the gains above). No springs ran. The aim has a pitch ceiling (+85), and the processor's delta is counted past it. The cutter has no pitch floor at -35: that was look to aim's own limit, -60 on an account 25 deg below the aim.
- What look to aim did: it took those ratios as its gain and divided its asks by them (the input queue is capped at 20 deg over the gain, so a gain of 0.002 lets 1000 deg through). The aim went to +85; what drove it there is not in the 1 s lines, which do not log the sub-second gains. The map's clamp kept 60 deg of the count and the follower kept all of it, so from 08:57:12 the follower asked down and the map refused.
- "Locked me in a weird position" was both. The body: the aim and the cutter were held at -35 while the head stood 4-61 deg above them, the chest leant 25-38 deg. The view: 25 deg above the head, because the account was 25 deg below the aim (the toggle's unwind took the aim to +25 with the view unmoved).
- Why 2135.3 of 2288.6 deg was applied: 180.2 deg short in the 20 s lock (177.8 of it pitch), 42.1 deg over in the 4 s of the start (the swing), and 15.3 short over the other 179 s (0.8%: the blocked calls and the follower's lag).

ruled out: an Arc Cutter pitch floor as the -35 deg hold, because the toggle's unwind took the aim from -35.0 to +25.0, exactly the account's 60 deg, and the account had parted from the aim by 25 deg in the +85 swing
ruled out: the springs as the game's term, because spring calls were 0 throughout the flight

The guard read 4.1-6.0 deg through the swing and at most 5.3 after it (16.4 in one second), and never tripped. Why the 25 deg did not show is open: a view step over 15 deg in a tick takes a new base, and the look to aim line does not count those.

**The fix (F109c).**
1. The gain only between the game's own ends. The processor hook reads comp+0x808 / +0x80C each call (the RE's hip and ADS ends of the one linear gain). A clean call whose delta over its input is outside them (5% either side, or of the other sign) is foreign: no gain is taken from it, and it is counted. Its delta stays the head aim's (F109's rule: the cancel holds the view, the follower brings the aim back, now with a sane gain). With the ends unread, F109's window applies.
2. One pitch account. AdsAimMap's carried pitch is exact, and only its publication is held to +-60 (the asks stay inside +-60 through adsPitchLimit). F68a clamped the account itself, so turn the game made past 60 was dropped from it for good while the follower kept it.
3. The instrument. The look to aim 1 s line ends with the gain's ends, the foreign calls, and the aim's pitch (the FP root, from the pin hook) against the carried pitch: the change in their difference since the engage. `look to aim (F109)` reports those. It reads PARTIAL when that drift is 5 deg or more in 3 seconds, and when the reported head stands 10 deg or more off the aim for 3 seconds in a row. The old rule judged only the still seconds and passed this flight: re-run on it, the new rule names a 13 s run.

**Open.** A pitch the game stops at its ceiling is still counted whole, so the exact account would sit above the aim by the excess; the drift names it. A fix would take the applied pitch from the aim itself; not built.

**Rig.** native_frame_test +2 (run109):
- the split with the ends read (1.0, 0.85335) takes the hip and the ADS gain, and refuses the flight's 741.1, -405.4 and 22.2, a 0.002 and a sign flip, while F109's window took 741; a 0.002 gain sends a 2 deg ask as 1000 deg of input;
- a turn of the game's own past 75 deg is carried whole with the publication held to 60, the follower's sum equals the map's account, and the aim comes back and follows the head 30 deg down; F68a's clamped account, computed alongside, is left as far from the aim as the turn went past 60.

edvr_log self-test: +2.

**For the flight** (Epic; `--health` first): look to aim on, the Arc Cutter on a panel, looking down and up while cutting. Expect `look to aim (F109)` with no "off the head for" or "parted" note, the gain's ends 1.00000 0.85335, and the foreign calls counted; the pilot: the cutter where he looks and the view his own.

**Build.** Full `build.bat --wait-lock` green, receipt `71e60a46c9ff...`, native_frame_test 1015 checks, commit 2a45847b. Not installed, not flown.
