- On the one panel owned by 0x4526E40 (09:01:20 to 09:01:26) it followed the uv in the pick's frame, in the owner's axes and for the eye (+0.94 to +0.99 each). That panel's pick camera agreed with the eye (+1.00 on all three axes, orthogonality 0.000), and the sprite as the eye sees it followed the mouse.
- So the turn is in the 0x47299F0 class's pick mesh, not in the pick camera or the eye.

**Read** (build 334925, capstone; not filed separately). 0x47299F0 builds its owner's transform in a camera's frame from the rows at [[owner+0x1B8]]+0xA0 to +0xD0. With the flag at +0x1C0 set, it scales the position's x and y and the scale (+0x50) by f(b/2)/f(a/2), f being 0x14055FF00 (INFERRED: a tangent): a is a float at +0x17C of the object [owner+8] returns at vtable +0xE8, b the float at +0x260 of the camera its vtable +0x28 returns. INFERRED: a negative angle there (an HMD sentinel) would turn such a panel 180 degrees in x and y. That was not measured, so the fix does not depend on it.

ruled out: the pick camera as the turn, because on the upright panel the camera derived from the owner transform agreed with the eye (+1.00, +1.00, +1.00) and the turn is per panel class (0x47299F0 turned, 0x4526E40 upright) in one session

**The fix.** After a 2D placement (the panel's window ran and the sprite is placed), EDVR reads the panel's pick triangles (panel +0x460: triangles at +0x18, count at +0x20, 0x60 bytes each with three vertices in the pick's frame and their uvs at +0x40). It finds the triangle holding the uv the game's way (0x452EC00: barycentric in uv), checks that the game's sprite is that point (1 cm), and reads from the triangle whether the mesh runs u along -x and v along +y in the pick's frame. An upright panel faces the camera with u along +x and v along -y. Only a turned panel's cursor is moved: the controller's sprite position (+0x140) and nothing else, so the clicks keep the true uv. Where it goes is the TEMPORARY live key `fix.native_on_foot_panel_cursor_fix` (menu "Panel cursor (test)"):
- `panel` (default): the mesh's point at (1 - u, 1 - v), which is the uv's place on the panel as drawn when the turned mesh lies where the drawn panel is. F114's fit put it straight ahead at 0.65 m with the drawn panel's angular size.
- `view`: the sprite mirrored through the view's centre (x and y negated), right if the mesh was turned about the view axis instead.
- `game`: the game's own place.

The flat profile is never moved. Lines `panel cursor fix (F117) 1 s` (and every 10 s `so far`) and a change line when the key moves; rule `panel cursor fix (F117)`, per setting:
- 2D placements, turned and upright, the cursor moved;
- refusals: no triangle at the uv, the sprite not at the uv, no triangle at the turned uv;
- whether the cursor on turned panels follows the true uv or moves against it (the uv against the cursor's place as drawn, after the setting).

It reads NEVER APPLIED when a moving setting met turned panels and moved none, and PARTIAL when the cursor still went against the uv. F111 and F114b's lines read the sprite after the fix, so their turn verdict reads "none" under `panel`.

**Rig.** native_frame_test +6 (run117), on a curved panel built as a pick mesh, upright or turned about its middle:
- the barycentric point and the turn read from a triangle;
- an upright panel left alone;
- `panel` lands on the uv's drawn place;
- `view` mirrors the cursor, and `game` leaves it in place but counts the panel as turned;
- the guards: the sprite 5 cm off, no triangle, a uv past the edge clamped;
- over a mouse path, `panel`'s cursor follows the uv and `game`'s moves against it.

hotkey_capture_test counts the Native on foot page at 40 rows; `edvr_log --health` self-test +4 cases.

**Build.** Full `build.bat --wait-lock` green on the third pass (the first two: the lock wait timed out behind other worktrees' builds; then the rig's local `far`, a Windows macro, renamed), receipt `354cd3e7b444...`, 212.6 s. Not installed, not flown.

**For the flight** (Epic; `--health` first). At a locker with the inventory open: move the mouse over the rows, click two rows, then switch "Panel cursor (test)" to `view`, then to `game`, repeating the same moves and clicks each time. `panel cursor fix (F117)`: under the setting the pilot prefers, the cursor follows the uv on turned panels, and the pilot's clicks land on the row under the cursor.

### 2026-10-25: F115c (an exit told apart at the edge)
**The flight.** Log `edvr_gfx_20261025_113157` (v0.21.1-261-gc53b06df, the right build): a quit from on foot. The journal has Shutdown and no Embark. Native stereo on foot ended at 11:38:19.215 (frame 37126) with the game session ended, the eye submits stopped at 11:38:20.760, and no tick came after the edge. F115b classes an exit only from the read-back a second later, so this quit had none, and `boarding reset (F115)` counted it as a boarding with no read-back and read PARTIAL.

ruled out: a missing read-back after a quit as a publish fault, because the game stopped presenting 1.5 s after the edge

**The change.** Health classification only; nothing the player sees changes. `nofoot::f115::exitAtEdge(fromPanels, statusSeated, session)` says what the edge can tell: the cockpit's panels or Status.json's seated flag make a boarding, a game session that has ended makes another exit ("not a boarding (the game session ended)"), and anything else is `kUnknown` ("not yet known (read back a second later)"). The edge line ends with `; the exit at the edge: ...`. `edvr_log --health` pairs each edge with the next read-back (after the edge, before the next edge) and takes an exit's kind from the read-back, else the edge, else unknown. Boardings, other exits and unknown exits are counted apart. An exit with no read-back is PARTIAL only when it is a boarding; for the others it is reported.

**Rig.** native_frame_test (run115): `exitAtEdge` for this quit, a seated flag, the panels and an exit still in session, and the two names. `edvr_log --health` self-test +8 cases: a quit with no read-back is OK with "0 boarding(s) and 1 other exit(s)"; a seated boarding edge with none is PARTIAL; an unknown exit is reported; the read-back over the edge; two pairing cases; the F115b edge line without the new field, with and without a read-back.

### 2026-10-25: F120 (the panel cursor stays on the panel when the head turns)
F117 put the cursor at the true uv on the turned panels and the clicks always landed there. What was left: the cursor rides with the head.

**The diagnosis.**
- The mouse sets a uv through the cursor window (FUN_144541A20), and that uv ignores the head: with the mouse still it drifted 0 per degree of head turn (log `edvr_gfx_20261025_113157`).
- The game places a cursor sprite from the uv on the panel's pick mesh and writes the sprite's position at the controller +0x140. That position is in the pick camera's frame, and the pick camera follows the head (it matches the eye at +1.00 on all three axes, F114b).
- The drawn panel stays in the HUD canvas's frame (the HRC matrix at +0x430). On these screen-space panels the pick mesh is camera-locked, so a uv that stays puts the sprite where the head points, and the panel stays behind.
- Read (build 334925, capstone, this session): 0x47299F0 leaves at once when the qword `[owner+0x1B0]` is 0, takes `rdx = [[owner+0x1B8]]`, leaves too when the byte `[rdx+0x90]` is 0, and with the byte `[rdx+0x1C0]` set takes the branch that reads the camera's rows and scales by the ratio of two tangents (F117's entry). Its first 16 bytes are `4C 8B DC 49 89 5B 18 57 48 81 EC 40 01 00 00 41`.

**The fix.** In `f111PlaceHooked`, after the game's placement and F117's decision, one write of the sprite position (+0x140, three floats) replaces F117's own write. Clicks keep the true uv: the cursor window's output and the NDC (+0x84/+0x88) are never written.
- *Which panels.* Screen-space panels only: the pick mesh owner's vtable +0x10 is exe+0x47299F0 with its first 16 bytes equal to the 334925 pin, `[owner+0x1B0]` > 0, and the byte at `[[owner+0x1B8]]+0x1C0` set. The `[rdx+0x90]` byte is not part of the test.
- *Inputs.* E: the eye's view rows from `f114bEyeView` (view 2), which share the camera's world space. H: the HRC matrix's rows 0..2 at `g_f12Hrc+0x430`, each normalised (it carries the HUD scale).
- *The correction.* The reference pair (E0, H0) is taken at the first screen-space 2D placement after 30 placement-free frames, which is a panel opening. At each placement p' = E Ht H0 E0t p, with p the game's sprite or F117's point where F117 moved it. Nothing moved gives the identity; a head turn with the HUD still counter-rotates p; the head and the HUD turning together leave p alone. The reference drops after 30 frames without a placement, or when the frame counter goes backwards.
- *Refusals, each counted:* flat profile; no eye view; no HRC matrix; a degenerate row (a zero row, or rows leaning more than 0.05 off orthogonal); not screen-space; owner bytes not pinned; the setting is `head`; the write failed. F117's key stays as it is: orientation first, then this rotation. F117's own statistics read its place before the rotation.

The key is the TEMPORARY live `fix.native_on_foot_panel_cursor_follow` (menu "Panel cursor follows (test)", Native on foot page): `panel` (default) or `head` (the game's place). Under `head` the readings below are still taken, so the drift the correction removes is on record.

Limits:
- The rotation is about the camera's origin, so the 7-29 cm between the HUD frame's origin and the eye is ignored (about 3 deg at a 20 deg head turn).
- The reference assumes the cursor sits right when the panel opens.
- E comes from the last HUD submit's view rows (the render side), H from the placement's read, so they can differ by a frame in a fast turn (an estimate, not measured: 100 deg/s at 90 Hz is about 1 deg, 1 cm of cursor at 0.65 m).

ruled out: rewriting the NDC (+0x84/+0x88) as the fix, because the uv already ignores the head (0 drift per degree in log edvr_gfx_20261025_113157)

**Lines and rule.** `panel cursor follow (F120) 1 s` once a second with a 2D placement, and every 10 such seconds with a screen-space panel `so far`; a change line when the key moves; one line saying whether the owner function's bytes match the pin. The 1 s line carries:
- the setting, the 2D and screen-space placements, the corrections, the references taken and each refusal;
- the head's turn this second (E), the HUD frame's (H) and the head against the HUD frame (E Ht), in degrees, and a sentence on the HUD frame;
- E Ht's yaw, pitch and roll and its determinant at the last placement (the validity reading);
- while the mouse was still (the same uv on the same panel in consecutive placements): the placements, the head's turn against the HUD frame, and the cursor's drift on the panel in mm (q = H Et p', the HUD frame's own coordinates).

If the HRC frame turns with the head (E Ht constant), the correction is near zero, and the sentence says so: the HUD frame turns with the head, so a panel seen to hold still is not in the HRC frame. With `fix.native_on_foot_hud_follow = head` (EDVR turns the HUD with the head) the same reading is expected, and the correct result there is a correction near zero.

`--health` rule `panel cursor follow (F120)`, a second being judged when the mouse was still and the head turned more than 5 deg against the HUD frame:
- OK: under `panel` most judged seconds drifted under 5 mm;
- PARTIAL: most drifted 5 mm or more, or the HRC frame turned with the head in every judged second (the drift cannot then tell);
- NEVER APPLIED: `panel` met screen-space placements and corrected none;
- IDLE: no screen-space panel, or no second to judge.

Under `head` the drift is expected at roughly distance x angle, about 11 cm per 10 deg at 0.65 m.

**Rig.** native_frame_test +13 (run120, `f120_checks.h`):
- nothing moved gives M = I (11 placements, one reference, the write skipped);
- a head turn of 5 to 40 deg with the HUD fixed keeps the written sprite's world point within 1e-9;
- the head and the HUD turned together give M = I;
- it composes with F117 (M on F117's panel point, not on the game's sprite; one final write; `head` leaves F117's point alone);
- the reference holds across 29 placement-free frames and drops after 30; a second panel in a frame keeps it; a frame counter going backwards drops it;
- the screen-space test and the pin (one differing byte fails it);
- each refusal counted apart, and only screen-space placements counted as such;
- a failed write counted as a refusal;
- the drift: under 1e-6 mm with `panel`, 113 mm with `head` for 10 deg at 0.65 m, none for a moving mouse or a HUD turning with the head; the sentences about the HUD frame; yaw, pitch and roll read back; merged seconds.

hotkey_capture_test counts the Native on foot page at 41 rows; `edvr_log --health` self-test +8 cases.

**Build.** Full `build.bat --wait-lock` green on the first pass, receipt `8896b466bae9...`, 201.5 s; native_frame_test 1047 checks, 0 failures. Not installed, not flown.

**For the flight** (Epic; `--health` first). At a locker with a panel open: turn the head 20 deg left and 20 deg right with the mouse still, then click a row; then switch "Panel cursor follows (test)" to `head` and repeat. `panel cursor follow (F120)`: under `panel` the mouse-still seconds with a head turn read a drift under 5 mm and the cursor stays on its row; under `head` they read a drift of a few centimetres. The line's `E.Ht` and the HUD frame sentence say whether the HRC frame held still.

### 2026-10-25: F121 (the helmet visor centred on each eye's axis)
**The report.** The pilot, native on foot on the Pimax Crystal Super (Epic, v0.21.1-261-gc53b06df, log `edvr_gfx_20261025_113157`): "the shaders inside the helmet (breath fog for example) are double rendered, anything we can do to clean this up? I'm thinking like cutting it in half and showing it appropriately in each eye." The eye dumps: 113657139001 shows the breath fog (a soft disc at the lower centre, median 32 of 255 in both eyes), 113736427002 shows it under the inventory panel (31), 113804916003 none (between breaths). The fog is already in the pre-UI DLSS images (`P*.bmp`), so it is a scene effect and not the UI layer's.

**The draw.** One draw makes every helmet-glass effect on foot: VS B553BB479B7C0B97 and PS 68ABCB9FEF6CA66C (F25-F27), a 3-vertex fullscreen triangle per eye, the last draw of each eye's HDR scene pass (R11G11B10, 2016x2017), before the tonemap and DLSS, with dual-source blending (add, and multiply the destination by the tint).
- Inputs (disassembled from `edvr_logs\shaders`): t0 the exposure (6x1), t1 a copy of the scene colour (the refraction, read at the pixel's own position), t2 BC4 1024, t3 BC5 512 (the edge lines), t4 BC7 1024 (a normal map and mask).
- It draws the RemLok edge lines, the condensation and the visor's curvature, the tint, and the breath fog: a radial mask centred at the visor frame's (0, -0.5), image uv (0.5, 0.75), which is where the disc is. All of it but the edge lines and the scene sample is built from the vertex shader's interpolated uv (`o1`); the edge lines and the refracted scene use SV_POSITION.
- The identification rests on the shader's mask maths and the disc's place, not on suppressing the draw. `remlok_lines = hide` on one flight would show the fog go with it.

**The numbers** (dumps of the flight above; `d` = xR - xL on the 4032x4034 final images, F104's patch match):
- The fog disc: d = -0.2 px (NCC 0.98; the high-passed mottle 0.89) in dump 1, 0.0 px in dump 2; equal brightness in both eyes, so the draw's constants are the same in both.
- The far field: d = -720 px in seven of ten dumps tried (-720 to -723), which is 2 x 0.1784 x 2016 from the projection's own offset (the runtime log: m02 -0.1784 / +0.1784, tangents outer 1.2546, inner 0.8746). Infinity is at -720 on this headset, not 0.
- The HUD and panels: -840 to -888 px, about 0.7-0.9 m at an assumed IPD of 63 mm.

**The cause.** The visor pass is built for a monitor, where the image centre is straight ahead. Each eye's straight ahead is 0.1784 NDC toward its nose, so the same pixels are two directions: the left eye sees the disc 10.9 degrees temporal of straight ahead, the right eye 10.6 degrees, and the disc (radius 24 degrees, centred 28 degrees below the axis) is seen as two discs 21.5 degrees apart: 720 px beyond infinity, which the eyes cannot fuse. Identical pixels are not infinity here; identical angles are. It is the mechanism `docs\remlok-lines.md` found for the edge lines (the nasal line 14 degrees from its twin), and the fog, the condensation and the curvature have it too.

ruled out: the halves idea (cut the fog in two, each eye its own half, offset as for a visor at its real distance), because a visor 2.5-10 cm from the eye is 35-100 degrees of binocular disparity against about 1 degree that fuses, so nothing on the glass can fuse and each half would land at its eye's nasal edge, mostly past the 41-degree frustum, and the fog would all but vanish; halves joined at the midline at zero angular disparity do not double but are monocular (rivalry, half the contrast, a seam)
ruled out: drawing the fog identically in both eyes as the way to put it at infinity, because identical pixels are 720 px beyond infinity on this headset (d = -0.2 px against -720 px)
ruled out: a difference between the eyes' constants as the cause, because the disc has the same median (32.0) in both eyes and d = -0.2 px

**The change.** `src\d3d11\visor_axis_vs.h`: a replacement for the game's vertex shader, transcribed from its disassembly (signatures and declarations equal, ours the one added b3, one float4), identical but the interpolated uv `o1.x` is moved by s. For the left eye s = +a/2 and for the right -a/2, with a = (outer - inner) / (outer + inner) from `eyeTangents()` (the axis in NDC from the image centre: the Crystal Super 0.1784, s +/-0.0892; a symmetric headset 0, and then nothing is bound). The pixel at NDC x = a (the left eye's axis) then has uv 0.5, the visor frame's centre. `remlok_fix.cpp`: `visorSwapBegin` binds the shader and its b3 around the game's visor draw (the F27 plumbing: the eye from the filing, outer mode, on foot) and `visorSwapEnd` puts the game's shader and b3 back. No key: a correction. It refuses, counts and logs once per reason when the eye is not known, the tangents are not published (or not ones it was written for: an axis past 0.6 NDC), the bound pixel shader is not 68ABCB9FEF6CA66C, or the replacement could not be made; the draw then runs the game's own shader. `stock` leaves the visor as the game draws it, `hide` removes it.
- The fog sits at infinity along each eye's axis (d = -720). Near gaze doubles its soft edge by IPD / distance (4.5 degrees at 0.8 m); a depth term (+/-(IPD/2) x f / Z: 60 px of 4032 at 1 m, 30 at 2 m) is a one-line addition if the pilot finds the haze too far.
- Lines: `visor axis (F121): armed` once; `visor axis (F121): the visor frame is centred ...` when s is first used or moves; `visor axis (F121): NOT shifted -- <why>` once per reason; every 30 s of visor draws `visor axis (F121) 30 s: visor draws seen N (left, right), shifted N (left, right), symmetric N, refused N (by reason); s left, right from the tangents outer, inner`. Rule `visor axis (F121)`: OK when both eyes' draws were shifted and s matches the tangents (or a symmetric frustum needed nothing); NEVER APPLIED when visor draws were seen and none was shifted; PARTIAL for one eye only, an s that does not match the tangents, or a fifth of the draws refused; IDLE when armed with no visor draw; no line at all is a stale DLL or `remlok_lines` not outer.

**The sign check** (before relying on the per-eye assignment). The eye filing's eye 0 is the left eye: F27's left PS variant (byte 0x41) is bound to it and the dump's left image shows only the left edge line; its projection is m02 -0.1784, so its axis is right of centre (+0.1784 NDC). In dump 113657139001 the left disc's centre is at pixel 2010.4 of 4032 and the right's at 2011.9. With s = +0.0892 the left frame moves right by 359.6 px (to 2370) and with s = -0.0892 the right moves left by 359.6 (to 1652.3): d = 1652.3 - 2370 = -717.7, the far field's -720, the disc on each eye's axis. The rig makes the same check on the shipped bytes (below).

**Rig.** `tools\visor_axis_test` (V1-V8, 39 checks, WARP with the debug layer, stream output) against the game's own bytecode (`fixtures\vs_B553BB479B7C0B97.dxbc`, held to its hash name):
- the signatures and every dcl line equal;
- 48 random constant sets (the tint, the slide, the colour buffer, the exposure): at s = 0 every output equals the game's (the uv and the position bit for bit); at s = 0.0892, -0.0892 and 0.31 only `o1.x` moves, by exactly s; a control shows the strict comparison sees the shift;
- the sign per eye from the production math and the dump's tangents: the left frame's centre (the pixel whose uv is 0.5) lands at NDC +a, the right's at -a, 719.5 px apart on 4032; the CPU model of the uv matches;
- a symmetric frustum gives exactly 0 (no negative zero), and the shipped shader is then bit for bit the game's; the math refuses non-finite and non-positive tangents, an axis past 0.6, an eye other than 0 and 1;
- the wiring scans: the shipped bytes are the ones `remlok_fix.cpp` creates, bound once and put back once, another pixel shader refused, no key.
`temporal_shader_build --self-test` holds the shader's contract (symbol, source, `vs_5_0`, b1[91], b2[2], b3[1], t0). `edvr_log --health` self-test +11 cases for the rule.

**Build.** Full `build.bat --wait-lock` green, receipt `2dd1b3e83efc...`, 166.4 s (v0.21.1-263-g4c450f6c, dirty until committed). Not installed, not flown.

**For the flight** (Epic, the Crystal Super; `--health` first). On foot with the visor down, in the cold and airless (the first flight's fog was at 132 K, 0.17 g), breathing until the fog shows. `visor axis (F121)` should read OK with s left +0.0892, right -0.0892 against outer 1.255, inner 0.875. Take an eye dump while the fog is visible: the fog disc's patch match (the F104 method, d = xR - xL) should read about -720 px at 4032, the same as the far field (it read -0.2). The pilot: one fog, not two, at a distance; the edge lines at the temples as before; looking at the weapon or a near panel, a soft doubled fog edge (4-9 degrees) is expected. If the fog is still double: `--health` says NEVER APPLIED (read why), or the line is absent (a stale DLL, or `remlok_lines` not outer), or the fog is another draw and one `remlok_lines = hide` pass tells which. Also: turn the head fast; a ghost of the fog (DLSS carries it with the world's motion vectors) is untested.

**Open: the right eye's nasal edge line.** In all three dumps the right eye keeps the line at its left edge at full strength (the mean of the 100 brightest columns in the left 700 px of the right image: 14.1, 14.5, 14.9, against 14.0-14.4 for the left eye's own temple line and 0.1-3.9 for the left eye's nasal side), although F27's right-eye variant (byte 1724 0x01, edge weight 0 for x < 0.3) is logged bound every frame (right eye 2266 per 30 s, no refusal after the first 70). The line is 11 degrees from the left eye's temple line (the right eye's nasal edge at -39 degrees against the left eye's temple at -50), a second double at the left edge. Not fixed here: the cause is not clear. Discriminators: one `remlok_lines = hide` pass (a line that survives is not this draw), and `remlok_swap_eyes = 1` (the F27 control) on a dump.

### 2026-10-25: F119 (head containment, Phase 0: measure)
Branch `claude/onfoot-head-containment` from c53b06df. Measure only: nothing the player sees changes.

**The feature this measures.** On foot the game's collision keeps the commander's head out of walls. EDVR adds the player's physical head translation on top of the game's camera: the eye is the camera plus the head's offset from its rest point, the seated origin the last recentre set. Leaning therefore pushes the eye through a wall, a PvP cheat. The design the pilot approved, for two later phases:
- Phase 1, a leash. Past a soft radius from the rest point the view fades toward black. Past a hard radius for about 0.3 s the position is recentred, never the yaw.
- Phase 2, wall contact. When world geometry fills much of an eye's view at near-zero depth, the view goes black at once, and the position is recentred if that persists.
- No user key, native on foot only, and normal play must never trigger either.
Phase 0 gives the numbers that set the radii and the contact threshold in one flight.

**1. The head's offset from the rest point** (`f119Tick`, once a frame in alignTick). The pose the runtime hands the d3d11 half (`np.render`) is the head in the seated space with EDVR's eye alignment applied. The physical head is that pose plus the alignment it carried, found by the serial the runtime reported with it (F89's rule; `nofoot::f119::AlignHistory3` keeps all three axes where F89's history keeps y; F38's `alignHeadTrue` and F87h's seat meter take the head the same way). The seated space is the runtime's, held on the body's heading (F40, psi 0): right is +x, up +y, forward -z. Kept for each frame: the horizontal distance (what pushes an eye through a wall), right, forward and up.
- Classes: the stance (the pin's crouch weight against its standing calibration, published by the Animate post-hook; unknown without the calibration or when older than a second), the item (a weapon when Status.json names a `$wpn_` item or F83's native primary is selected, a tool when anything else is drawn, nothing otherwise: F91's ADS item gate), and ADS.
- EDVR's own eye offsets are logged apart and are not in the head offset: the alignment as published (horizontal max, up range) and its terms (the ADS lock and sight lock F70/F93, the weapon eye offset F88, the view offset F74, the neck reference's raise F94a/F98c, the standing-height hold F87h).
- A move of the rest point on foot (the runtime's reference generation) logs the head's offset from the old one just before it.
- A frame is not sampled at the boarding edge (F115), in the game's third-person camera, with no pose, or when the applied alignment's serial has left the history; the line counts them.

**2. How close world geometry gets to each eye** (`f44::f119Boundary`, at the Present boundary after alignTick). The eye's rows come from the depth prepass or whichever F113 source drew (VS F516BF0201303B87 / PS B40B0462256E31C2); they give the depth fit (A, B) and the near plane (B). The depth read is the eye's scene depth texture of the frame that ended, not the prepass alone: a prepass-only read would need a dispatch in the middle of the frame, and the final depth holds the same world. One dispatch per eye (`head_containment_shader.h`, 64 threads, a cell each) takes the nearest view depth over 8 x 8 taps in each of 8 x 8 cells, twice: over the taps the world drew and over all of them. The cells are read back two frames later through a staging ring of three, DO_NOT_WAIT (the F85c pattern). A scene depth still bound as a depth target is taken off the output merger for the dispatch and put back, and the compute stage's shader, views, UAV and constants are restored. Per eye and second: the largest number of cells (of 64) within 5, 10 and 20 cm of the camera and within 3 cm of the near plane (a wall the near plane cuts reads at the near plane, not at 0), the nearest depth, and the baseline: the coverage in frames with a head offset under 3 cm, the game's own camera, which must read about 0.

**Does that depth hold the player's weapon, hands or body? Yes.** The depth texture's stencil bit 0x10 is what the first-person draws write, and the game's characters carry it too (measured 2026-10-08 in the eye depth stencil: a walking NPC's silhouette, 8,359 px, and the commander's own body, 785,022 px; `flat_mono_shader_source.h`). The prepass shader F516BF02 also draws the skinned characters (the walkers, `docs\kinematic-motion-injection-2026-09-19.md`). F118 found the player's weapon, hand and body absent from the aim line (a surface under 0.5 m in 1 of 17807 readbacks), which says nothing about the lower part of the view. So the grid keeps the two apart: "world" is the taps without the bit, "body" (the weapon, arms and the game's characters, the commander's body among them) is all of them. The mask is not a proof that nothing else carries the bit; the baseline checks it, and a world coverage of 4 cells or more at a head offset under 3 cm makes the rule PARTIAL.

**3. The commander's collision radius: not read.** A read-only search of build 334925 found no radius in the exe. HumanoidMovementComponent (constructor 0x19DCC00) and MotionGraphPhysicsComponent (constructor 0x43E3790) bind their data from the game's packed data by numeric type id; no string, RTTI name or float constant in the humanoid code is a radius, and the only capsule strings belong to AI navigation. The physics engine is the game's own (fPhysics). The note and its scripts wait in the analysis inbox (`20261025-120103-humanoid-collision-radius`). The session line logs "not read"; `nofoot::f119::kCollisionRadiusM` takes the number when someone reads it from the data or at run time. Until then the rule estimates the clearance from the flight: the smallest head offset at which a world cell reached the near plane.

**The lines.**
- `native on foot head containment (F119)`, once per process at the first Present boundary: measure only, the collision radius (`not read`), the grid and the stencil bit. It marks a build that carries the instrument.
- `... 1 s:` each on-foot second: the frames (those with no pose, those past the 512-sample limit), the rest point (generation, age, recentres), then for each class present (two at most, and the count of the others) `[stance/item/hip|ADS n N h p50 p95 max, right a..b, forward a..b, up a..b, hist ...]` in cm, the histogram being the horizontal distance in 17 bins (upper edges 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20, 25, 30, 40, 60 and 100 cm, the last open); EDVR's eye offsets; for each eye `near, nearest (body), cells 5/10/20/near+3 (body 20 cm), read`; the skips by reason; the contact (the smallest head offset with 1 and with 8 cells within 3 cm of the near plane); the baseline; and the cost of the sampling, the dispatch, the readback and the line, in microseconds a frame. A usual line is about 1,050 characters and the log's note holds 1,200, so a crowded second drops the second class's histogram, then the first's, then the second class.
- `... the rest point moved`, at each move on foot.
- `--health` rule `head containment (F119)`:
  - the classes' p95 (from the pooled histogram, an upper bin edge) and max;
  - normal play, the seconds after the first recentre on foot and before the first second past 30 cm (else all of them), with its p95 and p99.5;
  - radii: soft = p99.5 + 3 cm, hard = soft + 5 cm, kept 2 cm under a cap (the collision radius, else the smallest head offset at which a world cell reached the near plane) and flagged when the cap leaves no room;
  - the depth read in N of M seconds, the nearest depths, the largest coverage, the baseline and the contact.
  - NEVER APPLIED when the session line and three or more on-foot seconds (F87h's lines) came with no 1 s line, or when every second sampled no head. PARTIAL when the depth grid never read or read in under half the seconds, the shader stood down, or the baseline is not about 0. IDLE when armed and not on foot. A build without the instrument has no session line and shows as not present.
  - The margins (3 cm, 5 cm, 2 cm, and 30 cm for the first lean) are judgement calls from the design; the figures that decide them are printed beside them.

**Rig.** native_frame_test (run119): the physical head (right +0.11, up 0.00, forward +0.25 from a pose and its alignment); the alignment history; the classes; 100 samples at 1 to 100 cm giving p50 50, p95 95, max 100 and the histogram's bins; the sample limit; EDVR's offsets kept apart; the grid decoded from words packed in the shader's layout (a wall at 15 cm over 16 cells, the weapon's 16 cells only in "body", a wall at 12 cm filling the view, the near plane cutting a wall, the sky, a refused sequence and size); the baseline and contact tallies; the lines within the log's limit, a crowded second included. reticle_depth_test: the production bytecode on WARP over an R32G8X24 depth-stencil texture, both eyes, with and without a stencil view, 64 cells each, equal to the CPU procedure. `edvr_log --health` self-test +14 cases, rendered from the C format strings.

**Cost.** CPU a frame: the sampling in alignTick (a few reads and one pass over the classes) and, at the boundary, about 30 D3D calls for the two dispatches, one 1.5 KB copy and the state put back; no wait and no allocation. GPU: 2 x 64 threads x 64 taps and the copy. The line's `cost N us a frame` is the measured sum.

**For the flight** (Epic; `--health` first; native on foot with a weapon and a tool; note the clock at each step):
1. Recentre once on foot, standing, looking ahead, away from walls. Note the time.
2. Normal play for a few minutes: standing and crouched, walking and turning, a weapon at the hip and in ADS, a tool drawn. No deliberate leans. Note the time.
3. Deliberate leans, as far as is comfortable: forward, sideways to each side, and down, standing next to a wall. Note the time.
4. Lean the head toward the wall until it touches (the view cuts into the wall), from a few distances and angles, then back off.
`--health` gives `head containment (F119)` OK with the classes' p95 and max, normal play's p99.5, the radii, the contact offsets and a baseline near 0; `--health --until HH:MM:SS` with the time from step 2 reads normal play alone. The baseline's "body 20 cm" shows how often the commander's own body, the weapon or the arms are inside 20 cm, which the world figures leave out.

**Build.** Full `build.bat --wait-lock` green on the third pass (the first: a Windows macro, the grid's `near` parameter renamed; the second: a class name in the rig), receipt `b019c5f973a3...`, 211.7 s. Not installed, not flown.

### 2026-10-25: F121b (the black scene with F121; an A/B key and a non-finite census)
**The flight.** Log `edvr_gfx_20261025_132827` (v0.21.1-269-g058c59b1, the right build: F121 merged with F115c, F119 and F120), Epic, the Crystal Super, the training scenario. The pilot: "all I see is a black void and my hud."

**The evidence** (EDVR's luma probe; its `game` stage is the texture the game submits):
- On foot from 13:29:37.577. The probe read 0.323 and 0.208 (lit) at 13:29:37.7 and 13:29:39.7. The first visor draw, and with it the first F121-bound shift, came at 13:29:41.693 (`visor axis (F121)` created its vertex shader and said s +0.0890 / -0.0890). The probe read 0.000, 100% black at 13:29:41.763 and on, both eyes, the game stage and the final stage.
- The visor draws stopped at about 13:31:31 and started again at 13:32:05.329 (the window counts: 3432 draws in the window that closed then, the first draw after the 30 s). The probe read 0.232 and 0.200 (lit) at 13:32:01.8 and 13:32:03.8, then 0.000 at 13:32:05.828 and to the end of the log: the second transition, again within 0.5 s of the first F121-bound draw.
- The world was still being drawn through the black (about 9187 eye draws a window; the reticle readbacks hit geometry, 3114 of 9625), so the colour is erased late in the frame.
- The clean flight at 11:33 (`edvr_gfx_20261025_113157`, v0.21.1-261: F27's pixel shader variants, the game's own visor vertex shader, the same scenario) was lit from the start of on foot (0.197 at 11:33:08) through its visor draws (the first at 11:33:10.956).
- Every F121 line was healthy: 5188-5356 draws a window, all shifted, none refused, `--health` OK. The earlier black stretches (13:28:48-13:29:35 and 13:31:39-59) are loading screens with no visor draw.

**The A/B (the pilot, after the flight).** Switching "RemLok helmet lines" to `stock`, which leaves F121 unbound, brought the scene back. F121 is the trigger.

**Checked offline, not the cause.** The interface (rig V2: the input and output signatures and every dcl line equal, ours the one b3); b0-b2 untouched (only vertex slot 3 is set, the game's VS reads b1 and b2); the restore (`visorSwapEnd` puts the game's shader and b3 back, by code review); and the visor's pixel shader under the shifted uv: the game's PS 68ABCB9F on WARP with the game's VS and with the shifted one over 300 random constant sets gave no NaN or Inf and no zero multiply, and the same mean multiply (0.845) all three ways (stock, left +0.0892, right -0.0892). Limits: the real CB2 values are not in any log, and WARP is not the NVIDIA driver.

ruled out: the shifted uv alone as the cause through a non-finite or zero value in the visor pass's own output, because its output was finite and the multiply unchanged over 300 random constant sets on WARP (open for the real constants and driver)

**What stays open.** After the pixel shader's last `sat` its outputs are `r0.xzw` (the saturated weight times the barrel-distorted scene sample, over the refracted copy) and the multiply `(1 - mask) x v0`. A non-finite value gets out only through the t1 sample at coordinates the shifted frame makes NaN or Inf (a fetch with a NaN coordinate is undefined, and a weight of 0 times a NaN is a NaN), the game's exposure texel (t0, a pixel shader input), or the vertex shader's tint `v0`. The HDR target is R11G11B10, which holds NaN and Inf, and the game's exposure and bloom would average them into every later frame. The census below measures it.

**The change (F121b).**
- `fix.native_on_foot_visor_axis` = `off` (default) | `on`, TEMPORARY, live, menu "Visor axis (test)" on the Native on foot page (ini, `hotkey_capture_test` 42 rows, the Temporary keys bullet). `off` skips only F121's bind: `remlok_lines` outer and the F27 pixel shader variants keep running. Visor draws with the key off are counted (`key off N` in the 30 s line); the F121 rule reads IDLE when all of them were left to the game by the key.
- The census (measure only; `src\d3d11\visor_census_shader.h`, `visor_census_core.h`, run from `remlok_fix.cpp`): every sixth visor draw an eye, right after the draw, a copy of the eye's HDR target (R11G11B10 2016x2017, the draw's own render target; a copy, because a target still bound for output cannot be bound for reading), one dispatch of 64 x 64 threads of 4 x 4 taps (256 x 256 taps), the compute stage put back, the output into a staging ring of three read on a later sample (DO_NOT_WAIT). Per tap, by the float bits: non-finite (NaN or Inf, with their box), and of the finite ones black (luma under 1e-4), the largest channel and the luma; and the first two texels of the visor pixel shader's t0, the game's exposure, where that view is a float 2D texture. Nothing the game reads is written; the target is never taken off the output merger.
- `visor axis (F121b) 1 s: key on|off; samples N (eye 0 a, eye 1 b) of 65536 taps; nonfinite N (NaN n, Inf i) at x .., y ..; black B; max V; mean L; exposure e0 .. e1 .. (read in R samples, non-finite in K); dropped D`, a second's line by the key's state (a sample under the other state closes the second). `visor axis (F121b): census armed` once; `native on foot visor axis (F121b): on|off (TEMPORARY ...` when the key is read or changes.
- Rule `visor census (F121b)`: OK when it measured and found none of the three; PARTIAL naming what it finds, "non-finite pixels after the visor draw" (with the key's state and the box), "exposure non-finite", or "the HDR scene is all black right after the visor draw with the key on" (and "lit with the key off (the A/B)" when both states were flown); IDLE with no sample; NEVER APPLIED when the census could not make its resources.

**Rig.** `visor_axis_test` V9 (`census_checks.h`) runs the build's `kVisorCensusBytecode` on WARP against `visorcensus::cpuModel` and the decode: a 640x360 image with one Inf, one NaN and one black tap gives 2 non-finite (1 NaN, 1 Inf) boxed from (1,0) to (638,359), the largest finite value 2.0 and the mean luma of the base colour less the three taps; an all-black image is 65536 black taps; an all-NaN image is 65536 NaN taps over the whole box; the exposure texels (1.5 and 8; a NaN one read as non-finite) and no read when the dispatch says so; the decode refuses another dispatch's sequence, width or height and counts that do not add up. V8 holds the wiring (the key in the ini, defaulting off, read once with the same default; the bind gated by it; the census copies the target and never unbinds it; run once after the draw). `edvr_log --health` self-test +11 cases (F121's key-off and mid-flight, and nine for the census). A desk run of V9 on WARP before the build, with the shader compiled from its text: 19 checks, 0 failed.

**Build.** Full `build.bat --wait-lock` green (Elite closed first), receipt `d6c716d3cbb9...`, 283.2 s (v0.21.1-269-g058c59b1, dirty until committed); `visor_axis_test` PASS V1-V9, 63 checks. Not installed, not flown.

**For the flight** (Epic, the Crystal Super; `--health` first; one session, the key flipped live from the menu, no restart; one Insert eye dump while black).
1. Enter on foot with the key `off` (the default). Expect lit. 20 s.
2. Switch "Visor axis (test)" to `on`. Expect black (the F121 flight's behaviour). Press Insert once for an eye dump while black. 20 s.
3. Switch it `off` again. Expect lit. Then `on` once more (the repeat) for 20 s, and `off` to finish.
4. Read `visor census (F121b)` and `visor axis (F121)`. The census says, with the key on: non-finite pixels with a box (the visor pass makes NaN or Inf: the corners of the shifted frame, or the refraction sample); or an exposure that reads non-finite (the poison is in the game's exposure state: a NaN reaches it and it stays); or the HDR scene black right after the visor draw with finite exposure and no non-finite pixel (the multiply of the blend went to zero: the vertex shader's tint, or the pixel shader's mask); or a lit HDR scene after the visor draw while the luma probe's game stage is black (the damage is in a later pass, bloom or the tonemap reading what the visor wrote). With the key off the same seconds give the baseline: black 0%, finite exposure.

**Still open from F121: the right eye's nasal edge line.** In all three F121 dumps the right eye keeps the line at its left edge at full strength although F27's right-eye variant is logged bound every frame; not fixed here.

### 2026-10-25: F121c (the NaN scene was two 1e-9 floors written as 0.0; an eye-trust guard; the census only with the key on)
**The flight.** Log `edvr_gfx_20261025_151004` (v0.21.1-281-ga3b81532: the arc with F121b and F122 to F127), Epic, the Crystal Super, the training scenario. The pilot: "with the test on, it shows the world off in the right eye, but with the test off it shows the world in both eyes, but the hud in only right eye". `--health`: the census with the key on, 32 s, 454 samples, 29753344 of 29753344 taps non-finite (all NaN, x 3-2012, y 3-2013 of 2016x2017), mean luma 0, the exposure finite (e0 43.13); with the key off 0 non-finite. `visor axis (F121)`: visor draws 2457 (left 2457, right 0), shifted 1954 (left only), s left +0.0890 right +0.0000; the v269 flight had 2628 and 2628.

**The cause of the NaN: a transcription error, found and reproduced on the flight machine's RTX 5090.** The game's visor vertex shader floors its HUD colour and the frame block's exposure at 1e-9 before it divides and normalises them: SHEX instructions 33 and 34 of `tools\visor_axis_test\fixtures\vs_B553BB479B7C0B97.dxbc` (file offsets 1212 and 1252) are `max r0.xyz, r0.xyz, 1e-9` and `max r0.w, cb1[90].z, 1e-9`, immediate `0x3089705f`. The disassembler prints that as `l(0.000000)`, and F121 and F121b (written from its text) floored at `0.0`. With the colour buffer's first element zero, negative or tiny, or `cb1[90].z` at 0, `rsq(0) * 0` is NaN in o2 (the vertex colour, the HUD colour), the pixel shader multiplies the HDR target by it (the dual-source blend) and every pixel is NaN. The game's own shader stays finite (a zero colour is the direction (1,1,1)/sqrt(3)). Reproduced with the real pixel shader and the real vertex shader on the NVIDIA adapter, 360 trials of degenerate colour and exposure: the game's shader 0 NaN frames; the F121 shader 270 mostly-NaN frames, with the shift of either sign and with the shift removed (`o1.x = hi * 2.0`), and none with o2 held constant. Vertex stage alone, 12 degenerate cases: the game's o2 finite in all, F121's NaN in 11; with the floors restored the same as the game's in all 12. The rig did not see it because its colours were all positive and its exposures above 0.2 (V3 to V6), and the WARP probe of F121b used the same kind of inputs. In the flight the HUD colour or the exposure was degenerate (not logged; the two flights with the key on were black in both eyes and the census says all NaN). The two other immediates were 1 and 6 ULP off (`0x3f3504b2`, `0xbf350534` against 0.707103 and 0.707111): harmless, now exact.

ruled out: the shift as the cause of the NaN, because the shipped shader with the shift removed went NaN on the same degenerate inputs on the RTX 5090, and with o2 held constant it did not
ruled out: b3 (the shift's constant buffer at slot 3) as the cause, because the interpolated uv came out the same in the game's shader and F121's at every pixel (0.5625 at the centre) with b3 bound and the draws counted shifted 1954 of 2457, with no "no replacement" refusal (a failed Map would have been one)

**The eye filing: one eye's post-scene draws were missing in that session (open).** From the first visor draw (15:11:17.005) there was one VS-B553 draw a frame (2491 in 30 s; 5355 in the v269 flight; 5036 in the second session of the same build, 15:16-15:19), all with the RTV filed as the left eye and on the RIGHT eye's target (the UI layer's mismatch line, 4919 times from 15:11:17.217: mine `...5B20`, theirs and target `...3120`, copied 0, only the left layer ever); the marker pairs existed for eye 0 only (160 a second, "both-eyes rule not met 171-176"; eye 1 none in 64 of 67 seconds), though both eyes' scene passes ran (4554 and 4551 depth-target draws in 20 s). So after 15:11:17 only the right eye's target received the HUD and the visor, the first-target rule called it eye 0, F121's left shift went onto the right eye's frame and it went NaN (the pilot's black right eye), and with the key off the left eye had no HUD at all. The break was already there with `remlok_lines` stock (the first mismatch 15:11:17.217; the census shader was created at 15:11:27.334, F121's vertex shader at 15:11:34.578).

ruled out: the F121b census as the cause of the one-eye filing, because the first mismatch came with `remlok_lines` stock, ten seconds before the census shader existed, `copied` stayed 0 in all 4919 mismatch lines including the census's seconds, and its copy texture is never bound as a render target (so it never enters the eye table); the second session of the same build had 5036 visor draws per 30 s and no mismatch line
ruled out: F122 to F127 as the cause of the one-eye filing, because the same DLLs ran the second session (15:14:51, key off) clean for 3 minutes and the v269 flights without them were clean, and no code reads the F121b key outside the outer mode's visor draws (lines 346, 651, 746 of `remlok_fix.cpp` at a3b81532)
Open: why the left eye's HUD and visor draws were absent in that session. The one difference found is that the F121b key was ON from 15:11:10 (stock mode, where nothing reads it). F121c names the state when it happens (below); a second session with the key on before going on foot tests the key.

**The change (F121c).**
1. `visor_axis_vs.h`: the two floors `1.0e-9`, and the two immediates `asfloat(0x3f3504b2)` and `asfloat(0xbf350534)`.
2. Rig V10: 25 degenerate input sets (colour of zero, negative, 1e-30, 5e-10, normal; exposure of 0, -1, 1e-30, 5e-10, 1) run through the game's shader and the shipped one on WARP: every output bit for bit the same and finite, with the shift at zero and at s (only o1.x moves); a control compiles the floors at 0.0 and must go non-finite.
3. Rig V11: the float immediates of the two token streams (read from the tokens) are the same 19 distinct values; a control zeroes the game's floors and the audit must see it.
4. The eye-trust guard (`visor_eye_trust.h`, run by `remlok_fix.cpp` and V12): the filing's eye is used for the shift only when the visor draws arrive as one draw per eye on two targets (the previous draw the other eye on another target, the eye's target not moved) and, where the UI layer knows the eyes' submitted targets (`uiLayerSubmittedTarget`, new), the draw's target belongs to the eye the filing gave it. An untrusted draw runs the game's own vertex shader and is counted as `eye filing` in the 30 s line (the first draw of a session and one after a retarget are counted without a line; a run is said once as `NOT shifted -- the eye filing is not trusted`). The F27 pixel shader variants still take the filing's eye as before (adjacent, not changed here).
5. The census runs only with the key on (the sample is begun only inside `if (onFoot && g_axisKeyOn...)`; its last second is said when the key goes off), and its two copies go through `vScreenCopyResourceRaw`, past the copy hook that calls `uiLayerNoteCopy` (V8 holds that there is no `ctx->CopyResource` in the file).
6. Self-off: a census sample taken right after a draw through the replacement vertex shader (`sl.shifted`) with any non-finite tap turns the replacement off for the session (`visor axis (F121c): SELF-OFF -- ...`, once), counted as `self-off` in the 30 s line; turning the key off and on again re-arms it. `--health` `visor axis (F121)` reads that line as NEVER APPLIED.
7. The instrument `visor eyes (F121c)` (every remlok_lines mode, on foot, any visor draw): a line when the filing's state changes after 12 draws (paired, ONE EYE ONLY, DISAGREES with the submitted eye targets; the filed and submitted target pointers and the draw's), and a 10 s summary only for a window with an anomaly or the session's first (the targets, their eye, their draws). Nothing otherwise: no per-second line. Rule `visor eyes (F121c)`: OK paired; PARTIAL names the target and whether it is the other eye's submitted one.
The key `fix.native_on_foot_visor_axis` stays TEMPORARY, default off, live.

**Rig and gates.** `visor_axis_test` V1-V13; `edvr_log --health` self-test +12 cases (the eye filing's refusals, SELF-OFF, the new rule's OK, DISAGREES, ONE EYE ONLY, recovery, short anomaly, unparsed). The probes behind the cause are scratch (the real pixel shader and a vertex-stage comparison on the NVIDIA adapter), not shipped: the rig's V10 control covers them on WARP.

**Build.** Full `build.bat --wait-lock` green (Elite not running), receipt `96b59c0e913b...`, 272.8 s (v0.21.1-281-ga3b81532, dirty until committed); `visor_axis_test` PASS V1-V13, 102 checks. Not installed, not flown.

**For the flight** (Epic, the Crystal Super; `--health` first; one session, no restart).
1. Key `off`, `remlok_lines` stock (the default): on foot, visor down, 30 s. `visor eyes (F121c)`: a `paired` line and an OK; the UI layer's mismatch lines absent. If the one-eye state returns, the line names the target and whether it is the other eye's submitted one: keep the log (the open question).
2. `remlok_lines` outer, key `on`: both eyes lit, the fog one disc per eye on the eye's axis (compare the two eyes' dumps: d near -720 px against -0.2). `visor axis (F121)` OK (shifted left and right, eye filing 0 or 1 a window); `visor census (F121b)` OK with the key on (0 non-finite). If it still goes NaN the log has `SELF-OFF` within a second and the scene comes back by itself.
3. Key `off` again; then the same with the key `on` before going on foot (the open question: the key on from the menu, stock mode, then on foot).

### 2026-10-25: F122 (the on-foot mouse cursor hidden by default)
The F120 flight (log `edvr_gfx_20261025_134757`, v0.21.1-269-g058c59b1): the pilot found the mouse better and parked it, asking for the cursor to be hidden by default behind one advanced key. `--health` `panel cursor follow (F120)` PARTIAL: the cursor's drift on the panel with the mouse still read a median of 257.6 mm and a worst of 564.9 mm in 19 of 19 judged seconds. The correction therefore did not hold the cursor still. The cause is unexplained and was not investigated; the work is parked.

**The key.** `fix.native_on_foot_panel_mouse`, `off` (the default) or `on`, an advanced setting: `# ui: hidden` in `edvr.ini`, no menu row, live.
- `off`: the cursor sprite is not seen. In the placement hook (`f111PlaceHooked`), after the game's placement, if the hit byte (`+0x100`, set by a placement on a panel) is set, the sprite's position (`+0x140`, in the pick camera's frame) is written to (1e5, 1e5, -1): behind the camera and far off its axis, so the draw culls it whichever way it reads the position (projected, normalised and set at a depth, or offset after the projection). z is written first, so a write that stops part way has already taken the sprite out of view. Nothing else is written: not the mouse NDC (`+0x84/+0x88`), not the cursor window's output, not the hit byte; the clicks go through the uv and land where the game's pointer is.
- The instruments and corrections stay idle with the key off: only the placement hook's gate opens (VR, on foot); the update, ray hit, cursor window and owner transform hooks stay closed, so F111's and F114b's cycles and lines, F117's and F120's corrections and F120's pin check do not run. The flat profile hides nothing and opens nothing.
- `on`: the game's cursor is drawn with F117 `panel` and F120 `panel`, fixed, as in the F120 flight.
- Retired as hidden rows (the F109/F112 pattern: the marker line, `retiredKeysNote`, `config_test`'s list; a value that differs from `panel` is named once): `fix.native_on_foot_panel_cursor_fix` (panel, view, game) and `fix.native_on_foot_panel_cursor_follow` (panel, head). Their two menu rows are gone; the Native on foot page has 39 rows.

ruled out: hiding the cursor by skipping its draw by shader pair, because VS 4EF6DDB075A927FA / PS 85565E9261812E2F was also classified as a loading-screen family (F104) and other UI may share it

**What is not known.** That a write to `+0x140` hides the drawn sprite is inferred from F117, whose `+0x140` writes moved the drawn cursor (the clicks and the uv were not affected); the draw's own read of the sprite was not followed. If a flight shows the cursor still drawn with `off` while `panel mouse (F122)` counts the sprites hidden, the position is not what the draw reads, and the alternative is the hit byte or the draw's call site, to be read before being written.

**Lines and rule.** `panel mouse (F122) 1 s` once a second with a panel reached (the key, the panels seen, the sprites hidden, the hides whose write failed), a change line when the key moves, and once the line saying whether the placement hook is armed. `--health` rule `panel mouse (F122)`:
- OK: `off`, every sprite of the panels reached hidden;
- PARTIAL: `off`, some hides failed;
- NEVER APPLIED: `off` and panels were seen with nothing hidden, or the placement hook was not armed;
- IDLE: the key `on` (nothing is hidden by design) or no panel reached.

**Rig.** native_frame_test +7 (run122, `f122_checks.h`):
- the key: only the word `on` is on;
- what a placement does with the key and the profile (hide, no hit, leave, flat);
- the hidden position behind the camera and not taken for seen under any of the draw's reads;
- the write against a controller's memory: three floats at the sprite's position, z first, no other byte changed, the hit byte and the mouse NDC as they were;
- a refused write counted as a failure;
- the counts;
- the hooks the key opens.

hotkey_capture_test counts the Native on foot page at 39 rows; config_test names 17 retired keys; `edvr_log --health` self-test +7 cases.
